requirements.title: Header Form Bit
requirements.statement: The first bit of a QUIC long header packet MUST be set to 1.

requirements.title: Version-Specific Bits
requirements.statement: The other seven bits in the first byte of a QUIC long header packet MUST be version-specific.

requirements.title: Version Field
requirements.statement: The four bytes after the first byte in a QUIC long header packet MUST contain a 32-bit Version field.

requirements.title: Destination Connection ID Length Encoding
requirements.statement: The byte after the Version field MUST encode the Destination Connection ID length as an 8-bit unsigned integer.

requirements.title: Destination Connection ID Size
requirements.statement: The Destination Connection ID field MUST follow its length byte and be between 0 and 255 bytes long.

requirements.title: Source Connection ID Length Encoding
requirements.statement: The byte after the Destination Connection ID field MUST encode the Source Connection ID length as an 8-bit unsigned integer.

requirements.title: Source Connection ID Size
requirements.statement: The Source Connection ID field MUST follow its length byte and be between 0 and 255 bytes long.

requirements.title: Version-Specific Remainder
requirements.statement: The remainder of a QUIC long header packet MUST contain version-specific content.

requirements.title: Provide ordered byte-stream abstraction
requirements.statement: QUIC streams MUST provide an ordered byte-stream abstraction to an application.

requirements.title: Allow stream creation by sending data
requirements.statement: QUIC MUST allow streams to be created by sending data.

requirements.title: Single STREAM frame can open carry and close a stream
requirements.statement: A single STREAM frame MUST be able to open, carry data for, and close a stream.

requirements.title: Allow concurrent interleaved stream data
requirements.statement: QUIC MUST allow streams to send data concurrently interleaved with other streams.

requirements.title: Allow either endpoint to create streams
requirements.statement: QUIC MUST allow either endpoint to create streams.

requirements.title: Allow streams to be canceled
requirements.statement: QUIC MUST allow streams to be canceled.

requirements.title: Do not guarantee cross-stream byte ordering
requirements.statement: QUIC MUST NOT provide any means of ensuring ordering between bytes on different streams.

requirements.title: Allow arbitrary data per stream
requirements.statement: QUIC MUST allow an arbitrary amount of data to be sent on any stream, subject to flow control constraints and stream limits.

requirements.title: Allow concurrent streams
requirements.statement: QUIC MUST allow an arbitrary number of streams to operate concurrently, subject to flow control constraints and stream limits.

requirements.title: Limited on-path attacker cannot close idle connection after client resumes
requirements.statement: A limited on-path attacker MUST NOT cause an idle connection to close if the client is first to resume activity.

requirements.title: Keep stream IDs unique
requirements.statement: A stream ID MUST be unique for all streams on a connection.

requirements.title: Limit stream ID width
requirements.statement: A stream ID MUST be a 62-bit integer in the range 0 to 2^62-1.

requirements.title: Encode stream IDs as variable-length integers
requirements.statement: Stream IDs MUST be encoded as variable-length integers.

requirements.title: Do not reuse stream IDs
requirements.statement: A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a stream ID within a connection.

requirements.title: Successive streams use increasing IDs
requirements.statement: Successive streams of each type MUST be created with numerically increasing stream IDs.

requirements.title: Use Stream ID and Offset to order stream data
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST use the Stream ID and Offset fields in STREAM frames to place data in order.

requirements.title: Deliver stream data as an ordered byte stream
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST be able to deliver stream data to an application as an ordered byte stream.

requirements.title: Allow PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on conflicting duplicate data
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY treat receipt of different data at the same offset within a stream as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Provide stream priority indication
requirements.statement: A QUIC implementation SHOULD provide ways in which an application can indicate the relative priority of streams.

requirements.title: Generate STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED when flow control blocks sending
requirements.statement: An endpoint in the Send state MUST generate STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames if it is blocked from sending by stream flow control limits.

requirements.title: Enter Data Sent after FIN is sent
requirements.statement: After the application indicates that all stream data has been sent and a STREAM frame containing the FIN bit is sent, the sending part of the stream MUST enter the Data Sent state.

requirements.title: Create receiving part on bidirectional control frames
requirements.statement: For bidirectional streams initiated by a peer, receipt of a MAX_STREAM_DATA or STOP_SENDING frame for the sending part of the stream MUST also create the receiving part.

requirements.title: Create receiving part on first peer frame
requirements.statement: The receiving part of a stream initiated by a peer MUST be created when the first STREAM, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, or RESET_STREAM frame is received for that stream.

requirements.title: Receive STREAM and STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED in Recv state
requirements.statement: In the Recv state, the endpoint MUST receive STREAM and STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames.

requirements.title: Enter Data Recvd once all data is received
requirements.statement: Once all data for the stream has been received, the receiving part MUST enter the Data Recvd state.

requirements.title: Keep Data Recvd until delivery to the application
requirements.statement: The Data Recvd state MUST persist until stream data has been delivered to the application.

requirements.title: Allow interruption, discard, and reset signaling on RESET_STREAM
requirements.statement: An implementation MAY interrupt delivery of stream data, discard any data that was not consumed, and signal the receipt of the RESET_STREAM.

requirements.title: Limit peer-initiated stream concurrency
requirements.statement: A QUIC endpoint MUST control the maximum cumulative number of streams that its peer can initiate.

requirements.title: Exclude CRYPTO frames from stream flow control
requirements.statement: Data sent in CRYPTO frames MUST NOT be flow controlled in the same way as stream data.

requirements.title: Provide buffering limit interfaces
requirements.statement: QUIC implementations SHOULD provide an interface for the cryptographic protocol implementation to communicate its buffering limits.

requirements.title: Limit connection flow control
requirements.statement: Connection flow control MUST prevent senders from exceeding a receiver's buffer capacity for the connection by limiting the total bytes of stream data sent in STREAM frames on all streams.

requirements.title: Disallow excess data
requirements.statement: Senders MUST NOT send data in excess of either limit.

requirements.title: Set initial limits via transport parameters
requirements.statement: A receiver MUST set initial limits for all streams through transport parameters during the handshake.

requirements.title: Advertise larger stream limits with MAX_STREAM_DATA
requirements.statement: A receiver MAY advertise a larger limit for a stream by sending a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame with the corresponding stream ID.

requirements.title: Define MAX_STREAM_DATA offset
requirements.statement: A MAX_STREAM_DATA frame MUST indicate the maximum absolute byte offset of a stream.

requirements.title: Track cumulative received bytes
requirements.statement: A receiver MUST maintain a cumulative sum of bytes received on all streams to check for violations of the advertised connection or stream data limits.

requirements.title: Close on flow-control violations
requirements.statement: A receiver MUST close the connection with an error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR if the sender violates the advertised connection or stream data limits.

requirements.title: Signal flow-control blocking
requirements.statement: A sender SHOULD send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame to indicate to the receiver that it has data to write but is blocked by flow control limits.

requirements.title: Periodically signal blocked flow control
requirements.statement: A sender that is flow control limited SHOULD periodically send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame when it has no ack-eliciting packets in flight.

requirements.title: Do not wait for blocked-flow-control frames before sending credit updates
requirements.statement: A receiver MUST NOT wait for a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame before sending a MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frame.

requirements.title: Leave opposite data flow unaffected
requirements.statement: For a bidirectional stream, RESET_STREAM MUST have no effect on data flow in the opposite direction.

requirements.title: Maintain flow control state after RESET_STREAM
requirements.statement: Both endpoints MUST maintain flow control state for the stream in the unterminated direction until that direction enters a terminal state.

requirements.title: Keep final stream size immutable
requirements.statement: Once a final size for a stream is known, it MUST NOT change.

requirements.title: Allow zero-length connection IDs when routing is unnecessary
requirements.statement: A zero-length connection ID MAY be used when a connection ID is not needed to route to the correct endpoint.

requirements.title: Send the initial connection ID in the long header Source Connection ID field
requirements.statement: The initial connection ID issued by an endpoint MUST be sent in the Source Connection ID field of the long packet header during the handshake.

requirements.title: Initial connection ID sequence number
requirements.statement: The sequence number of the initial connection ID MUST be 0.

requirements.title: Preferred-address connection ID sequence number
requirements.statement: If the preferred_address transport parameter is sent, the sequence number of the supplied connection ID MUST be 1.

requirements.title: Issued connection ID sequence numbers increase by 1
requirements.statement: The sequence number on each newly issued connection ID MUST increase by 1.

requirements.title: Change the peer connection ID at any time during the connection
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY change the connection ID it uses for a peer to another available one at any time during the connection.

requirements.title: Limit each connection ID to one local and one destination address
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST limit the use of a connection ID to packets sent from a single local address to a single destination address.

requirements.title: Retire connection IDs when they are no longer actively used
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD retire connection IDs when they are no longer actively using either the local or destination address for which the connection ID was used.

requirements.title: Allow connection close when indicated connection IDs cannot be processed
requirements.statement: If the endpoint can no longer process the indicated connection IDs, it MAY close the connection.

requirements.title: Match zero-length DCI packets by address
requirements.statement: If the Destination Connection ID is zero length and the addressing information in the packet matches the addressing information the endpoint uses to identify a connection with a zero-length connection ID, QUIC MUST process the packet as part of that connection.

requirements.title: Identify zero-length DCID connections by local address and port
requirements.statement: Clients that choose to receive zero-length connection IDs MAY use the local address and port to identify a connection.

requirements.title: Proceed with the handshake for valid Initial packets
requirements.statement: If the packet is an Initial packet fully conforming with the specification, the server MUST proceed with the handshake.

requirements.title: Indicate that migration is unsupported
requirements.statement: A server in a deployment that does not implement a solution to maintain connection continuity when the client address changes SHOULD indicate that migration is not supported by using the disable_active_migration transport parameter.

requirements.title: disable_active_migration does not block migration after preferred_address
requirements.statement: The disable_active_migration transport parameter MUST NOT prohibit connection migration after a client has acted on a preferred_address transport parameter.

requirements.title: Send Version Negotiation packets for new-connection attempts
requirements.statement: A server MUST send a Version Negotiation packet in response to each packet that might initiate a new connection.

requirements.title: Size the first datagram for multi-version support
requirements.statement: Clients that support multiple QUIC versions SHOULD ensure that the first UDP datagram they send is sized to the largest of the minimum datagram sizes from all versions they support, using PADDING frames as necessary.

requirements.title: Omit Version Negotiation on undersized datagrams
requirements.statement: A server MAY omit sending a Version Negotiation packet if the datagram it receives is smaller than the minimum size specified in a different version.

requirements.title: Include accepted versions in Version Negotiation packets
requirements.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST include a list of versions that the server will accept.

requirements.title: Respond with Version Negotiation for unacceptable versions
requirements.statement: If the version selected by the client is not acceptable to the server, the server MUST respond with a Version Negotiation packet.

requirements.title: Do not send Version Negotiation in response to Version Negotiation
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send a Version Negotiation packet in response to receiving a Version Negotiation packet.

requirements.title: Start CRYPTO offsets at zero in each packet number space
requirements.statement: The offsets used by CRYPTO frames to ensure ordered delivery of cryptographic handshake data MUST start from zero in each packet number space.

requirements.title: Explicitly negotiate an application protocol
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST explicitly negotiate an application protocol.

requirements.title: Adopt the server Source Connection ID for subsequent packets
requirements.statement: Upon first receiving an Initial or Retry packet from the server, the client MUST use the Source Connection ID supplied by the server as the Destination Connection ID for subsequent packets, including any 0-RTT packets.

requirements.title: Discard packets with different source connection IDs after a valid Initial
requirements.statement: Once a client has received a valid Initial packet from the server, it MUST discard any subsequent packet it receives on that connection with a different Source Connection ID.

requirements.title: Include zero-length connection ID transport parameter with zero-length value
requirements.statement: If a zero-length connection ID is selected, the corresponding transport parameter MUST be included with a zero-length value.

requirements.title: Set application-data-capable parameters non-zero for 0-RTT
requirements.statement: The applicable subset of transport parameters that permit the sending of application data SHOULD be set to non-zero values for 0-RTT.

requirements.title: Server may retain remembered parameters and reject smaller 0-RTT values
requirements.statement: A server MAY store and recover the previously sent values of the max_idle_timeout, max_udp_payload_size, and disable_active_migration parameters and reject 0-RTT if it selects smaller values.

requirements.title: Reject unsupported 0-RTT transport parameters
requirements.statement: A server MUST reject 0-RTT data if the restored values for transport parameters cannot be supported.

requirements.title: Use only remembered transport parameters in 0-RTT
requirements.statement: When sending frames in 0-RTT packets, a client MUST only use remembered transport parameters.

requirements.title: Allow protocol error for updated transport parameters in 0-RTT
requirements.statement: A server MAY treat the use of updated transport parameters in 0-RTT as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Apply anti-amplification limits after client IP changes
requirements.statement: If the client IP address has changed, the server MUST adhere to the anti-amplification limit.

requirements.title: Send at most one PATH_RESPONSE per PATH_CHALLENGE
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send more than one PATH_RESPONSE frame in response to one PATH_CHALLENGE frame.

requirements.title: Do not migrate before handshake confirmation
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST not initiate connection migration before the handshake is confirmed, as defined in Section 4.1.2 of [QUIC-TLS].

requirements.title: Validate changed peer addresses
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST perform path validation (Section 8.2) if it detects any change to a peer's address, unless it has previously validated that address.

requirements.title: Wait for a non-probing packet before sending to a client address
requirements.statement: Servers MUST not send non-probing packets toward a client address until they see a non-probing packet from that address.

requirements.title: Discard packets from unknown server addresses
requirements.statement: If a client receives packets from an unknown server address, the client MUST discard these packets.

requirements.title: Initiate path validation to establish reachability
requirements.statement: To establish reachability on the new path, an endpoint MUST initiate path validation on the new path.

requirements.title: Allow deferred path validation after the next non-probing frame
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY defer path validation until after a peer sends the next non-probing frame to its new address.

requirements.title: Send address validation tokens after verifying a new client address
requirements.statement: After verifying a new client address, the server SHOULD send new address validation tokens to the client.

requirements.title: Close silently without last validated peer address
requirements.statement: If an endpoint has no state about the last validated peer address, it MUST close the connection silently by discarding all connection state.

requirements.title: Move back to the original path on packet number increase
requirements.statement: A non-probing packet received on the original path that increases the maximum received packet number MUST cause the endpoint to move back to that path.

requirements.title: Send ACK frames for all received packets on multiple paths
requirements.statement: A receiver of packets on multiple paths MUST send ACK frames covering all received packets.

requirements.title: Avoid initiating migration with peers that request zero-length connection IDs
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD NOT initiate migration with a peer that has requested a zero-length connection ID.

requirements.title: Change addresses infrequently
requirements.statement: Addresses SHOULD only be changed infrequently.

requirements.title: Provide new connection IDs before migration
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD provide new connection IDs before peers migrate.

requirements.title: Select an address and start path validation after handshake confirmation
requirements.statement: Once the handshake is confirmed, the client SHOULD select one of the two addresses provided by the server and initiate path validation.

requirements.title: Validate chosen preferred address before migrating
requirements.statement: A client that migrates to a preferred address MUST validate the address it chooses before migrating.

requirements.title: Send non-probing packets from the original address until validation completes
requirements.statement: The server MUST send non-probing packets from its original address until it receives a non-probing packet from the client at its preferred address and until the server has validated the new path.

requirements.title: Protect against source-address mismatch attacks at the preferred address
requirements.statement: If packets received at the server's preferred address have a different source address than observed from the client during the handshake, the server MUST protect against potential attacks as described in Sections 9.3.1 and 9.3.2.

requirements.title: Initiate path validation on probe packets from a different address
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD initiate path validation to the client's new address upon receiving a probe packet from a different address.

requirements.title: Client may use the preferred-address connection ID on any path
requirements.statement: The client MAY use the connection ID provided in the preferred_address transport parameter on any path.

requirements.title: Discard state without a validated path
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY discard connection state if it does not have a validated path on which it can send packets.

requirements.title: Raise idle timeout to at least 3x PTO
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST increase the idle timeout period to be at least three times the current Probe Timeout (PTO).

requirements.title: Send CONNECTION_CLOSE to terminate immediately
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame to terminate the connection immediately.

requirements.title: Enter closing state after immediate close
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST enter the closing state after initiating an immediate close.

requirements.title: Bind stateless reset tokens to a connection ID
requirements.statement: A stateless reset token MUST be specific to a connection ID.

requirements.title: Invalidate tokens on connection ID retirement
requirements.statement: Tokens MUST be invalidated when their associated connection ID is retired via a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.

requirements.title: Limit Stateless Reset amplification
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send a Stateless Reset that is three times or more larger than the packet it receives.

requirements.title: Enter the draining period when a stateless reset token matches
requirements.statement: If the last 16 bytes of the datagram are identical in value to a stateless reset token, the endpoint MUST enter the draining period.

requirements.title: Generate a valid stateless reset token after state loss
requirements.statement: An endpoint that loses state MAY use the same method to generate a valid stateless reset token.

requirements.title: Allow applicable error codes
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY use any applicable error code when it detects an error condition.

requirements.title: Allow generic error codes in place of specific codes
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY use a generic error code such as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION or INTERNAL_ERROR in place of a specific error code.

requirements.title: Prepare to retransmit CONNECTION_CLOSE packets after additional traffic on a terminated connection
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD be prepared to retransmit a packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame if it receives more packets on a terminated connection.

requirements.title: Process coalesced packets
requirements.statement: Receivers MUST be able to process coalesced packets.

requirements.title: Do not reuse packet numbers within a space
requirements.statement: A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a packet number within the same packet number space in one connection.

requirements.title: Close the connection when packet-number exhaustion is reached
requirements.statement: If the packet number for sending reaches 2^62-1, the sender MUST close the connection without sending a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame or any further packets.

requirements.title: Discard newly unprotected packets when duplicate status is uncertain
requirements.statement: A receiver MUST discard a newly unprotected packet unless it is certain that it has not processed another packet with the same packet number from the same packet number space.

requirements.title: Forbid frames in Version Negotiation, Stateless Reset, and Retry packets
requirements.statement: Version Negotiation, Stateless Reset, and Retry packets MUST not contain frames.

requirements.title: Allow multiple frames and frame types in frame-bearing packet payloads
requirements.statement: The payload of a packet that contains frames MAY contain multiple frames and multiple frame types.

requirements.title: Require at least one frame in frame-bearing packet payloads
requirements.statement: The payload of a packet that contains frames MUST contain at least one frame.

requirements.title: Treat empty frame packets as protocol violations
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a packet containing no frames as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Frame type precedes type-dependent fields
requirements.statement: Each frame MUST begin with a Frame Type, followed by additional type-dependent fields.

requirements.title: Other frames use Frame Type as identifier
requirements.statement: For all other frames, the Frame Type field MUST simply identify the frame.

requirements.title: Allow all frames in 1-RTT packets
requirements.statement: All frames MAY appear in 1-RTT packets.

requirements.title: Treat frames in forbidden packet types as protocol violation
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a frame in a packet type that is not permitted as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Use the shortest possible frame type encoding
requirements.statement: A frame type MUST use the shortest possible encoding.

requirements.title: PADDING, PING, and CRYPTO frames allowed in any packet number space
requirements.statement: PADDING, PING, and CRYPTO frames MAY appear in any packet number space.

requirements.title: All other frame types limited to application data packet number space
requirements.statement: All other frame types MUST only be sent in the application data packet number space.

requirements.title: Delay acknowledgment until processing completes
requirements.statement: A packet MUST NOT be acknowledged until packet protection has been successfully removed and all frames contained in the packet have been processed.

requirements.title: Acknowledge all received packets
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST acknowledge all packets they receive and process.

requirements.title: Retransmit CRYPTO data until acknowledged
requirements.statement: Data sent in CRYPTO frames MUST be retransmitted according to the rules in [QUIC-RECOVERY] until all data has been acknowledged.

requirements.title: Keep RESET_STREAM content unchanged on retransmission
requirements.statement: The content of a RESET_STREAM frame MUST NOT change when it is sent again.

requirements.title: Do not resend CONNECTION_CLOSE on loss
requirements.statement: Connection close signals, including packets that contain CONNECTION_CLOSE frames, MUST NOT be sent again when packet loss is detected.

requirements.title: Retransmit MAX_DATA when lost or updated
requirements.statement: An updated value MUST be sent in a MAX_DATA frame if the packet containing the most recently sent MAX_DATA frame is declared lost or when the endpoint decides to update the limit.

requirements.title: Send stream-type limits in MAX_STREAMS frames
requirements.statement: The limit on streams of a given type MUST be sent in MAX_STREAMS frames.

requirements.title: Send PATH_CHALLENGE checks periodically until satisfied
requirements.statement: A liveness or path validation check using PATH_CHALLENGE frames MUST be sent periodically until a matching PATH_RESPONSE frame is received or until there is no remaining need for liveness or path validation checking.

requirements.title: Use a different payload in each PATH_CHALLENGE
requirements.statement: PATH_CHALLENGE frames MUST include a different payload each time they are sent.

requirements.title: Send PATH_RESPONSE only once
requirements.statement: Responses to path validation using PATH_RESPONSE frames MUST be sent just once.

requirements.title: Avoid retransmitting acknowledged information
requirements.statement: A sender SHOULD avoid retransmitting information from packets once they are acknowledged.

requirements.title: Take congestion control action upon loss
requirements.statement: Upon detecting losses, a sender MUST take appropriate congestion control action.

requirements.title: Set ECT(0) on early packets for validation
requirements.statement: The endpoint MUST set an ECT(0) codepoint in the IP header of early outgoing packets sent on a new path to the peer.

requirements.title: UDP datagrams may carry multiple QUIC packets
requirements.statement: A UDP datagram MAY include one or more QUIC packets.

requirements.title: Require path support for 1200-byte datagrams
requirements.statement: QUIC MUST NOT be used if the network path cannot support a maximum datagram size of at least 1200 bytes.

requirements.title: Do not fragment UDP datagrams at the IP layer
requirements.statement: UDP datagrams MUST not be fragmented at the IP layer.

requirements.title: Identify QUIC versions with 32-bit numbers
requirements.statement: QUIC versions MUST be identified using a 32-bit unsigned number.

requirements.title: Reserve version 0x00000000 for version negotiation
requirements.statement: The version 0x00000000 MUST be reserved to represent version negotiation.

requirements.title: Use TLS for QUIC version 1 handshake
requirements.statement: Version 0x00000001 of QUIC MUST use TLS as a cryptographic handshake protocol.

requirements.title: Reserve versions with cleared high 16 bits
requirements.statement: Versions with the most significant 16 bits of the version number cleared MUST be reserved for use in future IETF consensus documents.

requirements.title: Reserve 0x?a?a?a?a versions for negotiation exercise
requirements.statement: Versions that follow the pattern 0x?a?a?a?a MUST be reserved for use in forcing version negotiation to be exercised.

requirements.title: Allow advertising support for reserved versions
requirements.statement: A client or server MAY advertise support for any of these reserved versions.

requirements.title: Allow servers to advertise reserved versions
requirements.statement: A server MAY advertise support for one of these versions and can expect that clients ignore the value.

requirements.title: Reserve leading bits in variable-length integer encoding
requirements.statement: The QUIC variable-length integer encoding MUST reserve the two most significant bits of the first byte to encode the base-2 logarithm of the integer encoding length in bytes.

requirements.title: Encode integer values in remaining bits
requirements.statement: The integer value MUST be encoded on the remaining bits, in network byte order.

requirements.title: Encode variable-length integers in 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes
requirements.statement: Variable-length integers MUST be encoded on 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes.

requirements.title: Limit variable-length integer bit capacity
requirements.statement: Variable-length integers MUST encode 6-, 14-, 30-, or 62-bit values, respectively.

requirements.title: Allow non-minimum-length integer encodings
requirements.statement: Values MAY be encoded on more than the minimum number of bytes necessary, except the Frame Type field.

requirements.title: Connection ID lengths in long headers do not use variable-length integer encoding
requirements.statement: The length of connection IDs in long header packets MUST NOT use variable-length integer encoding.

requirements.title: Packet numbers in headers do not use variable-length integer encoding
requirements.statement: Packet numbers sent in the header MUST NOT use variable-length integer encoding.

requirements.title: Versions do not use variable-length integer encoding
requirements.statement: Versions MUST NOT use variable-length integer encoding.

requirements.title: Encode Destination Connection ID length after version
requirements.statement: The byte following the version MUST contain the length in bytes of the Destination Connection ID field that follows it.

requirements.title: Encode Source Connection ID length after Destination Connection ID
requirements.statement: The byte following the Destination Connection ID MUST contain the length in bytes of the Source Connection ID field that follows it.

requirements.title: Ignore the Unused field value
requirements.statement: Clients MUST ignore the value of this field.

requirements.title: Echo the received Source Connection ID
requirements.statement: The server MUST include the value from the Source Connection ID field of the packet it receives in the Destination Connection ID field.

requirements.title: Version Negotiation packet is not acknowledged
requirements.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST NOT be acknowledged.

requirements.title: Do not send multiple Version Negotiation packets for one datagram
requirements.statement: A server MUST NOT send more than one Version Negotiation packet in response to a single UDP datagram.

requirements.title: Client handling of non-zero token length
requirements.statement: A client that receives an Initial packet with a non-zero Token Length field MUST either discard the packet or generate a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Server token length in Initial packets
requirements.statement: Initial packets sent by the server MUST set the Token Length field to 0.

requirements.title: Resend 0-RTT data after a new Initial packet
requirements.statement: A client SHOULD attempt to resend data in 0-RTT packets after it sends a new Initial packet.

requirements.title: Stop sending 0-RTT after processing 1-RTT
requirements.statement: A client MUST NOT send 0-RTT packets once it starts processing 1-RTT packets from the server.

requirements.title: Carry 1-RTT acknowledgments in 1-RTT packets
requirements.statement: An acknowledgment for a 1-RTT packet MUST be carried in a 1-RTT packet.

requirements.title: Use Handshake packets after receiving one from the server
requirements.statement: Once a client has received a Handshake packet from a server, it MUST use Handshake packets to send subsequent cryptographic handshake messages and acknowledgments to the server.

requirements.title: Treat Handshake packets with other frames as a protocol violation
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST treat receipt of Handshake packets with other frames as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Allow Retry on Initial and 0-RTT
requirements.statement: A server MAY send Retry packets in response to Initial and 0-RTT packets.

requirements.title: Allow multiple Retry packets while receiving Initial or 0-RTT
requirements.statement: A server MAY send multiple Retry packets as it receives Initial or 0-RTT packets.

requirements.title: Use short packet header for 1-RTT packets
requirements.statement: A 1-RTT packet MUST use a short packet header.

requirements.title: Mark reserved bits in byte 0
requirements.statement: The next two bits (those with a mask of 0x18) of byte 0 MUST be reserved.

requirements.title: Reject non-zero reserved bits after protection removal
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a packet that has a non-zero value for these bits, after removing both packet and header protection, as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Encode packet number length in byte 0
requirements.statement: The least significant two bits (those with a mask of 0x03) of byte 0 MUST contain the length of the Packet Number field, encoded as an unsigned two-bit integer that is one less than the length of the Packet Number field in bytes.

requirements.title: Carry transport parameters in extension data
requirements.statement: The extension_data field of the quic_transport_parameters extension defined in [QUIC-TLS] MUST contain the QUIC transport parameters.

requirements.title: Transport parameter length field contains value length
requirements.statement: The Transport Parameter Length field MUST contain the length of the Transport Parameter Value field in bytes.

requirements.title: Preferred address can cover one family
requirements.statement: Servers MAY choose to only send a preferred address of one address family by sending an all-zero address and port (0.0.0.0:0 or [::]:0) for the other family.

requirements.title: IP addresses use network byte order
requirements.statement: IP addresses MUST be encoded in network byte order.

requirements.title: Preferred address includes IPv4 and IPv6 pairs
requirements.statement: The preferred_address transport parameter MUST contain an address and port for both IPv4 and IPv6.

requirements.title: Stateless Reset Token carries connection ID token
requirements.statement: Finally, a 16-byte Stateless Reset Token field MUST include the stateless reset token associated with the connection ID.

requirements.title: Zero-length connection IDs forbid preferred addresses
requirements.statement: A server that chooses a zero-length connection ID MUST NOT provide a preferred address.

requirements.title: Preferred address violations are transport parameter errors
requirements.statement: A client MUST treat a violation of these requirements as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.

requirements.title: Active connection ID limit minimum
requirements.statement: The value of the active_connection_id_limit parameter MUST be at least 2.

requirements.title: Reject active connection ID limits below 2
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives a value less than 2 MUST close the connection with an error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.

requirements.title: Forbid server-only transport parameters on clients
requirements.statement: A client MUST NOT include any server-only transport parameter: original_destination_connection_id, preferred_address, retry_source_connection_id, or stateless_reset_token.

requirements.title: ACKs indicate packet number and space
requirements.statement: An acknowledgment for a packet MUST indicate both a packet number and a packet number space.

requirements.title: VN and Retry packets are not acknowledged
requirements.statement: Version Negotiation and Retry packets MUST NOT be acknowledged because they do not contain a packet number.

requirements.title: Order ACK range components in descending packet number order
requirements.statement: Each ACK Range MUST consist of alternating Gap and ACK Range Length values in descending packet number order.

requirements.title: Interpret zero ACK range length as largest packet only
requirements.statement: A value of 0 MUST indicate that only the largest packet number is acknowledged.

requirements.title: Use gaps to represent unacknowledged packet ranges
requirements.statement: Each Gap MUST indicate a range of packets that are not being acknowledged.

requirements.title: Use RESET_STREAM to terminate sending
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST use a RESET_STREAM frame (type=0x04) to abruptly terminate the sending part of a stream.

requirements.title: Include a length field in long-header packets
requirements.statement: Initial, 0-RTT, and Handshake packets MUST contain a Length field that determines the end of the packet.

requirements.title: Require short-header packets to be last in a datagram
requirements.statement: A packet with a short header MUST be the last packet included in a UDP datagram.

requirements.title: Use CRYPTO frames for handshake messages
requirements.statement: A CRYPTO frame (type=0x06) MUST be used to transmit cryptographic handshake messages.

requirements.title: Oversized CRYPTO frames are connection errors
requirements.statement: Receipt of a frame that exceeds this limit MUST be treated as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR or CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED.

requirements.title: Require non-empty NEW_TOKEN tokens
requirements.statement: The token MUST NOT be empty.

requirements.title: Reject empty NEW_TOKEN frames as frame encoding errors
requirements.statement: A client MUST treat receipt of a NEW_TOKEN frame with an empty Token field as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.

requirements.title: Prohibit clients from sending NEW_TOKEN frames
requirements.statement: Clients MUST NOT send NEW_TOKEN frames.

requirements.title: Treat NEW_TOKEN frames as protocol violations for servers
requirements.statement: A server MUST treat receipt of a NEW_TOKEN frame as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Terminate on STREAM_STATE_ERROR for invalid locally initiated stream
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST terminate the connection with error STREAM_STATE_ERROR if it receives a STREAM frame for a locally initiated stream that has not yet been created, or for a send-only stream.

requirements.title: Terminate on FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR when exceeding MAX_DATA
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST terminate a connection with an error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR if it receives more data than the maximum data value that it has sent.

requirements.title: Do not exceed the advertised stream data limit
requirements.statement: The data sent on a stream MUST NOT exceed the largest maximum stream data value advertised by the receiver.

requirements.title: Flow control error on excess stream data
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST terminate a connection with an error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR if it receives more data than the largest maximum stream data that it has sent for the affected stream.

requirements.title: Limit stream openings to peer allowance
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT open more streams than permitted by the current stream limit set by its peer.

requirements.title: Terminate on stream limit violation
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST terminate a connection with an error of type STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR if a peer opens more streams than was permitted.

requirements.title: Count closed streams toward the limit
requirements.statement: The limit MUST include streams that have been closed as well as those that are open.

requirements.title: Immediately acknowledge ECN CE packets
requirements.statement: Packets marked with the ECN Congestion Experienced (CE) codepoint in the IP header SHOULD be acknowledged immediately.

requirements.title: Acknowledge most recent packets
requirements.statement: ACK frames SHOULD always acknowledge the most recently received packets.

requirements.title: Limit remembered ACK ranges
requirements.statement: A receiver MUST limit the number of ACK Ranges it remembers and sends in ACK frames.

requirements.title: Stop tracking acknowledged ACK ranges
requirements.statement: After receiving acknowledgments for an ACK frame, the receiver SHOULD stop tracking those acknowledged ACK Ranges.

requirements.title: Discard unacknowledged ACK ranges to reduce size
requirements.statement: A receiver MAY discard unacknowledged ACK Ranges to limit ACK frame size.

requirements.title: Further limit ACK frame size
requirements.statement: Receivers MAY also limit ACK frame size further to preserve space for other frames or to limit the capacity that acknowledgments consume.

requirements.title: Reject RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID sequence numbers that refer to the packet's destination CID
requirements.statement: The sequence number specified in a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame MUST NOT refer to the Destination Connection ID field of the packet in which the frame is contained.

requirements.title: Treat RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION with zero-length CID
requirements.statement: An endpoint that provides a zero-length connection ID MUST treat receipt of a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Retransmit HANDSHAKE_DONE until acknowledged
requirements.statement: The HANDSHAKE_DONE frame MUST be retransmitted until it is acknowledged.

requirements.title: Accept packets containing outdated frames
requirements.statement: A receiver MUST accept packets containing an outdated frame, such as a MAX_DATA frame carrying a smaller maximum data value than one found in an older packet.

requirements.title: Use transport error code space for 0x1c
requirements.statement: A CONNECTION_CLOSE frame of type 0x1c MUST use codes from the space defined in Section 20.1.

requirements.title: Omit the field from application-specific CONNECTION_CLOSE
requirements.statement: The application-specific variant of CONNECTION_CLOSE (type 0x1d) MUST not include this field.

requirements.title: Permit handshake-time APPLICATION_ERROR closes
requirements.statement: When an application wishes to abandon a connection during the handshake, an endpoint MAY send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame (type 0x1c) with an error code of APPLICATION_ERROR in an Initial or Handshake packet.

requirements.title: Do not send HANDSHAKE_DONE before handshake completes
requirements.statement: Servers MUST not send a HANDSHAKE_DONE frame before completing the handshake.

requirements.title: Treat HANDSHAKE_DONE receipt as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION
requirements.statement: A server MUST treat receipt of a HANDSHAKE_DONE frame as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Non-self-describing frame encoding
requirements.statement: QUIC frames MUST NOT use a self-describing encoding.

requirements.title: Ensure peers understand new extension frames first
requirements.statement: An extension to QUIC that wishes to use a new type of frame MUST first ensure that a peer is able to understand the frame.

requirements.title: Signal extension-frame willingness with transport parameters
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY use a transport parameter to signal its willingness to receive extension frame types.

requirements.title: One transport parameter can cover multiple extension frame types
requirements.statement: One transport parameter MAY indicate support for one or more extension frame types.

requirements.title: Extension frames excluded from flow control by default
requirements.statement: Extension frames MUST NOT be included in flow control unless specified in the extension.

requirements.title: Allow omission of provisional-registration fields
requirements.statement: Provisional registrations MAY omit the Specification and Notes fields, plus any additional fields that might be required for a permanent registration.

requirements.title: Reserve codepoint 0x00000000
requirements.statement: The codepoint of 0x00000000 MUST be permanently reserved.

requirements.title: Allow CONNECTION_CLOSE frames in Handshake packets
requirements.statement: Handshake packets MAY contain CONNECTION_CLOSE frames of type 0x1c.

requirements.title: Padding frame carries no semantic value
requirements.statement: A PADDING frame (type=0x00) MUST have no semantic value.

requirements.title: Do not send NEW_CONNECTION_ID when peer uses zero-length DCID
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST not send this frame if it currently requires that its peer send packets with a zero-length Destination Connection ID.

requirements.title: Treat NEW_CONNECTION_ID on zero-length DCID as a protocol violation
requirements.statement: An endpoint that is sending packets with a zero-length Destination Connection ID MUST treat receipt of a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Allow protocol-violation handling for inconsistent NEW_CONNECTION_ID state
requirements.statement: If an endpoint receives a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame that repeats a previously issued connection ID with a different Stateless Reset Token field value or a different Sequence Number field value, or if a sequence number is used for different connection IDs, the endpoint MAY treat that receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Limit Retire Prior To to the Sequence Number
requirements.statement: The value in the Retire Prior To field MUST be less than or equal to the value in the Sequence Number field.

requirements.title: Treat oversized Retire Prior To as FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR
requirements.statement: Receiving a value in the Retire Prior To field that is greater than that in the Sequence Number field MUST be treated as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.

requirements.title: Ignore non-increasing Retire Prior To values
requirements.statement: A receiver MUST ignore any Retire Prior To fields that do not increase the largest received Retire Prior To value.

requirements.title: Retire lower-sequence NEW_CONNECTION_ID entries
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame with a sequence number smaller than the Retire Prior To field of a previously received NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame MUST send a corresponding RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame that retires the newly received connection ID, unless it has already done so for that sequence number.

requirements.title: Defend version negotiation against downgrade
requirements.statement: Future versions of QUIC that use Version Negotiation packets MUST define a mechanism that is robust against version downgrade attacks.

requirements.title: Discard connection state if it does not have a validated path on which it can send packets
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY discard connection state if it does not have a validated path on which it can send packets; see Section 8.2.

requirements.title: To avoid excessively small idle timeout periods, endpoints MUST increase the idle timeout period to be at least three times the current Probe Timeout (PTO)
requirements.statement: To avoid excessively small idle timeout periods, endpoints MUST increase the idle timeout period to be at least three times the current Probe Timeout (PTO).

requirements.title: Advertise and compute idle timeout
requirements.statement: Each endpoint MUST advertise a `max_idle_timeout`, and the effective value at an endpoint is the minimum of the two advertised values, or the sole advertised value if only one endpoint advertises a non-zero value.

requirements.title: Allow liveness probes
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY send a PING or another ack-eliciting frame to test the connection for liveness if the peer could time out soon.

requirements.title: Allow deferring idle timeout
requirements.statement: An implementation of QUIC MAY provide applications with an option to defer an idle timeout.

requirements.title: Close all streams on CONNECTION_CLOSE
requirements.statement: A CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MUST cause all streams to immediately become closed.

requirements.title: Reset open streams implicitly
requirements.statement: Open streams MUST be implicitly reset when a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame is sent.

requirements.title: Permit immediate close after application shutdown
requirements.statement: An immediate close MAY be used after an application protocol has arranged to close a connection.

requirements.title: While otherwise identical to the closing state, an endpoint in the draining state MUST NOT send any packets
requirements.statement: While otherwise identical to the closing state, an endpoint in the draining state MUST NOT send any packets.

requirements.title: Enter draining on peer close
requirements.statement: The draining state MUST be entered once an endpoint receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, which indicates that its peer is closing or draining.

requirements.title: After the handshake is confirmed (see Section 4
requirements.statement: After the handshake is confirmed (see Section 4.1.2 of [QUIC-TLS]), an endpoint MUST send any CONNECTION_CLOSE frames in a 1-RTT packet.

requirements.title: However, prior to confirming the handshake, it is possible that more advanced packet protection keys are not available to the peer, so another CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY be sent in a packet that uses a lower packet protection level
requirements.statement: However, prior to confirming the handshake, it is possible that more advanced packet protection keys are not available to the peer, so another CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY be sent in a packet that uses a lower packet protection level.

requirements.title: Under these circumstances, a server SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and Initial packets to ensure that at least one of them is processable by the client
requirements.statement: Under these circumstances, a server SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and Initial packets to ensure that at least one of them is processable by the client.

requirements.title: Prior to confirming the handshake, a peer might be unable to process 1-RTT packets, so an endpoint SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and 1-RTT packets
requirements.statement: Prior to confirming the handshake, a peer might be unable to process 1-RTT packets, so an endpoint SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and 1-RTT packets.

requirements.title: Also send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in an Initial packet
requirements.statement: A server SHOULD also send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in an Initial packet.

requirements.title: For this reason, endpoints MAY discard packets rather than immediately close if errors are detected in packets that lack authentication
requirements.statement: For this reason, endpoints MAY discard packets rather than immediately close if errors are detected in packets that lack authentication.

requirements.title: Send post-handshake close in 1-RTT
requirements.statement: After the handshake is confirmed, an endpoint MUST send any CONNECTION_CLOSE frames in a 1-RTT packet.

requirements.title: Allow lower-protection close before handshake confirmation
requirements.statement: Prior to confirming the handshake, another CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY be sent in a packet that uses a lower packet protection level.

requirements.title: Close in Handshake and 1-RTT before confirmation
requirements.statement: Prior to confirming the handshake, an endpoint SHOULD send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in both Handshake and 1-RTT packets.

requirements.title: Downgrade close type for Initial and Handshake
requirements.statement: A CONNECTION_CLOSE frame of type 0x1d MUST be replaced by a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame of type 0x1c when sending the frame in Initial or Handshake packets.

requirements.title: Clear Reason Phrase when downgrading close type
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST clear the value of the Reason Phrase field when converting to a CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1c.

requirements.title: Prefer APPLICATION_ERROR when downgrading close type
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD use the APPLICATION_ERROR code when converting to a CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1c.

requirements.title: Use a hard-to-guess 16-byte stateless reset token
requirements.statement: A stateless reset token MUST be 16 bytes long and difficult to guess.

requirements.title: Use the Figure 10 packet layout for Stateless Reset
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives packets that it cannot process MUST send a packet in the layout shown in Figure 10.

requirements.title: Send Stateless Reset as a short-header packet
requirements.statement: A Stateless Reset MUST use an entire UDP datagram, starting with the first two bits of the packet header.

requirements.title: The remainder of the first byte and an arbitrary number of bytes following it are set to values that SHOULD be indistinguishable from random
requirements.statement: The remainder of the first byte and an arbitrary number of bytes following it are set to values that SHOULD be indistinguishable from random.

requirements.title: Include at least 38 unpredictable bits
requirements.statement: For the Stateless Reset to appear as a valid QUIC packet, the Unpredictable Bits field MUST include at least 38 bits of data.

requirements.title: Pad packets to keep Stateless Reset hard to distinguish
requirements.statement: To achieve that end, the endpoint SHOULD ensure that all packets it sends are at least 22 bytes longer than the minimum connection ID length that it requests the peer to include in its packets, adding PADDING frames as necessary.

requirements.title: Make short-packet Stateless Resets one byte shorter
requirements.statement: An endpoint that sends a Stateless Reset in response to a packet that is 43 bytes or shorter SHOULD send a Stateless Reset that is one byte shorter than the packet it responds to.

requirements.title: Format Stateless Resets with a short header
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST send Stateless Resets formatted as a packet with a short header.

requirements.title: Treat any packet ending in a valid reset token as a Stateless Reset
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST treat any packet ending in a valid stateless reset token as a Stateless Reset.

requirements.title: Make reset tokens hard to guess
requirements.statement: The stateless reset token MUST be difficult to guess.

requirements.title: Advertise reset tokens in NEW_CONNECTION_ID
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST issue a stateless reset token by including the value in the Stateless Reset Token field of a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.

requirements.title: Permit server transport-parameter reset tokens
requirements.statement: Servers MAY issue a stateless_reset_token transport parameter during the handshake that applies to the connection ID that it selected during the handshake.

requirements.title: End the connection on received reset
requirements.statement: If a peer receives a Stateless Reset, it MUST immediately end the connection.

requirements.title: Send reset using the Figure 10 layout
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives packets it cannot process MUST send a packet using the Stateless Reset layout shown in Figure 10.

requirements.title: Set fixed bits to 1
requirements.statement: Stateless Reset packets MUST set the fixed bits to 1.

requirements.title: Make leading reset bytes look random
requirements.statement: The remainder of the first byte and an arbitrary number of bytes following it SHOULD be indistinguishable from random.

requirements.title: Place the token in the tail
requirements.statement: The last 16 bytes of a Stateless Reset datagram MUST contain a stateless reset token.

requirements.title: Provide enough unpredictable bits
requirements.statement: The Unpredictable Bits field MUST include at least 38 bits of data.

requirements.title: Use a full UDP datagram
requirements.statement: A Stateless Reset MUST use an entire UDP datagram starting with the first two bits of the packet header.

requirements.title: Pad packets to improve reset indistinguishability
requirements.statement: To achieve that end, the endpoint SHOULD ensure that all packets it sends are at least 22 bytes longer than the minimum connection ID length it requests the peer to include in its packets, adding PADDING frames as necessary.

requirements.title: Avoid amplification with Stateless Reset
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send a Stateless Reset that is three times or more larger than the packet it receives to avoid being used for amplification.

requirements.title: Support all negotiated versions in reset generation
requirements.statement: An endpoint that supports multiple versions of QUIC MUST generate a Stateless Reset that will be accepted by peers that support any version that the endpoint might support or might have supported prior to losing state.

requirements.title: Use the trailing 16 bytes to detect Stateless Reset
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST use the trailing 16 bytes of the UDP datagram to detect a potential Stateless Reset.

requirements.title: Enter draining on a matching stateless reset token
requirements.statement: If the last 16 bytes of the datagram are identical in value to a stateless reset token, the endpoint MUST enter the draining period and not send any further packets on this connection.

requirements.title: Remember and scope reset tokens
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST remember all stateless reset tokens associated with connection IDs and remote addresses for datagrams it has recently sent, including Stateless Reset Token field values from NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames and the server's transport parameters, and excluding tokens associated with connection IDs that are unused or retired.

requirements.title: Be difficult to guess
requirements.statement: The stateless reset token MUST be difficult to guess.

requirements.title: Truncate the stateless reset token to 16 bytes
requirements.statement: The output of this function MUST be truncated to 16 bytes to produce the stateless reset token for that connection.

requirements.title: Disallow zero-length connection IDs for static-key tokens
requirements.statement: A static-key token function MUST NOT provide a zero-length connection ID.

requirements.title: Allow per-connection random secrets
requirements.statement: In order to create a stateless reset token, an endpoint MAY randomly generate a secret for every connection that it creates.

requirements.title: Allow static-key token generation
requirements.statement: A single static key MAY be used across all connections to the same endpoint by generating the proof using a pseudorandom function that takes a static key and the connection ID chosen by the endpoint as input.

requirements.title: Forbid zero-length connection IDs
requirements.statement: An endpoint that uses this design MUST NOT provide a zero-length connection ID.

requirements.title: Keep Stateless Reset smaller than the triggering packet
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST ensure that every Stateless Reset that it sends is smaller than the packet that triggered it, unless it maintains state sufficient to prevent looping.

requirements.title: Allow a reset-send limit
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY remember the number of Stateless Resets that it has sent and stop generating new Stateless Resets once a limit is reached.

requirements.title: Limiting the number of retransmissions and the time over which this final packet is sent limits the effort expended on terminated connections
requirements.statement: Limiting the number of retransmissions and the time over which this final packet MUST be sent limits the effort expended on terminated connections.

requirements.title: An endpoint that continues to receive data for a terminated connection MUST attempt the stateless reset process
requirements.statement: An endpoint that continues to receive data for a terminated connection MUST attempt the stateless reset process (Section 10.3).

requirements.title: If an application-level error affects a single stream but otherwise leaves the connection in a recoverable state, the endpoint can send a RESET_STREAM frame (Section 19
requirements.statement: If an application-level error MUST affects a single stream but otherwise leaves the connection in a recoverable state, the endpoint can send a RESET_STREAM frame (Section 19.4) with an appropriate error code to terminate just the affected stream.

requirements.title: Allow stream termination only by the application protocol
requirements.statement: A stream MUST only be terminated by the application protocol.

requirements.title: A local instance of the application protocol uses a direct API call, and a remote instance uses the STOP_SENDING frame, which triggers an automatic RESET_STREAM
requirements.statement: A local instance of MUST the application protocol uses a direct API call, and a remote instance uses the STOP_SENDING frame, which triggers an automatic RESET_STREAM.

requirements.title: Retry packets use an AEAD function [AEAD] to protect against accidental modification
requirements.statement: Retry packets use an MUST AEAD function [AEAD] to protect against accidental modification.

requirements.title: Initial packets use an AEAD function, the keys for which are derived using a value that is visible on the wire
requirements.statement: Initial packets use an MUST AEAD function, the keys for which are derived using a value that is visible on the wire.

requirements.title: Initial protection exists to ensure that the sender of the packet is on the network path
requirements.statement: Initial protection exists to MUST ensure that the sender of the packet is on the network path.

requirements.title: Any entity that receives an Initial packet from a client can recover the keys that will allow them to both read the contents of the packet and generate Initial packets that will be successfully authenticated at either endpoint
requirements.statement: Any entity that receives MUST an Initial packet from a client can recover the keys that will allow them to both read the contents of the packet and generate Initial packets that will be successfully authenticated at either endpoint.

requirements.title: The AEAD also protects Initial packets against accidental modification
requirements.statement: The AEAD also protects MUST Initial packets against accidental modification.

requirements.title: The cryptographic handshake ensures that only the communicating endpoints receive the corresponding keys for Handshake, 0-RTT, and 1-RTT packets
requirements.statement: The cryptographic handshake ensures MUST that only the communicating endpoints receive the corresponding keys for Handshake, 0-RTT, and 1-RTT packets.

requirements.title: The length includes both the Packet Number and Payload fields, both of which are confidentiality protected and initially of unknown length
requirements.statement: The length includes both MUST the Packet Number and Payload fields, both of which are confidentiality protected and initially of unknown length.

requirements.title: Using the Length field, a sender can coalesce multiple QUIC packets into one UDP datagram
requirements.statement: Using the Length MUST field, a sender can coalesce multiple QUIC packets into one UDP datagram.

requirements.title: include multiple frames in a single packet if they are to be sent at the same encryption level, instead of coalescing multiple packets at the same encryption level
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD include multiple frames in a single packet if they are to be sent at the same encryption level, instead of coalescing multiple packets at the same encryption level.

requirements.title: Retry packets (Section 17
requirements.statement: Retry packets (Section 17.2.5), Version Negotiation packets (Section 17.2.1), and packets with a short header (Section 17.3) MUST NOT contain a Length field or be followed by other packets in the same UDP datagram.

requirements.title: This number is used in determining the cryptographic nonce for packet protection
requirements.statement: This number MUST be used in determining the cryptographic nonce for packet protection.

requirements.title: maintains a separate packet number for sending and receiving
requirements.statement: Each endpoint maintains a MUST separate packet number for sending and receiving.

requirements.title: Version Negotiation (Section 17
requirements.statement: Version Negotiation (Section 17.2.1) and Retry (Section 17.2.5) packets MUST NOT include a packet number.

requirements.title: Initial packets can only be sent with Initial packet protection keys and acknowledged in packets that are also Initial packets
requirements.statement: Initial packets MUST only be sent with Initial packet protection keys and acknowledged in packets that are also Initial packets.

requirements.title: Similarly, Handshake packets are sent at the Handshake encryption level and can only be acknowledged in Handshake packets
requirements.statement: Handshake packets MUST be sent at the Handshake encryption level and be acknowledged only in Handshake packets.

requirements.title: Allow Stateless Reset after packet-number exhaustion
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to further packets that it receives after packet-number exhaustion.

requirements.title: Duplicate suppression MUST happen after removing packet protection for the reasons described in Section 9
requirements.statement: Duplicate suppression MUST happen after removing packet protection for the reasons described in Section 9.5 of [QUIC-TLS].

requirements.title: Keep frames within one packet
requirements.statement: Frames MUST fit within a single QUIC packet rather than span multiple packets.

requirements.title: A description of this summary is included after the table
requirements.statement: A description of this summary MUST be included after the table.

requirements.title: Use Frame Type for frame-specific flags in selected frames
requirements.statement: The Frame Type in ACK, STREAM, MAX_STREAMS, STREAMS_BLOCKED, and CONNECTION_CLOSE frames MUST be used to carry other frame-specific flags.

requirements.title: Limit Initial and Handshake appearance of CONNECTION_CLOSE type 0x1c
requirements.statement: Only a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame of type 0x1c MAY appear in Initial or Handshake packets.

requirements.title: Treat N-marked packets as not ack-eliciting
requirements.statement: Packets containing only frames with the N marking MUST NOT be ack-eliciting.

requirements.title: Exclude C-marked packets from bytes in flight
requirements.statement: Packets containing only frames with the C marking MUST NOT count toward bytes in flight for congestion control purposes.

requirements.title: Allow P-marked packets to probe new paths
requirements.statement: Packets containing only frames with the P marking MAY be used to probe new network paths during connection migration.

requirements.title: Treat F-marked frame contents as flow controlled
requirements.statement: The contents of frames with the F marking MUST be flow controlled.

requirements.title: Treat unknown frame types as frame encoding errors
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a frame of unknown type as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.

requirements.title: Make frames idempotent
requirements.statement: All frames MUST be idempotent in this version of QUIC.

requirements.title: That is, a valid frame does not cause undesirable side effects or errors when received more than once
requirements.statement: That is, a valid frame MUST NOT cause undesirable side effects or errors when received more than once.

requirements.title: Allow longer-than-necessary frame-type encodings to fail
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY treat receipt of a frame type that uses a longer encoding than necessary as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: The rules here generalize those of TLS, in that frames associated with establishing the connection can usually appear in packets in any packet number space, whereas those associated with transferring data can only appear in the application data packet number space
requirements.statement: The rules here generalize those of TLS, in that frames associated with establishing the connection can usually appear in packets in any packet number space, whereas those associated with transferring data MUST only appear in the application data packet number space:

requirements.title: Allow QUIC-layer CONNECTION_CLOSE in any packet number space
requirements.statement: CONNECTION_CLOSE frames signaling errors at the QUIC layer MAY appear in any packet number space.

requirements.title: Restrict application-error CONNECTION_CLOSE to application data
requirements.statement: CONNECTION_CLOSE frames signaling application errors MUST only appear in the application data packet number space.

requirements.title: Allow ACK in any packet number space but only acknowledge within that space
requirements.statement: ACK frames MAY appear in any packet number space, but they can only acknowledge packets that appeared in that packet number space.

requirements.title: treat receipt of these frames in 0-RTT packets as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION
requirements.statement: A server MAY treat receipt of these frames in 0-RTT packets as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Send one or more frames in each QUIC packet
requirements.statement: A sender MUST send one or more frames in a QUIC packet.

requirements.title: A single QUIC packet can include multiple STREAM frames from one or more streams
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY include multiple STREAM frames from one or more streams in a single QUIC packet.

requirements.title: Implementations are advised to include as few streams as necessary in outgoing packets without losing transmission efficiency to underfilled packets
requirements.statement: Implementations SHOULD include as few streams as necessary in outgoing packets without losing transmission efficiency to underfilled packets.

requirements.title: For STREAM frames, this means the data has been enqueued in preparation to be received by the application protocol, but it does not require that data be delivered and consumed
requirements.statement: For STREAM frames, this means the data has been enqueued in preparation to be received by the application protocol, but it MUST NOT require that data be delivered and consumed.

requirements.title: Acknowledge processed packets with ACK frames
requirements.statement: Once the packet has been fully processed, a receiver MUST acknowledge receipt by sending one or more ACK frames containing the packet number of the received packet.

requirements.title: Send ACK frames within max_ack_delay only for ack-eliciting packets
requirements.statement: Only ack-eliciting packets MUST cause an ACK frame to be sent within the maximum ack delay.

requirements.title: Acknowledge non-ack-eliciting packets only for other reasons
requirements.statement: Packets that are not ack-eliciting MUST only be acknowledged when an ACK frame is sent for other reasons.

requirements.title: Acknowledge ack-eliciting packets within max_ack_delay
requirements.statement: Ack-eliciting packets MUST be acknowledged at least once within the maximum delay the endpoint communicated using the max_ack_delay transport parameter.

requirements.title: uses the receiver's max_ack_delay value in determining timeouts for timer-based retransmission, as detailed in Section 6
requirements.statement: A sender uses the MUST receiver's max_ack_delay value in determining timeouts for timer-based retransmission, as detailed in Section 6.2 of [QUIC-RECOVERY].

requirements.title: Do not send non-ack-eliciting packets in response to non-ack-eliciting packets
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send a non-ack-eliciting packet in response to a non-ack-eliciting packet, even if there are packet gaps that precede the received packet.

requirements.title: Non-ack-eliciting packets are eventually acknowledged when the endpoint sends an ACK frame in response to other events
requirements.statement: Non-ack-eliciting packets are eventually MUST acknowledged when the endpoint sends an ACK frame in response to other events.

requirements.title: Send ACK frames without delay for out-of-order or gap-detecting packets
requirements.statement: To assist loss detection at the sender, an endpoint SHOULD generate and send an ACK frame without delay when it receives an ack-eliciting packet that has a packet number less than another ack-eliciting packet that has been received, or when the packet has a packet number larger than the highest-numbered ack-eliciting packet that has been received and there are missing packets between that packet and this packet.

requirements.title: determines how frequently to send acknowledgments in response to ack-eliciting packets
requirements.statement: A receiver determines how MUST frequently to send acknowledgments in response to ack-eliciting packets.

requirements.title: When an ACK frame is sent, one or more ranges of acknowledged packets are included
requirements.statement: When an ACK frame is sent, one or more ranges of acknowledged packets MUST be included.

requirements.title: If it does not, then older ranges (those with the smallest packet numbers) are omitted
requirements.statement: If it MUST NOT, then older ranges (those with the smallest packet numbers) are omitted.

requirements.title: Senders can expect acknowledgments for most packets, but QUIC does not guarantee receipt of an acknowledgment for every packet that the receiver processes
requirements.statement: Senders can expect acknowledgments for most packets, but QUIC MUST NOT guarantee receipt of an acknowledgment for every packet that the receiver processes.

requirements.title: Discard ACK ranges when a frame would be too large
requirements.statement: A receiver MUST discard unacknowledged ACK Ranges if an ACK frame would be too large to fit in a packet.

requirements.title: Section 13
requirements.statement: Section MUST 13.2.4 describes an exemplary approach for determining what packets to acknowledge in each ACK frame.

requirements.title: In cases with ACK frame loss and reordering, this approach does not guarantee that every acknowledgment is seen by the sender before it is no longer included in the ACK frame
requirements.statement: In cases with ACK frame loss and reordering, this approach MUST NOT guarantee that every acknowledgment is seen by the sender before it is no longer included in the ACK frame.

requirements.title: Measure intentional acknowledgment delays
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST measure the delays intentionally introduced between the time the packet with the largest packet number is received and the time an acknowledgment is sent.

requirements.title: Encode acknowledgment delay in ACK Delay
requirements.statement: The endpoint MUST encode this acknowledgment delay in the ACK Delay field of an ACK frame.

requirements.title: Acknowledge client 0-RTT packets with 1-RTT packets
requirements.statement: Packets that a client sends with 0-RTT packet protection MUST be acknowledged by the server in packets protected by 1-RTT keys.

requirements.title: This can mean that the client is unable to use these acknowledgments if the server cryptographic handshake messages are delayed or lost
requirements.statement: A client MAY be unable to use 0-RTT acknowledgments when the server cryptographic handshake messages are delayed or lost.

requirements.title: Do not retransmit lost packets whole
requirements.statement: QUIC packets that are determined to be lost MUST NOT be retransmitted whole.

requirements.title: Do not retransmit lost frames whole
requirements.statement: The same rule MUST apply to the frames that are contained within lost packets.

requirements.title: Send lost information again in new frames
requirements.statement: Instead, the information that might be carried in frames MUST be sent again in new frames as needed.

requirements.title: Use new frames and packets for lost information
requirements.statement: New frames and packets MUST be used to carry information that is determined to have been lost.

requirements.title: Stop resending information once it is acknowledged
