requirements.statement: In general, information MUST be sent again when a packet containing that information is determined to be lost and cease being sent when a packet containing that information is acknowledged.

requirements.title: Discard CRYPTO data when its packet number space is discarded
requirements.statement: Data in CRYPTO frames for Initial and Handshake packets MUST be discarded when the keys for the corresponding packet number space are discarded.

requirements.title: Retransmit STREAM data unless RESET_STREAM was sent
requirements.statement: Application data sent in STREAM frames MUST be retransmitted in new STREAM frames unless the endpoint has sent a RESET_STREAM for that stream.

requirements.title: Stop needing STREAM frames after RESET_STREAM
requirements.statement: Once an endpoint sends a RESET_STREAM frame, it MAY omit further STREAM frames.

requirements.title: Carry the most recent acknowledgments and delay in ACK frames
requirements.statement: ACK frames MUST carry the most recent set of acknowledgments and the acknowledgment delay from the largest acknowledged packet.

requirements.title: Retransmit RESET_STREAM until acknowledged or data is acknowledged
requirements.statement: Cancellation of stream transmission, as carried in a RESET_STREAM frame, MUST be sent until acknowledged or until all stream data is acknowledged by the peer.

requirements.title: Retransmit STOP_SENDING until the stream reaches a terminal state
requirements.statement: A request to cancel stream transmission, as encoded in a STOP_SENDING frame, MUST be sent until the receiving part of the stream enters either a Data Recvd state or a Reset Recvd state.

requirements.title: Send current connection maximum data in MAX_DATA frames
requirements.statement: The current connection maximum data MUST be sent in MAX_DATA frames.

requirements.title: Send current stream data offsets in MAX_STREAM_DATA frames
requirements.statement: The current maximum stream data offset MUST be sent in MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.

requirements.title: Send updated MAX_STREAM_DATA values when the frame is lost or the limit changes
requirements.statement: Like MAX_DATA, an updated value MUST be sent when the packet containing the most recent MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a stream is lost or when the limit is updated.

requirements.title: Stop sending MAX_STREAM_DATA once the stream is closed or reset
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD stop sending MAX_STREAM_DATA frames when the receiving part of the stream enters a Size Known or Reset Recvd state.

requirements.title: Send updated MAX_STREAMS values when the frame is lost or the limit changes
requirements.statement: Like MAX_DATA, an updated value MUST be sent when a packet containing the most recent MAX_STREAMS for a stream type frame is declared lost or when the limit is updated.

requirements.title: Carry blocked signals in dedicated frames
requirements.statement: Blocked signals MUST be carried in DATA_BLOCKED, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, and STREAMS_BLOCKED frames.

requirements.title: Scope blocked signals appropriately
requirements.statement: DATA_BLOCKED, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, and STREAMS_BLOCKED frames MUST use connection, stream, and stream-type scope respectively.

requirements.title: Send a new blocked frame while blocked and the latest frame is lost
requirements.statement: A new frame MUST be sent if a packet containing the most recent frame for a scope is lost, but only while the endpoint is blocked on the corresponding limit.

requirements.title: Include the blocking limit in blocked frames
requirements.statement: These frames MUST always include the limit that is causing blocking at the time that they are transmitted.

requirements.title: Send new connection IDs in NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames and retransmit them if lost
requirements.statement: New connection IDs MUST be sent in NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames and retransmitted if the packet containing them is lost.

requirements.title: Send retired connection IDs in RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames and retransmit them if lost
requirements.statement: Retired connection IDs MUST be sent in RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames and retransmitted if the packet containing them is lost.

requirements.title: Compare NEW_TOKEN frames directly for duplicates and reordering
requirements.statement: No special support MUST be used for detecting reordered and duplicated NEW_TOKEN frames other than a direct comparison of the frame contents.

requirements.title: PING and PADDING frames contain no information, so lost PING or PADDING frames do not require repair
requirements.statement: PING and PADDING frames contain no information, so lost PING or PADDING frames MUST NOT require repair.

requirements.title: prioritize retransmission of data over sending new data, unless priorities specified by the application indicate otherwise
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD prioritize retransmission of data over sending new data, unless priorities specified by the application indicate otherwise; see Section 2.3.

requirements.title: This includes packets that are acknowledged after being declared lost, which can happen in the presence of network reordering
requirements.statement: This includes packets that MUST are acknowledged after being declared lost, which can happen in the presence of network reordering.

requirements.title: can discard this information after a period of time elapses that adequately allows for reordering, such as a PTO (Section 6
requirements.statement: A sender can discard MUST this information after a period of time elapses that adequately allows for reordering, such as a PTO (Section 6.2 of [QUIC-RECOVERY]), or based on other events, such as reaching a memory limit.

requirements.title: QUIC endpoints MAY use ECN to detect and respond to network congestion
requirements.statement: QUIC endpoints MAY use ECN [RFC3168] to detect and respond to network congestion.

requirements.title: Do not report ECN counts without ECN support or ECN field access
requirements.statement: If an endpoint does not implement ECN support or does not have access to received ECN fields, it MUST NOT report ECN counts for packets it receives.

requirements.title: Even if an endpoint does not set an ECT field in packets it sends, the endpoint MUST provide feedback about ECN markings it receives, if these are accessible
requirements.statement: Even if an endpoint does not set an ECT field in packets it sends, the endpoint MUST provide feedback about ECN markings it receives, if these are accessible.

requirements.title: Failing to report the ECN counts will cause the sender to disable the use of ECN for this connection
requirements.statement: Failing to report the MUST ECN counts will cause the sender to disable the use of ECN for this connection.

requirements.title: Update ECN counts when receiving marked IP packets
requirements.statement: On receiving an IP packet with an ECT(0), ECT(1), or ECN-CE codepoint, an ECN-enabled endpoint MUST access the ECN field and increase the corresponding ECT(0), ECT(1), or ECN-CE count.

requirements.title: Keep separate ECN counts per packet number space
requirements.statement: Each packet number space MUST maintain separate acknowledgment state and separate ECN counts.

requirements.title: Count ECN once per coalesced QUIC packet
requirements.statement: Coalesced QUIC packets share the same IP header so the ECN counts MUST be incremented once for each coalesced QUIC packet.

requirements.title: Count ECN for each packet number space in a coalesced datagram
requirements.statement: If one Initial, one Handshake, and one 1-RTT QUIC packet are coalesced into a single UDP datagram, the ECN counts for all three packet number spaces MUST be incremented by one each based on the ECN field of the single IP header.

requirements.title: Validate ECN counts per path and disable ECN on errors
requirements.statement: To ensure connectivity in the presence of such devices, an endpoint MUST validate the ECN counts for each network path and disable the use of ECN on that path if errors are detected.

requirements.title: Watch for ECN-marked packets being lost
requirements.statement: The endpoint MUST monitor whether all packets sent with an ECT codepoint are eventually deemed lost, indicating that ECN validation has failed.

requirements.title: Validate ECN for each new connection and path change
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST attempt to use ECN and validate this for each new connection, when switching to a server's preferred address, and on active connection migration to a new path.

requirements.title: Implementations MAY use other methods defined in RFCs
requirements.statement: Implementations MAY use other methods defined in RFCs; see [RFC8311].

requirements.title: Validate ECN using ECT(1) counts when ECT(1) is used
requirements.statement: Implementations that use the ECT(1) codepoint MUST perform ECN validation using the reported ECT(1) counts.

requirements.title: Fail ECN validation when counts are missing for newly acknowledged ECT packets
requirements.statement: If an ACK frame newly acknowledges a packet that the endpoint sent with either the ECT(0) or ECT(1) codepoint set, ECN validation MUST fail if the corresponding ECN counts are not present in the ACK frame.

requirements.title: This check detects a network element that zeroes the ECN field or a peer that does not report ECN markings
requirements.statement: This check detects a network element that zeroes the ECN field or a peer that MUST NOT report ECN markings.

requirements.title: Fail ECN validation when received counts exceed sent counts
requirements.statement: ECN validation MUST fail if the received total count for either ECT(0) or ECT(1) exceeds the total number of packets sent with each corresponding ECT codepoint.

requirements.title: Fail ECN validation for never-applied ECT counts
requirements.statement: Validation MUST fail when an endpoint receives a non-zero ECN count corresponding to an ECT codepoint that it never applied.

requirements.title: Disable ECN when validation fails
requirements.statement: If validation fails, then the endpoint MUST disable ECN.

requirements.title: It stops setting the ECT codepoint in IP packets that it sends, assuming that either the network path or the peer does not support ECN
requirements.statement: It stops setting the ECT codepoint in IP packets that it sends, assuming that either the network path or the peer MUST NOT support ECN.

requirements.title: The datagram size includes one or more QUIC packet headers and protected payloads, but not the UDP or IP headers
requirements.statement: The datagram size includes MUST one or more QUIC packet headers and protected payloads, but not the UDP or IP headers.

requirements.title: Define maximum datagram size as the largest UDP payload across a path
requirements.statement: The maximum datagram size MUST be defined as the largest size of UDP payload that can be sent across a network path using a single UDP datagram.

requirements.title: Use PMTUD or DPLPMTUD to discover larger datagram sizes
requirements.statement: Any maximum datagram size larger than 1200 bytes MUST be discovered using Path Maximum Transmission Unit Discovery (PMTUD) or Datagram Packetization Layer PMTU Discovery (DPLPMTUD).

requirements.title: Avoid exceeding the max_udp_payload_size once known
requirements.statement: A sender MUST avoid exceeding the max_udp_payload_size transport parameter limit once the value is known.

requirements.title: In IPv4 [IPv4], the Don't Fragment (DF) bit MUST be set if possible, to prevent fragmentation on the path
requirements.statement: In IPv4 [IPv4], the Don't Fragment (DF) bit MUST be set if possible, to prevent fragmentation on the path.

requirements.title: Treat received datagram size as unauthenticated
requirements.statement: If an endpoint receives a datagram of a certain size, it MUST NOT assume that the sender sent the datagram at the same size.

requirements.title: Initial packets can even be coalesced with invalid packets, which a receiver will discard
requirements.statement: Initial packets can even MUST be coalesced with invalid packets, which a receiver will discard.

requirements.title: Sending UDP datagrams of this size ensures that the network path supports a reasonable Path Maximum Transmission Unit (PMTU), in both directions
requirements.statement: Sending UDP datagrams of MUST this size ensures that the network path supports a reasonable Path Maximum Transmission Unit (PMTU), in both directions.

requirements.title: The UDP payload includes one or more QUIC packet headers and protected payloads
requirements.statement: The UDP payload includes MUST one or more QUIC packet headers and protected payloads.

requirements.title: The largest UDP payload an endpoint sends at any given time is referred to as the endpoint's maximum datagram size
requirements.statement: The largest UDP payload MUST an endpoint sends at any given time is referred to as the endpoint's maximum datagram size.

requirements.title: Both DPLPMTUD and PMTUD send datagrams that are larger than the current maximum datagram size, referred to as PMTU probes
requirements.statement: Both DPLPMTUD and PMTUD MUST send datagrams that are larger than the current maximum datagram size, referred to as PMTU probes.

requirements.title: Size non-PMTU-probe packets to fit within the maximum datagram size
requirements.statement: All QUIC packets that are not sent in a PMTU probe SHOULD be sized to fit within the maximum datagram size.

requirements.title: DPLPMTUD [DPLPMTUD] relies on tracking loss or acknowledgment of QUIC packets that are carried in PMTU probes
requirements.statement: DPLPMTUD [DPLPMTUD] relies on tracking loss or acknowledgment of QUIC packets that MUST be carried in PMTU probes.

requirements.title: PMTU probes for DPLPMTUD that use the PADDING frame implement "Probing using padding data", as defined in Section 4
requirements.statement: PMTU probes for DPLPMTUD MUST that use the PADDING frame implement "Probing using padding data", as defined in Section 4.1 of [DPLPMTUD].

requirements.title: Make PMTU probes ack-eliciting
requirements.statement: PMTU probes MUST be ack-eliciting packets.

requirements.statement: The largest offset delivered on a stream -- the sum of the offset and data length -- MUST NOT exceed 262-1, as it is not possible to provide flow control credit for that data.

requirements.title: Receipt of a frame that exceeds this limit MUST be treated as a connection error of type FRAM...
requirements.statement: Receipt of a frame that exceeds this limit MUST be treated as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR or FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.

requirements.title: A MAX_DATA frame (type=0x10) MUST be used in flow control to inform the peer of the maximum a...
requirements.statement: A MAX_DATA frame (type=0x10) MUST be used in flow control to inform the peer of the maximum amount of data that can be sent on the connection as a whole.

requirements.title: The Type field MUST be encoded as a variable-length integer with value 0x10
requirements.statement: The Type field MUST be encoded as a variable-length integer with value 0x10.

requirements.title: The Maximum Data field MUST be encoded as a variable-length integer
requirements.statement: The Maximum Data field MUST be encoded as a variable-length integer.

requirements.title: MAX_DATA frames MUST contain the following field:
requirements.statement: MAX_DATA frames MUST contain the following field:

requirements.title: A variable-length integer indicating the maximum amount of data that MAY be sent on the entir...
requirements.statement: A variable-length integer indicating the maximum amount of data that MAY be sent on the entire connection, in units of bytes.

requirements.title: The sum of the final sizes on all streams -- including streams in terminal states -- MUST NOT...
requirements.statement: The sum of the final sizes on all streams -- including streams in terminal states -- MUST NOT exceed the value advertised by a receiver.

requirements.title: This MUST include violations of remembered limits in Early Data; see Section 7.4.1
requirements.statement: This MUST include violations of remembered limits in Early Data; see Section 7.4.1.

requirements.title: Allow streams to be long-lived
requirements.statement: Streams in QUIC MAY last for the entire duration of a connection.

requirements.title: This section lists the defined QUIC transport error codes that MAY be used in a CONNECTION_CL...
requirements.statement: This section lists the defined QUIC transport error codes that MAY be used in a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with a type of 0x1c.

requirements.title: An endpoint MUST use this with CONNECTION_CLOSE to signal that the connection is being closed...
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST use this with CONNECTION_CLOSE to signal that the connection is being closed abruptly in the absence of any error.

requirements.title: The endpoint encountered an internal error and MUST NOT continue with the connection
requirements.statement: The endpoint encountered an internal error and MUST NOT continue with the connection.

requirements.title: An endpoint has received more data in CRYPTO frames than it MAY buffer
requirements.statement: An endpoint has received more data in CRYPTO frames than it MAY buffer.

requirements.title: An endpoint is unlikely to receive a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame carrying this code except when th...
requirements.statement: An endpoint is unlikely to receive a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame carrying this code except when the path MUST NOT support a large enough MTU.

requirements.title: A range of 256 values is reserved for carrying error codes specific to the cryptographic hand...
requirements.statement: A range of 256 values is reserved for carrying error codes specific to the cryptographic handshake that MUST be used.

requirements.title: Codes for errors occurring when TLS MUST be used for the cryptographic handshake are describe...
requirements.statement: Codes for errors occurring when TLS MUST be used for the cryptographic handshake are described in Section 4.8 of [QUIC-TLS].

requirements.title: Absent either of these conditions, error codes MUST be used to identify a general function of...
requirements.statement: Absent either of these conditions, error codes MUST be used to identify a general function of the stack, like flow control or transport parameter handling.

requirements.title: Application protocol error codes MUST be used for the RESET_STREAM frame (Section 19.4), the...
requirements.statement: Application protocol error codes MUST be used for the RESET_STREAM frame (Section 19.4), the STOP_SENDING frame (Section 19.5), and the CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with a type of 0x1d (Section 19.19).

requirements.title: If duplicate packets are discarded by a receiver, an attacker will MUST race the duplicate pa...
requirements.statement: If duplicate packets are discarded by a receiver, an attacker will MUST race the duplicate packet against the original to be successful in this attack.

requirements.title: Keep Version Negotiation packets free of downgrade prevention mechanisms
requirements.statement: Version Negotiation packets MUST NOT contain any mechanism to prevent version downgrade attacks.

requirements.title: Use address validation to confirm receipt capability
requirements.statement: Address validation (Section 8) MUST be used to verify that an entity that claims a given address is able to receive packets at that address.

requirements.title: Limit bytes sent to unvalidated addresses
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST NOT send data toward an unvalidated address in excess of three times the data received from that address.

requirements.title: Disallow address change during handshake
requirements.statement: Addresses MUST NOT change during the handshake.

requirements.title: Discard packets that cannot be authenticated
requirements.statement: Packets that cannot be authenticated MUST be discarded.

requirements.title: For request forgery to be effective, an attacker MUST be able to influence what packets the p...
requirements.statement: For request forgery to be effective, an attacker MUST be able to influence what packets the peer sends and where these packets are sent.

requirements.title: Require Expert Review for provisional registrations
requirements.statement: Provisional registrations MUST undergo Expert Review, as defined in Section 4.5 of [RFC8126].

requirements.title: Include a Date field in provisional registrations
requirements.statement: Provisional registrations MUST include a Date field that indicates when the registration was last updated.

requirements.title: Allow provisional date updates without expert review
requirements.statement: A request to update the date on any provisional registration MAY be made without review from the designated expert(s).

requirements.title: Include provisional registration support fields
requirements.statement: All QUIC registries MUST include the following fields to support provisional registration.

requirements.title: Define the Value field
requirements.statement: The Value field MUST be the assigned codepoint.

requirements.title: Define the Status field
requirements.statement: The Status field MUST be "permanent" or "provisional".

requirements.title: Define the Specification field
requirements.statement: The Specification field MUST be a reference to a publicly available specification for the value.

requirements.title: Define the Date field
requirements.statement: The Date field MUST be the date of the last update to the registration.

requirements.title: Define the Change Controller field
requirements.statement: The Change Controller field MUST be the entity responsible for the definition of the registration.

requirements.title: Define the Contact field
requirements.statement: The Contact field MUST be contact details for the registrant.

requirements.title: Define the Notes field
requirements.statement: The Notes field MUST be supplementary notes about the registration.

requirements.title: Do not require Date when requesting registration
requirements.statement: The Date field MUST NOT be required as part of requesting a registration.

requirements.title: Reserve first unassigned codepoint for Standards Action
requirements.statement: The use of the first unassigned codepoint MUST be reserved for allocation using the Standards Action policy.

requirements.title: Allow early codepoint assignment for selected values
requirements.statement: The early codepoint assignment process MAY be used for these values.

requirements.title: Use Specification Required for permanent registrations
requirements.statement: Permanent registrations in QUIC registries MUST use the Specification Required policy (Section 4.6 of [RFC8126]), unless otherwise specified.

requirements.title: Verify the specification for permanent registrations
requirements.statement: The designated expert or experts MUST verify that a specification exists and is readily accessible.

requirements.title: The creation of a registry MAY specify additional constraints on permanent registrations
requirements.statement: The creation of a registry MAY specify additional constraints on permanent registrations.

requirements.title: Do not block provisional registrations with stricter permanent requirements
requirements.statement: Any stricter requirements for permanent registrations MUST NOT prevent provisional registrations for affected codepoints.

requirements.title: Assign document registrations permanent status
requirements.statement: All registrations in this document MUST be assigned a permanent status.

requirements.title: Record the change controller and contact for document registrations
requirements.statement: All registrations in this document MUST list a change controller of the IETF and a contact of the QUIC Working Group (quic@ietf.org).

requirements.title: Assign codepoint 0x00000001
requirements.statement: The codepoint of 0x00000001 for the protocol MUST be assigned with permanent status to the protocol defined in this document.

requirements.title: Use Specification Required for transport parameters
requirements.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST be assigned using the Specification Required policy.

requirements.title: Define Parameter Name
requirements.statement: The Parameter Name field MUST be a short mnemonic for the parameter.

requirements.title: Use Specification Required for frame types
requirements.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST be assigned using the Specification Required policy.

requirements.title: Use stricter policy for low frame-type codepoints
requirements.statement: Values between 0x00 and 0x3f inclusive MUST be assigned using Standards Action or IESG Approval.

requirements.title: Define Frame Type Name
requirements.statement: The Frame Type Name field MUST be a short mnemonic for the frame type.

requirements.title: In addition to the advice in Section 22.1, specifications for new permanent registrations SHO...
requirements.statement: In addition to the advice in Section 22.1, specifications for new permanent registrations SHOULD describe the means by which an endpoint might determine that it can send the identified type of frame.

requirements.title: Describe frame field semantics in specifications
requirements.statement: Specifications for permanent registrations MUST describe the format and assigned semantics of any fields in the frame.

requirements.title: Use Specification Required for transport error codes
requirements.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST be assigned using the Specification Required policy.

requirements.title: Use stricter policy for low transport error codepoints
requirements.statement: Values between 0x00 and 0x3f inclusive MUST be assigned using Standards Action or IESG Approval.

requirements.title: Include Code and Description for transport error codes
requirements.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST include the following fields.

requirements.title: Define Code
requirements.statement: The Code field MUST be a short mnemonic for the parameter.

requirements.title: Define Description
requirements.statement: The Description field MUST be a brief description of the error code semantics.

requirements.title: Constrain unidirectional stream direction
requirements.statement: A unidirectional stream MUST carry data only from the initiator of the stream to its peer.

requirements.title: Constrain bidirectional stream direction
requirements.statement: A bidirectional stream MUST allow data to be sent in both directions.

requirements.title: Identify streams by stream ID
requirements.statement: Each stream MUST be identified within a connection by a numeric value called the stream ID.

requirements.title: Use the low bit to identify stream initiator
requirements.statement: The least significant bit of a stream ID MUST identify the initiator of the stream.

requirements.title: Use even IDs for client-initiated streams
requirements.statement: Client-initiated streams MUST have even-numbered stream IDs with the least significant bit set to 0.

requirements.title: Use odd IDs for server-initiated streams
requirements.statement: Server-initiated streams MUST have odd-numbered stream IDs with the least significant bit set to 1.

requirements.title: Use the second low bit to distinguish stream direction
requirements.statement: The second least significant bit of a stream ID MUST distinguish bidirectional streams from unidirectional streams, with 0 indicating bidirectional and 1 indicating unidirectional.

requirements.title: Start each stream space at its minimum value
requirements.statement: The stream space for each type MUST begin at its minimum value.

requirements.title: Open lower-numbered streams when a stream ID is used out of order
requirements.statement: Using a stream ID out of order MUST cause all lower-numbered streams of that type to be opened.

requirements.title: Encapsulate application data in STREAM frames
requirements.statement: STREAM frames MUST encapsulate data sent by an application.

requirements.title: Buffer out-of-order stream data until it can be delivered in order
requirements.statement: To deliver an ordered byte stream, an endpoint MUST buffer any out-of-order data it receives up to the advertised flow control limit.

requirements.title: Permit discarded received data
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY discard data that has already been received.

requirements.title: Expose streams as ordered byte streams only
requirements.statement: Streams MUST be an ordered byte-stream abstraction with no other structure visible to QUIC.

requirements.title: Avoid a built-in prioritization exchange
requirements.statement: QUIC MUST NOT provide a mechanism for exchanging prioritization information.

requirements.title: Use application priority information for resource allocation
requirements.statement: A QUIC implementation SHOULD use information provided by the application to determine how to allocate resources to active streams.

requirements.title: Provide the stream operations described here
requirements.statement: A QUIC implementation MUST provide an interface that includes the operations described in this section.

requirements.title: Allow protocol-specific implementations to expose only needed operations
requirements.statement: An implementation designed for use with a specific application protocol MAY provide only those operations that are used by that protocol.

requirements.title: Allow writing data after reserving flow control credit
requirements.statement: An application protocol MAY write data only after stream flow control credit has been successfully reserved to send the written data.

requirements.title: Allow clean stream termination
requirements.statement: An application protocol MAY end a stream, resulting in a STREAM frame with the FIN bit set.

requirements.title: Allow abrupt stream termination
requirements.statement: An application protocol MAY reset a stream if the stream is not already in a terminal state, resulting in a RESET_STREAM frame.

requirements.title: Allow reading data
requirements.statement: An application protocol MAY read data from a stream.

requirements.title: Allow aborting stream reads
requirements.statement: An application protocol MAY abort reading a stream and request closure, possibly resulting in a STOP_SENDING frame.

requirements.title: Allow stream state-change notifications
requirements.statement: An application protocol MAY request to be informed of stream state changes, including when the peer has opened or reset a stream, when a peer aborts reading on a stream, when new data is available, and when data can or cannot be written to the stream due to flow control.

requirements.title: Choose the correct state machine for unidirectional streams
requirements.statement: Unidirectional streams MUST use either the sending or receiving state machine, depending on the stream type and endpoint role.

requirements.title: Use both state machines for bidirectional streams
requirements.statement: Bidirectional streams MUST use both state machines at both endpoints.

requirements.title: Allow alternate stream state machines with consistent behavior
requirements.statement: An implementation MAY define a different stream state machine as long as its behavior is consistent with an implementation that implements these states.

requirements.title: Treat Ready as a newly created sendable stream
requirements.statement: The Ready state MUST represent a newly created stream that is able to accept data from the application.

requirements.title: Permit buffering in Ready
requirements.statement: An implementation MAY buffer stream data in the Ready state in preparation for sending.

requirements.title: Enter Send state on first outbound stream frame
requirements.statement: Sending the first STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame MUST cause a sending part of a stream to enter the Send state.

requirements.title: Allow deferred stream ID allocation
requirements.statement: An implementation MAY defer allocating a stream ID to a stream until it sends the first STREAM frame and enters the Send state.

requirements.title: Start peer-initiated bidirectional senders in Ready
requirements.statement: The sending part of a bidirectional stream initiated by a peer MUST start in the Ready state when the receiving part is created.

requirements.title: Transmit and retransmit in Send
requirements.statement: In the Send state, an endpoint MUST transmit and retransmit as necessary stream data in STREAM frames.

requirements.title: Respect peer flow control while sending
requirements.statement: An endpoint in the Send state MUST respect the flow control limits set by its peer and continue to accept and process MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.

requirements.title: Restrict Data Sent retransmissions
requirements.statement: From the Data Sent state, the endpoint MUST retransmit stream data only as necessary.

requirements.title: Stop flow control checks in Data Sent
requirements.statement: An endpoint in the Data Sent state MUST NOT need to check flow control limits or send STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames for the stream.

requirements.title: Allow ignoring MAX_STREAM_DATA in Data Sent
requirements.statement: An endpoint in the Data Sent state MAY safely ignore any MAX_STREAM_DATA frames it receives from its peer for that stream.

requirements.title: Enter Data Recvd after all data is acknowledged
requirements.statement: Once all stream data has been successfully acknowledged, the sending part of the stream MUST enter the Data Recvd state.

requirements.title: Allow application abandonment of stream transmission
requirements.statement: From any state that is Ready, Send, or Data Sent, an application MAY signal that it wishes to abandon transmission of stream data.

requirements.title: Send RESET_STREAM when abandoning transmission
requirements.statement: In either case, the endpoint MUST send a RESET_STREAM frame, which causes the stream to enter the Reset Sent state.

requirements.title: Enter Reset Recvd after RESET_STREAM is acknowledged
requirements.statement: Once a packet containing a RESET_STREAM has been acknowledged, the sending part of the stream MUST enter the Reset Recvd state.

requirements.title: Do not track unobservable sending-part states
requirements.statement: The receiving part of a stream MUST NOT track states on the sending part that cannot be observed, such as the Ready state.

requirements.title: Track data delivery to the application
requirements.statement: The receiving part of a stream MUST track the delivery of data to the application, including data that cannot be observed by the sender.

requirements.title: Start receiving parts in Recv
requirements.statement: The initial state for the receiving part of a stream MUST be Recv.

requirements.title: Open bidirectional streams on peer flow-control or stop-sending frames
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST open a bidirectional stream when a MAX_STREAM_DATA or STOP_SENDING frame is received from the peer for that stream.

requirements.title: Interpret MAX_STREAM_DATA on an unopened stream as peer opening
requirements.statement: Receiving a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for an unopened stream MUST indicate that the remote peer has opened the stream and is providing flow control credit.

requirements.title: Interpret STOP_SENDING on an unopened stream as a peer desire to stop reception
requirements.statement: Receiving a STOP_SENDING frame for an unopened stream MUST indicate that the remote peer no longer wishes to receive data on this stream.

requirements.title: Allow reordered peer flow-control or stop-sending frames
requirements.statement: Either frame MAY arrive before a STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame if packets are lost or reordered.

requirements.title: Buffer received stream data for ordered delivery
requirements.statement: Incoming data MUST be buffered for ordered delivery to the application, including any reassembly needed to place it in the correct order.

requirements.title: Advertise more receive credit as data is consumed
requirements.statement: As data is consumed by the application and buffer space becomes available, the endpoint MUST send MAX_STREAM_DATA frames to allow the peer to send more data.

requirements.title: Discard further stream frames after all data is received
requirements.statement: After all data has been received, any STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames for the stream MAY be discarded.

requirements.title: Enter Data Read after delivery to the application
requirements.statement: Once stream data has been delivered, the stream MUST enter the Data Read state.

requirements.title: Enter Reset Recvd on RESET_STREAM in Recv or Size Known
requirements.statement: Receiving a RESET_STREAM frame in the Recv or Size Known state MUST cause the stream to enter the Reset Recvd state.

requirements.title: Remain in Data Recvd when RESET_STREAM is suppressed
requirements.statement: If the RESET_STREAM is suppressed, the receiving part of the stream MUST remain in Data Recvd.

requirements.title: Enter Reset Read after the application receives reset notification
requirements.statement: Once the application receives the signal indicating that the stream was reset, the receiving part of the stream MUST transition to the Reset Read state.

requirements.title: Allow delayed receipt of state-changing frames
requirements.statement: A receiver MAY receive STREAM, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, or RESET_STREAM frames in any state due to delayed delivery of packets carrying them.

requirements.title: Limit MAX_STREAM_DATA to Recv
requirements.statement: The receiver MUST only send MAX_STREAM_DATA frames in the Recv state.

requirements.title: Allow STOP_SENDING except after reset reception
requirements.statement: A receiver MAY send a STOP_SENDING frame in any state where it has not received a RESET_STREAM frame.

requirements.title: Allow delayed receipt of receiver-side frames
requirements.statement: A sender MAY receive MAX_STREAM_DATA or STOP_SENDING frames in any state as a result of delayed delivery of packets.

requirements.title: Compose bidirectional streams from send and receive parts
requirements.statement: A bidirectional stream MUST be composed of sending and receiving parts.

requirements.title: Allow composite stream-state representations
requirements.statement: Implementations MAY represent bidirectional stream states as composites of sending and receiving stream states.

requirements.title: Require acknowledgment before closed-state transitions in the example mapping
requirements.statement: Any mapping to a closed or half-closed state MUST require data to be acknowledged before the transition.

requirements.title: Allow aborting stream reads with an application error code
requirements.statement: If an application is no longer interested in the data it is receiving on a stream, it MAY abort reading the stream and specify an application error code.

requirements.title: Treat STOP_SENDING as a request for RESET_STREAM
requirements.statement: A STOP_SENDING frame MUST request that the receiving endpoint send a RESET_STREAM frame.

requirements.title: Send RESET_STREAM after receiving STOP_SENDING in Ready or Send
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives a STOP_SENDING frame MUST send a RESET_STREAM frame if the stream is in the Ready or Send state.

requirements.title: Repeat STOP_SENDING after loss
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD send another STOP_SENDING frame if a packet containing a previous STOP_SENDING is lost.

requirements.title: Allow RESET_STREAM to terminate one direction of a bidirectional stream
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY terminate one direction of a bidirectional stream by sending a RESET_STREAM frame.

requirements.title: Allow STOP_SENDING to encourage prompt opposite-direction termination
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY encourage prompt termination in the opposite direction by sending a STOP_SENDING frame.

requirements.title: Flow-control streams and the whole connection
requirements.statement: Streams MUST be flow controlled both individually and across a connection as a whole.

requirements.title: Limit bytes on streams and across the connection
requirements.statement: A QUIC receiver MUST control the maximum amount of data the sender can send on a stream and across all streams at any time.

requirements.title: Use limit-based flow control
requirements.statement: QUIC MUST employ a limit-based flow control scheme in which a receiver advertises the total bytes it is prepared to receive on a given stream or for the entire connection.

requirements.title: Limit per-stream receive buffer use
requirements.statement: Stream flow control MUST prevent a single stream from consuming the entire receive buffer for a connection by limiting the amount of data that can be sent on each stream.

requirements.title: Advertise larger flow-control limits with MAX frames
requirements.statement: Subsequently, a receiver MUST send MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frames to advertise larger limits.

requirements.title: Advertise larger connection limits with MAX_DATA
requirements.statement: A receiver MAY advertise a larger limit for a connection by sending a MAX_DATA frame.

requirements.title: Ignore smaller advertised limits
requirements.statement: Once a receiver advertises a limit for the connection or a stream, advertising a smaller limit MUST have no effect rather than be treated as an error.

requirements.title: Allow autotuning of flow-control credit
requirements.statement: A receiver MAY use an autotuning mechanism to tune the frequency and amount of advertised additional credit based on a round-trip time estimate and the rate at which the receiving application consumes data.

requirements.title: Send flow-control frames opportunistically
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY send frames related to flow control only when there are other frames to send, ensuring that flow control does not cause extra packets to be sent.

requirements.title: Do not require blocked senders to signal blocking
requirements.statement: A blocked sender MUST NOT be required to send STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frames.

requirements.title: Tear down state and ignore later data after RESET_STREAM
requirements.statement: On receipt of a RESET_STREAM frame, an endpoint MUST tear down state for the matching stream and ignore further data arriving on that stream.

requirements.title: Terminate only one direction on RESET_STREAM
requirements.statement: RESET_STREAM MUST terminate one direction of a stream abruptly.

requirements.title: Communicate final size reliably
requirements.statement: A sender MUST always communicate the final size of a stream to the receiver reliably, no matter how the stream is terminated.

requirements.title: Use STREAM FIN to carry final size
requirements.statement: The final size of a stream MUST be the sum of the Offset and Length fields of a STREAM frame with a FIN flag, including any implicit values.

requirements.title: Use RESET_STREAM Final Size to carry final size
requirements.statement: The Final Size field of a RESET_STREAM frame MUST carry the final size value.

requirements.title: Treat final-size changes as errors
requirements.statement: If a RESET_STREAM or STREAM frame is received indicating a change in the final size for the stream, an endpoint SHOULD respond with an error of type FINAL_SIZE_ERROR.

requirements.title: Limit the cumulative number of incoming streams
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST limit the cumulative number of incoming streams its peer can open.

requirements.title: Restrict stream IDs to the advertised limit
requirements.statement: Only streams with stream IDs less than max_streams * 4 + first_stream_id_of_type MAY be opened.

requirements.title: Set initial stream limits in transport parameters
requirements.statement: Initial limits MUST be set in the transport parameters.

requirements.title: Advertise later stream limits with MAX_STREAMS
requirements.statement: Subsequent limits MUST be advertised using MAX_STREAMS frames.

requirements.title: Apply separate limits by stream direction
requirements.statement: Separate limits MUST apply to unidirectional and bidirectional streams.

requirements.title: Ignore smaller advertised stream limits
requirements.statement: Once a receiver advertises a stream limit using the MAX_STREAMS frame, advertising a smaller limit MUST have no effect.

requirements.title: Ignore non-increasing MAX_STREAMS frames
requirements.statement: MAX_STREAMS frames that do not increase the stream limit MUST be ignored.

requirements.title: Treat a QUIC connection as shared client-server state
requirements.statement: A QUIC connection MUST be shared state between a client and a server.

requirements.title: Start every connection with a handshake phase
requirements.statement: Each connection MUST start with a handshake phase during which the two endpoints establish a shared secret using the cryptographic handshake protocol and negotiate the application protocol.

requirements.title: Use the handshake to confirm willingness and establish parameters
requirements.statement: The handshake MUST confirm that both endpoints are willing to communicate and establish parameters for the connection.

requirements.title: Allow limited connection use during the handshake
requirements.statement: An application protocol MAY use the connection during the handshake phase with some limitations.

requirements.title: Allow 0-RTT client data before server response
requirements.statement: 0-RTT MUST allow application data to be sent by a client before receiving a response from the server.

requirements.title: Do not provide replay protection for 0-RTT
requirements.statement: 0-RTT MUST NOT provide protection against replay attacks.

requirements.title: Allow server data before final handshake messages
requirements.statement: A server MAY send application data to a client before it receives the final cryptographic handshake messages that allow it to confirm the identity and liveness of the client.

requirements.title: Use connection IDs to enable migration
requirements.statement: Connection IDs MUST allow connections to migrate to a new network path, both as a direct choice of an endpoint and when forced by a change in a middlebox.

requirements.title: Assign each connection a set of CIDs
requirements.statement: Each connection MUST possess a set of connection IDs, each of which can identify the connection.

requirements.title: Let endpoints choose peer-used connection IDs
requirements.statement: Connection IDs MUST be independently selected by endpoints, with each endpoint selecting the connection IDs that its peer uses.

requirements.title: Use CIDs to survive address changes
requirements.statement: Connection IDs MUST ensure that changes in lower-layer addressing do not cause packets for a QUIC connection to be delivered to the wrong endpoint.

requirements.title: Make CID selection routable and recognizable
requirements.statement: Each endpoint MUST select connection IDs using an implementation-specific method that allows packets with that connection ID to be routed back to the endpoint and to be identified by the endpoint upon receipt.

requirements.title: Use multiple CIDs for privacy
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST use multiple connection IDs so that they can send packets that an observer cannot identify as belonging to the same connection without cooperation from an endpoint.

requirements.title: Include CID fields in long headers
requirements.statement: Packets with long headers MUST include Source Connection ID and Destination Connection ID fields.

requirements.title: Include only the destination CID in short headers
requirements.statement: Packets with short headers MUST include only the Destination Connection ID and omit the explicit length.

requirements.title: Know the short-header destination CID length
requirements.statement: The length of the Destination Connection ID field MUST be known to endpoints.

requirements.title: Allow load balancers to agree on CID handling
requirements.statement: Endpoints using a load balancer that routes based on connection ID MAY agree with the load balancer on a fixed length for connection IDs or on an encoding scheme.

requirements.title: Echo client CIDs in Version Negotiation
requirements.statement: A Version Negotiation packet MUST echo the connection IDs selected by the client.

requirements.title: Avoid concurrent zero-length-CID connections on the same address tuple
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT use the same IP address and port for multiple concurrent connections with zero-length connection IDs unless it is certain that peer connection migration, NAT rebinding, and client port reuse are not in use.

requirements.title: Associate each CID with a sequence number
requirements.statement: Each connection ID MUST have an associated sequence number to assist in detecting when NEW_CONNECTION_ID or RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames refer to the same value.

requirements.title: Use NEW_CONNECTION_ID for additional CIDs
requirements.statement: Additional connection IDs MUST be communicated to the peer using NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames.

requirements.title: Do not sequence the first client-selected CID or Retry-provided CID
requirements.statement: The connection ID that a client selects for the first Destination Connection ID field it sends and any connection ID provided by a Retry packet MUST NOT be assigned sequence numbers.

requirements.title: Accept packets carrying an issued CID for the connection lifetime
requirements.statement: When an endpoint issues a connection ID, it MUST accept packets that carry this connection ID for the duration of the connection or until its peer invalidates the connection ID via a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.

requirements.title: Treat active CIDs as valid at any time
requirements.statement: Connection IDs that are issued and not retired MUST be considered active and valid for use with the current connection at any time in any packet type.

requirements.title: Consume CIDs in response to migration
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY consume connection IDs in response to a migrating peer.

requirements.title: Maintain a set of peer-issued CIDs
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST maintain a set of connection IDs received from its peer for use when sending packets.

requirements.title: Retire a CID by sending RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID
requirements.statement: When the endpoint wishes to remove a connection ID from use, it MUST send a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame to its peer.

requirements.title: Make RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID a no-reuse request
requirements.statement: Sending a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame MUST indicate that the connection ID will not be used again and request that the peer replace it with a new connection ID using a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.

requirements.title: Prompt peer retirement with an increased Retire Prior To
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY cause its peer to retire connection IDs by sending a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame with an increased Retire Prior To field.

requirements.title: Classify incoming packets on receipt
requirements.statement: Incoming packets MUST be classified on receipt.

requirements.title: Allow existing-connection association or new server connections
requirements.statement: Packets MAY either be associated with an existing connection or, for servers, potentially create a new connection.

requirements.title: Try to associate packets with an existing connection
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST try to associate a packet with an existing connection.

requirements.title: Process packets that match the existing CID
requirements.statement: If the packet has a non-zero-length Destination Connection ID corresponding to an existing connection, QUIC MUST process that packet accordingly.

requirements.title: Allow fragile zero-length-CID matching strategies
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY use just the destination IP and port or both source and destination addresses for identification.

requirements.title: Allow Stateless Reset for unattributed packets
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY send a Stateless Reset for any packets that cannot be attributed to an existing connection.

requirements.title: Discard packets inconsistent with connection state
requirements.statement: Packets that are matched to an existing connection MUST be discarded if the packets are inconsistent with the state of that connection.

requirements.title: Discard packets with a different protocol version
requirements.statement: Packets MUST be discarded if they indicate a different protocol version than that of the connection.

requirements.title: Discard packets if packet protection cannot be removed
requirements.statement: Packets MUST be discarded if removal of packet protection is unsuccessful once the expected keys are available.

requirements.title: Generate a connection error on pre-error processing
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST generate a connection error if it processes the contents of these packets before discovering an error.

requirements.title: Revert changes made while processing weakly protected invalid packets
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST fully revert any changes made during that processing.

requirements.title: Match client packets by client-selected CID
requirements.statement: Valid packets sent to clients MUST always include a Destination Connection ID that matches a value the client selects.

requirements.title: Discard packets that do not match an existing client connection
requirements.statement: Packets that do not match an existing connection based on Destination Connection ID or, if that value is zero length, local IP address and port MUST be discarded.

requirements.title: Allow clients to drop or buffer not-yet-decryptable packets
requirements.statement: A client MAY drop packets encrypted with a key it has not yet computed or buffer them in anticipation of later packets that allow it to compute the key.

requirements.title: Match supported-version packets by connection ID or address tuple
requirements.statement: Packets with a supported version or no Version field MUST be matched to a connection using the connection ID or, for packets with zero-length connection IDs, the local address and port.

requirements.title: Allow out-of-band forwarding for simple load balancers
requirements.statement: Servers MAY use an out-of-band mechanism to forward packets to the correct server based on connection ID.

requirements.title: Allow preferred-address migration for dedicated server addresses
requirements.statement: If servers can use a dedicated server IP address or port other than the one that the client initially connects to, they MAY use the preferred_address transport parameter to request that clients move connections to that dedicated address.

requirements.title: Allow clients to decline preferred addresses
requirements.statement: Clients MAY choose not to use the preferred address.

requirements.title: Allow clients to open connections
requirements.statement: When implementing the client role, an application protocol MAY open a connection, which begins the exchange described in Section 7.

requirements.title: Allow clients to enable Early Data
requirements.statement: When implementing the client role, an application protocol MAY enable Early Data when available.

requirements.title: Allow clients to learn Early Data acceptance
requirements.statement: When implementing the client role, an application protocol MAY be informed when Early Data has been accepted or rejected by a server.

requirements.title: Allow servers to listen for connections
requirements.statement: When implementing the server role, an application protocol MAY listen for incoming connections, which prepares for the exchange described in Section 7.

requirements.title: Allow servers to embed application data in resumption tickets
requirements.statement: If Early Data is supported, an application protocol MAY embed application-controlled data in the TLS resumption ticket sent to the client.

requirements.title: Allow servers to use resumption-ticket data for Early Data decisions
requirements.statement: If Early Data is supported, an application protocol MAY retrieve application-controlled data from the client's resumption ticket and accept or reject Early Data based on that information.

requirements.title: Allow configuring initial stream counts
requirements.statement: In either role, an application protocol MAY configure minimum values for the initial number of permitted streams of each type as communicated in the transport parameters.

requirements.title: Allow receive-buffer control via flow control limits
requirements.statement: In either role, an application protocol MAY control resource allocation for receive buffers by setting flow control limits both for streams and for the connection.

requirements.title: Allow handshake status queries
requirements.statement: In either role, an application protocol MAY identify whether the handshake has completed successfully or is still ongoing.

requirements.title: Allow connection liveness maintenance
requirements.statement: In either role, an application protocol MAY keep a connection from silently closing by either generating PING frames or requesting that the transport send additional frames before the idle timeout expires.

requirements.title: Allow immediate connection close
requirements.statement: In either role, an application protocol MAY immediately close the connection.

requirements.title: Clients that support multiple QUIC versions SHOULD ensure that the first UDP datagram they send is sized to the largest of the minimum datagram sizes from all versions they support, using PADDING frames (Section 19
requirements.statement: Clients that support multiple QUIC versions SHOULD ensure that the first UDP datagram they send is sized to the largest of the minimum datagram sizes from all versions they support, using PADDING frames (Section 19.1) as necessary.

requirements.title: Reject unsupported Version Negotiation attempts
requirements.statement: A client that supports only this version of QUIC MUST abandon the current connection attempt if it receives a Version Negotiation packet unless it has received and successfully processed any other packet or the Version Negotiation packet lists the QUIC version selected by the client.

requirements.title: Provide the following properties:
requirements.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST provide the following properties:

requirements.title: Provide authenticated key exchange
requirements.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST provide authenticated key exchange.

requirements.title: Always authenticate the server
requirements.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST always authenticate the server.

requirements.title: Allow optional client authentication
requirements.statement: The cryptographic handshake MAY optionally authenticate the client.

requirements.title: Produce distinct keys per connection
requirements.statement: Every connection MUST produce distinct and unrelated keys.

requirements.title: Use handshake keys for 0-RTT and 1-RTT protection
requirements.statement: Keying material from the cryptographic handshake MUST be usable for packet protection for both 0-RTT and 1-RTT packets.

requirements.title: Authenticate transport parameter exchange
requirements.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST provide authenticated exchange of transport parameter values for both endpoints.

requirements.title: Protect server transport parameters
requirements.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST provide confidentiality protection for server transport parameters.

requirements.title: Authenticate application protocol negotiation
requirements.statement: The cryptographic handshake MUST provide authenticated negotiation of an application protocol.

requirements.title: Use an unpredictable client Destination Connection ID
requirements.statement: When a client sends its first Initial packet without having previously received an Initial or Retry packet from the server, it MUST populate the Destination Connection ID field with an unpredictable value.

requirements.title: Authenticate connection ID choices through transport parameters
requirements.statement: The choice each endpoint makes about connection IDs during the handshake MUST be authenticated by including all values in transport parameters.

requirements.title: Treat the following as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR or PROTOCOL_VIOLATION:
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST treat the following as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR or PROTOCOL_VIOLATION:

requirements.title: Do not use updated transport-parameter values in 0-RTT
requirements.statement: When sending frames in 0-RTT packets, a client MUST NOT use updated values it learns from the server's updated transport parameters or from frames received in 1-RTT packets.

requirements.title: Allow 0-RTT only with remembered transport parameters
requirements.statement: Updated values of transport parameters from the handshake MUST apply only to 1-RTT packets.

requirements.title: Once the handshake completes, if an endpoint is unable to buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame, it MAY discard that CRYPTO frame and all CRYPTO frames received in the future, or it MAY close the connection with a CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code
requirements.statement: Once the handshake completes, if an endpoint is unable to buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame, it MAY discard that CRYPTO frame and all future CRYPTO frames or close the connection with a CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code.

requirements.title: Specifically, the client MUST send an Initial packet in a UDP datagram that contains at least 1200 bytes if it does not have Handshake keys, and otherwise send a Handshake packet
requirements.statement: Specifically, the client MUST send an Initial packet in a UDP datagram that contains at least 1200 bytes if it does not have Handshake keys, and otherwise send a Handshake packet.

requirements.title: This token MUST be repeated by the client in all Initial packets it sends for that connection after it receives the Retry packet
requirements.statement: This token MUST be repeated by the client in all Initial packets it sends for that connection after it receives the Retry packet.

requirements.title: Instead, the server SHOULD immediately close (Section 10
requirements.statement: Instead, the server SHOULD immediately close (Section 10.2) the connection with an INVALID_TOKEN error.

requirements.title: Validate Retry token returns
requirements.statement: The Retry token MUST be repeated by the client in all Initial packets it sends for that connection after it receives the Retry packet.

requirements.title: Close on invalid Retry tokens
requirements.statement: If a server receives a client Initial that contains an invalid Retry token but is otherwise valid, it SHOULD immediately close the connection with an INVALID_TOKEN error.

requirements.title: In comparison, a token obtained in a Retry packet MUST be used immediately during the connection attempt and cannot be used in subsequent connection attempts
requirements.statement: In comparison, a token obtained in a Retry packet MUST be used immediately during the connection attempt and cannot be used in subsequent connection attempts.

requirements.title: Clients MAY use tokens obtained on one connection for any connection attempt using the same version
requirements.statement: Clients MAY use tokens obtained on one connection for any connection attempt using the same version.

requirements.title: If the client IP address has changed, the server MUST adhere to the anti-amplification limit
requirements.statement: If the client IP address has changed, the server MUST adhere to the anti-amplification limit; see Section 8.

requirements.title: To protect against such attacks, servers MUST ensure that replay of tokens is prevented or limited
requirements.statement: To protect against such attacks, servers MUST ensure that replay of tokens is prevented or limited.

requirements.title: Tokens that are provided in NEW_TOKEN frames (Section 19
requirements.statement: Tokens that are provided in NEW_TOKEN frames (Section 19.7) need to be valid for longer but SHOULD NOT be accepted multiple times.

requirements.title: Servers are encouraged to allow tokens to be used only once, if possible
requirements.statement: Servers are encouraged to allow tokens to be used only once, if possible; tokens MAY include additional information about clients to further narrow applicability or reuse.

requirements.title: Make address-validation tokens hard to guess and integrity protected
requirements.statement: An address validation token MUST be difficult to guess and, for token-based schemes, covered by integrity protection against modification or falsification by clients.

requirements.title: Protect against token replay
requirements.statement: To protect against replay attacks, servers MUST ensure that replay of tokens is prevented or limited.

requirements.title: Use PATH_CHALLENGE to validate a path
requirements.statement: To initiate path validation, an endpoint MUST send a PATH_CHALLENGE frame containing an unpredictable payload on the path to be validated.

requirements.title: Send more than one PATH_RESPONSE frame in response to one PATH_CHALLENGE frame
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send more than one PATH_RESPONSE frame in response to one PATH_CHALLENGE frame; see Section 13.3.

requirements.title: That has no valid network path to its peer MAY signal this using the NO_VIABLE_PATH connection error, noting that this is only possible if the network path exists but does not support the required MTU (Section 14)
requirements.statement: An endpoint that has no valid network path to its peer MAY signal this using the NO_VIABLE_PATH connection error, noting that this is only possible if the network path exists but does not support the required MTU (Section 14).

requirements.title: Signal no viable path when appropriate
requirements.statement: An endpoint that has no valid network path to its peer MAY signal this using the NO_VIABLE_PATH connection error.

requirements.title: If the peer sent the disable_active_migration transport parameter, an endpoint also MUST NOT send packets (including probing packets
requirements.statement: If the peer sent the disable_active_migration transport parameter, an endpoint also MUST NOT send packets (including probing packets; see Section 9.1) from a different local address to the address the peer used during the handshake, unless the endpoint has acted on a preferred_address transport parameter from the peer.

requirements.title: Forbid migration before handshake confirmation
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT initiate connection migration before the handshake is confirmed.

requirements.title: Respect Disable Active Migration
requirements.statement: If the peer sent the disable_active_migration transport parameter, an endpoint MUST NOT send packets from a different local address to the address the peer used during the handshake unless the endpoint has acted on a preferred_address transport parameter from the peer.

requirements.title: Validate Peer Address Changes
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST perform path validation if it detects any change to a peer's address unless it has previously validated that address.

requirements.title: Discard Packets from Unknown Server Addresses
requirements.statement: If a client receives packets from an unknown server address, the client MUST discard those packets.

requirements.title: Probe for peer reachability from a new local address using path validation (Section 8
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY probe for peer reachability from a new local address using path validation (Section 8.2) prior to migrating the connection to the new local address.

requirements.title: Probe New Local Addresses Before Migration
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY probe for peer reachability from a new local address using path validation before migrating the connection to the new local address.

requirements.title: Reset Congestion State on Migration
requirements.statement: When migrating, an endpoint MUST immediately reset its congestion controller and round-trip time estimator for the new path to initial values unless the only change in the peer's address is its port number.

requirements.title: Retain State for Port-Only Changes
requirements.statement: When the only change in the peer's address is its port number, an endpoint MAY retain its congestion control state and round-trip estimate instead of reverting to initial values.

requirements.title: If the recipient permits the migration, it MUST send subsequent packets to the new peer address and MUST initiate path validation (Section 8
requirements.statement: If the recipient permits the migration, it MUST send subsequent packets to the new peer address and initiate path validation (Section 8.2) to verify the peer's ownership of the address if validation is not already underway.

requirements.title: Protect unvalidated peer-address traffic
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST protect against potential attacks as described in Sections 9.3.1 and 9.3.2 when it sends data to an unvalidated peer address.

requirements.title: Initiate Path Validation After Permitting Migration
requirements.statement: If the recipient permits the migration, it MUST initiate path validation to verify the peer's ownership of the address if validation is not already underway.

requirements.title: Protect Against Address-Spoofing Attacks
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST protect against potential attacks as described in Sections 9.3.1 and 9.3.2.

requirements.title: Allow Abandoning Other Path Validation
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY abandon any path validation for other addresses after changing the address to which it sends non-probing packets.

requirements.title: To protect the connection from failing due to such a spurious migration, an endpoint MUST revert to using the last validated peer address when validation of a new peer address fails
requirements.statement: To protect the connection from failing due to such a spurious migration, an endpoint MUST revert to using the last validated peer address when validation of a new peer address fails.

requirements.title: For instance, an endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to any further incoming packets
requirements.statement: For instance, an endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to any further incoming packets.

requirements.title: Revert to the Last Validated Peer Address
requirements.statement: When validation of a new peer address fails, an endpoint MUST revert to using the last validated peer address.

requirements.title: Allow Stateless Reset After Silent Close
requirements.statement: After discarding all connection state, an endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to any further incoming packets.

requirements.title: Use Heuristics for Attack Detection
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY use heuristics to improve detection of this style of attack.

requirements.title: Retain congestion state for port-only changes
requirements.statement: Because port-only changes are commonly the result of NAT rebinding or other middlebox activity, the endpoint MAY instead retain its congestion control state and round-trip estimate in those cases instead of reverting to initial values.

requirements.title: Keep ACK coverage across multiple paths
requirements.statement: A receiver of packets on multiple paths MUST still send ACK frames covering all received packets.

requirements.title: Retain State for Port-Only Peer Changes
requirements.statement: When the only change in the peer's address is its port number, an endpoint MAY retain its congestion control state and round-trip estimate instead of reverting to initial values.

requirements.title: Due to network changes outside the control of its peer, an endpoint might receive packets from a new source address with the same Destination Connection ID field value, in which case it MAY continue to use the current connection ID with the new remote address while still sending from the same local address
requirements.statement: Due to network changes outside the control of its peer, an endpoint might receive packets from a new source address with the same Destination Connection ID field value, in which case it MAY continue to use the current connection ID with the new remote address while still sending from the same local address.

requirements.title: Limit use of the zero-length connection ID for migration
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD NOT initiate migration with a peer that has requested a zero-length connection ID, because traffic over the new path might be trivially linkable to traffic over the old one.

requirements.title: Keep address changes infrequent
requirements.statement: Changing address can cause a peer to reset its congestion control state, so addresses SHOULD only be changed infrequently.

requirements.title: Provide new connection IDs before peers migrate
requirements.statement: To ensure that migration is possible and packets sent on different paths cannot be correlated, endpoints SHOULD provide new connection IDs before peers migrate.

requirements.title: Allow Reuse with the Same Local Address
requirements.statement: If an endpoint receives packets from a new source address with the same Destination Connection ID field value, it MAY continue to use the current connection ID with the new remote address while still sending from the same local address.

requirements.title: If a client receives packets from a new server address when the client has not initiated a migration to that address, the client SHOULD discard these packets
requirements.statement: If a client receives packets from a new server address when the client has not initiated a migration to that address, the client SHOULD discard these packets.

requirements.title: Discard Unexpected Server-Address Packets
requirements.statement: If a client receives packets from a new server address when it has not initiated a migration to that address, the client SHOULD discard those packets.

requirements.title: Servers MAY communicate a preferred address of each address family (IPv4 and IPv6) to allow clients to pick the one most suited to their network attachment
requirements.statement: Servers MAY communicate a preferred address of each address family (IPv4 and IPv6) to allow clients to pick the one most suited to their network attachment.

requirements.title: Once the handshake is confirmed, the client SHOULD select one of the two addresses provided by the server and initiate path validation (see Section 8
requirements.statement: Once the handshake is confirmed, the client SHOULD select one of the two addresses provided by the server and initiate path validation (see Section 8.2).

requirements.title: Begin sending packets to the new server address after successful validation
requirements.statement: As soon as path validation succeeds, the client SHOULD begin sending all future packets to the new server address using the new connection ID.

requirements.title: Discontinue use of the old server address after successful validation
requirements.statement: As soon as path validation succeeds, the client SHOULD discontinue use of the old server address.

requirements.title: Convey a Preferred Address in the TLS Handshake
requirements.statement: A server MUST convey a preferred address by including the preferred_address transport parameter in the TLS handshake.

requirements.title: Allow Per-Family Preferred Addresses
requirements.statement: Servers MAY communicate a preferred address of each address family to allow clients to pick the one most suited to their network attachment.

requirements.title: Use an Unused Active Connection ID for Preferred-Address Migration
requirements.statement: A client MUST construct packets using any previously unused active connection ID, taken from either the preferred_address transport parameter or a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.

requirements.title: Move Future Packets to the New Server Address After Validation
requirements.statement: As soon as path validation succeeds, the client SHOULD begin sending all future packets to the new server address using the new connection ID and discontinue use of the old server address.

requirements.title: That migrates to a preferred address MUST validate the address it chooses before migrating
requirements.statement: A client that migrates to a preferred address MUST validate the address it chooses before migrating; see Section 21.5.3.

requirements.title: Do not use preferred-address values for other connections
requirements.statement: The addresses that a server provides in the preferred_address transport parameter MUST be treated as valid only for the connection in which they are provided.

requirements.title: Use these for other connections, including connections that are resumed from the current connection
requirements.statement: A client MUST NOT use these for other connections, including connections that are resumed from the current connection.

requirements.title: Respond to PATH_CHALLENGE with PATH_RESPONSE
requirements.statement: If the received packet contains a PATH_CHALLENGE frame, the server MUST send a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame as described in Section 8.2.

requirements.title: Restrict Preferred-Address Values to the Current Connection
requirements.statement: A client MUST NOT use the addresses provided in the preferred_address transport parameter for other connections, including connections that are resumed from the current connection.

requirements.title: Servers SHOULD initiate path validation to the client's new address upon receiving a probe packet from a different address
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD initiate path validation to the client's new address upon receiving a probe packet from a different address; see Section 8.

requirements.title: Keep preferred-address connection IDs path-agnostic
requirements.statement: The connection ID provided in the `preferred_address` transport parameter MAY be used independently of the addresses that are provided.

requirements.title: Use the preferred-address connection ID on any path
requirements.statement: The connection ID is provided to ensure that the client has a connection ID available for migration, but the client MAY use this connection ID on any path.

requirements.title: Protect Preferred-Address Traffic from Attacks
requirements.statement: If packets received at the server's preferred address have a different source address than was observed from the client during the handshake, the server MUST protect against potential attacks as described in Sections 9.3.1 and 9.3.2.

requirements.title: That send data using IPv6 SHOULD apply an IPv6 flow label in compliance with [RFC6437], unless the local API does not allow setting IPv6 flow labels
requirements.statement: Endpoints that send data using IPv6 SHOULD apply an IPv6 flow label in compliance with [RFC6437], unless the local API does not allow setting IPv6 flow labels.
