requirements.statement: The :protocol pseudo-header field SHALL be "connect-ip".

requirements.title: Authority pseudo-header contains proxy authority
requirements.statement: The :authority pseudo-header field SHALL contain the authority of the IP proxy.

requirements.title: Path pseudo-header is not empty
requirements.statement: The :path pseudo-header field SHALL NOT be empty.

requirements.title: Scheme pseudo-header is not empty
requirements.statement: The :scheme pseudo-header field SHALL NOT be empty.

requirements.title: URI Template values contain scheme and path
requirements.statement: The values MUST contain the scheme and path from the URI Template after the URI Template expansion process has been completed.

requirements.title: Nonconforming IP proxying request is malformed
requirements.statement: An IP proxying request that does not conform to these restrictions MUST be treated as malformed.

requirements.title: Response status code is 2xx
requirements.statement: The HTTP status code on the response MUST be in the 2xx (Successful) range.

requirements.title: Failed proxying attempts are aborted
requirements.statement: If any of these requirements are not met, the client MUST treat this proxying attempt as failed and abort the request.

requirements.title: IP prefix targets support only one IP version
requirements.statement: If `target` is an IP prefix, the request MUST use only a single IP version.

requirements.title: IP proxy sends scoped route advertisement
requirements.statement: The IP proxy SHOULD send a ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule that includes routes for all addresses that were resolved for the requested hostname, that are accessible to the IP proxy, and belong to an address family for which the IP proxy also sends an Assigned Address.

requirements.title: Scope proxying to a specific IP protocol
requirements.statement: If present, `ipproto` MUST specify a specific IP protocol for this request.

requirements.title: Wildcard or absent ipproto means any protocol
requirements.statement: If the value is `*` or the variable is omitted, the client MUST request any IP protocol.

requirements.title: Define ipproto as allowable next-header value
requirements.statement: The `ipproto` variable MUST indicate an allowable next-header value carried in the outermost IP headers of HTTP Datagrams.

requirements.title: Always allow ICMP traffic
requirements.statement: ICMP traffic MUST always be allowed, regardless of the `ipproto` value.

requirements.title: Conform target and ipproto to Figure 6 format
requirements.statement: Using the terms IPv6address, IPv4address, and reg-name from [URI], the `target` and `ipproto` variables MUST conform to the Figure 6 format using [ABNF] notation.

requirements.title: Percent-encode colons in IPv6 targets
requirements.statement: If `target` contains an IPv6 literal or prefix, its colons (":") MUST be percent-encoded.

requirements.title: Precede target prefix lengths with %2F
requirements.statement: If present, the IP prefix length in `target` SHALL be preceded by a percent-encoded slash ("/"): "%2F".

requirements.title: Constrain target prefix length to address bits
requirements.statement: The IP prefix length MUST represent a decimal integer between 0 and the length of the IP address in bits, inclusive.

requirements.title: Zero uncovered lower bits in scoped targets
requirements.statement: If `target` contains an IP prefix and the prefix length is strictly less than the length of the IP address in bits, the lower bits of the IP address that are not covered by the prefix length MUST all be set to 0.

requirements.title: Constrain ipproto to decimal 0-255 or wildcard
requirements.statement: `ipproto` MUST represent a decimal integer between 0 and 255 inclusive or the wildcard value `*`.

requirements.title: Define ipproto grammar alternatives
requirements.statement: The `ipproto` grammar MUST be `1*3DIGIT / "*"`.

requirements.title: Define target grammar alternatives
requirements.statement: The `target` grammar MUST be `IPv6prefix / IPv4prefix / reg-name / "*"`.

requirements.title: Optionally perform access control using client scope
requirements.statement: IP proxies MAY perform access control using the scoping information provided by the client, and if the client is not authorized to access any of the destinations included in the scope, the proxy can immediately reject the request.

requirements.title: Contain the full assigned prefix list
requirements.statement: The ADDRESS_ASSIGN Capsule MUST contain the full list of IP prefixes currently assigned to the receiver.

requirements.title: Define ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule wire format
requirements.statement: The ADDRESS_ASSIGN Capsule MUST have Type 0x01, Length, and Assigned Address fields in that order.

requirements.title: Contain zero or more Assigned Addresses
requirements.statement: The ADDRESS_ASSIGN Capsule MUST contain a sequence of zero or more Assigned Addresses.

requirements.title: Define Assigned Address field layout and widths
requirements.statement: The Assigned Address structure MUST contain Request ID, IP Version (8 bits), IP Address (32 to 128 bits), and IP Prefix Length (8 bits) fields in that order.

requirements.title: Encode Request ID as variable-length integer
requirements.statement: Request ID MUST be encoded as a variable-length integer.

requirements.title: Set Request ID from Address Request context
requirements.statement: Request ID MUST contain the corresponding request field value when this address assignment is in response to an Address Request, and be zero otherwise.

requirements.title: IP Version field encoding
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: IP Version field meaning
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST identify the IP version of this address assignment.

requirements.title: Restrict IP Version to 4 or 6
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST be either 4 or 6.

requirements.title: Set IP Address length by IP Version
requirements.statement: The IP Address field MUST be 32 bits when the IP Version field has value 4 and 128 bits when it has value 6.

requirements.title: IP Prefix Length field encoding
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: IP Prefix Length field meaning
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST be the number of bits in the IP address used to define the prefix being assigned.

requirements.title: IP Prefix Length upper bound
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST be less than or equal to the length of the IP Address field in bits.

requirements.title: Single-source-address permission at full-length prefix
requirements.statement: If the prefix length is equal to the length of the IP address, the receiver of this capsule MAY send packets from a single source address.

requirements.title: Prefix-scoped source-address permission
requirements.statement: If the prefix length is less than the length of the IP address, the receiver of this capsule MAY send packets from any source address that falls within the prefix.

requirements.title: Zero unused IP Address bits
requirements.statement: If the prefix length is strictly less than the length of the IP address in bits, the lower bits of the IP Address field that are not covered by the prefix length MUST all be set to 0.

requirements.title: Malformed capsule field handling
requirements.statement: If any of the capsule fields are malformed upon reception, the receiver of the capsule MUST follow the error-handling procedure defined in Section 3.3 of [HTTP-DGRAM].

requirements.title: Omitted address indicates removal
requirements.statement: If an ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule does not contain an address that was previously transmitted in another ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule, the receiver of the capsule MUST treat that address as removed.

requirements.title: Empty ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule removes all addresses
requirements.statement: If an ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule is empty, the receiver of the capsule MUST treat all addresses as removed.

requirements.title: ADDRESS_REQUEST from an address-assignment expectation
requirements.statement: An endpoint that is expecting an address assignment MUST send an ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule, unless it does not need any address assignment.

requirements.title: Unprompted ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsules
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY send ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsules unprompted.

requirements.title: ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule length field
requirements.statement: The Length field MUST follow the Type field and be encoded as a variable-length integer.

requirements.title: ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule type
requirements.statement: The ADDRESS_REQUEST Capsule Type field MUST be 0x02 and appear first.

requirements.title: ADDRESS_REQUEST requested address field
requirements.statement: The Requested Address field MUST follow the Length field.

requirements.title: ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule contains one or more Requested Addresses
requirements.statement: The ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule MUST contain one or more Requested Address entries.

requirements.title: Requested Address IP Address field
requirements.statement: The IP Address field MUST appear third and be encoded as 32 to 128 bits.

requirements.title: Requested Address IP Prefix Length field
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST appear fourth and be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: Requested Address IP Version field
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST appear second and be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: Requested Address request ID field
requirements.statement: The Request ID field MUST appear first and be encoded as a variable-length integer.

requirements.title: Encode Request ID as a variable-length integer
requirements.statement: The Request ID field MUST be encoded as a variable-length integer.

requirements.title: Request ID reuse prohibition
requirements.statement: Request IDs MUST NOT be reused by an endpoint.

requirements.title: Request ID zero prohibition
requirements.statement: Request IDs MUST NOT be zero.

requirements.title: Use 32-bit IP addresses for IPv4
requirements.statement: If the IP Version field has value 4, the IP Address field SHALL have a length of 32 bits.

requirements.title: Use 128-bit IP addresses for IPv6
requirements.statement: If the IP Version field has value 6, the IP Address field SHALL have a length of 128 bits.

requirements.title: Encode IP Prefix Length as an 8-bit integer
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: Bound prefix length by address length
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST be less than or equal to the length of the IP Address field in bits.

requirements.title: Zero unused address bits beyond the prefix
requirements.statement: If the prefix length is strictly less than the length of the IP address in bits, the lower bits of the IP Address field that are not covered by the prefix length MUST all be set to 0.

requirements.title: Handle malformed capsule fields
requirements.statement: If any of the capsule fields are malformed upon reception, the receiver of the capsule MUST follow the error-handling procedure defined in Section 3.3 of [HTTP-DGRAM].

requirements.title: Assign addresses and send address assignment
requirements.statement: Upon receiving the ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule, an endpoint SHOULD assign one or more IP addresses to its peer and then respond with an ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule to inform the peer of the assignment.

requirements.title: Match request IDs in assigned addresses
requirements.statement: For each Requested Address, the receiver of the ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule SHALL respond with an Assigned Address with a matching Request ID.

requirements.title: Set assigned values in assigned address responses
requirements.statement: If the requested address was assigned, the IP Address and IP Prefix Length fields in the Assigned Address response SHALL be set to the assigned values.

requirements.title: Encode unassigned addresses with zero values
requirements.statement: If the requested address was not assigned, the IP address and IP Prefix Length in the Assigned Address response SHALL be set to all-zero and the maximum length (0.0.0.0/32 or ::/128), respectively, to indicate that no address was assigned.

requirements.title: Keep address rejections out of later assignments
requirements.statement: These address rejections SHOULD NOT be included in subsequent ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsules.

requirements.title: Reject empty address request capsules
requirements.statement: If an endpoint receives an ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule that contains zero Requested Addresses, it MUST abort the IP proxying request stream.

requirements.title: Route advertisement capsule format
requirements.statement: A ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT Capsule MUST have Type 0x03, a Length field, and zero or more IP Address Range entries in that order.

requirements.title: IP address range layout
requirements.statement: An IP Address Range MUST contain IP Version (8), Start IP Address (32..128), End IP Address (32..128), and IP Protocol (8) fields in that order.

requirements.title: IP Version field encoding
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: IP Version value constraint
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST be either 4 or 6.

requirements.title: IPv4 field length
requirements.statement: When the IP Version field has value 4, the Start IP Address and End IP Address fields MUST have a length of 32 bits.

requirements.title: IPv6 field length
requirements.statement: When the IP Version field has value 6, the Start IP Address and End IP Address fields MUST have a length of 128 bits.

requirements.title: Start address ordering
requirements.statement: The Start IP Address MUST be less than or equal to the End IP Address.

requirements.title: Malformed capsule error handling
requirements.statement: If any of the capsule fields are malformed upon reception, the receiver of the capsule MUST follow the error-handling procedure defined in Section 3.3 of [HTTP-DGRAM].

requirements.title: Order routes by IP Version
requirements.statement: The IP Version of A MUST be less than or equal to the IP Version of B.

requirements.title: Order routes by IP Protocol when versions match
requirements.statement: If the IP Version of A and B are equal, the IP Protocol of A MUST be less than or equal to the IP Protocol of B.

requirements.title: Order route ranges by end and start addresses
requirements.statement: If the IP Version and IP Protocol of A and B are both equal, the End IP Address of A MUST be strictly less than the Start IP Address of B.

requirements.title: Abort invalid ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsules
requirements.statement: If an endpoint receives a ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule that does not meet these requirements, it MUST abort the IP proxying request stream.

requirements.title: Do not send overlapping ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT routes
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST NOT send a ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule with routes that overlap in such a way.

requirements.title: Abort on detected route violations
requirements.statement: If an endpoint detects the violation, it MUST abort the IP proxying request stream.

requirements.title: Optionally validate ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT routes
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY validate whether a ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule meets these requirements.

requirements.title: Start HTTP Datagrams with a Context ID field
requirements.statement: HTTP Datagrams associated with IP proxying request streams MUST start with a Context ID field.

requirements.title: Allow any Context ID allocation order
requirements.statement: Context IDs MAY be allocated in any order.

requirements.title: Allow either endpoint to use an allocated Context ID
requirements.statement: Once a Context ID has been allocated, it MAY be used by either the client or the IP proxy, regardless of which endpoint initially allocated it.

requirements.title: Place Context ID after Quarter Stream ID
requirements.statement: When HTTP Datagrams are encoded using QUIC DATAGRAM frames, the Context ID field MUST directly follow the Quarter Stream ID field at the start of the QUIC DATAGRAM frame payload.

requirements.title: Define the IP Proxying HTTP Datagram Payload layout
requirements.statement: The IP Proxying HTTP Datagram Payload MUST consist of a Context ID field followed by a Payload field.

requirements.title: Encode Context ID as a variable-length integer
requirements.statement: The Context ID field MUST be a variable-length integer that contains the value of the Context ID.

requirements.title: Handle unknown Context ID datagrams by dropping or buffering
requirements.statement: If an HTTP/3 datagram carries an unknown Context ID, the receiver SHALL either drop that datagram silently or buffer it temporarily, on the order of a round trip, while awaiting registration of the corresponding Context ID.

requirements.title: Make Payload semantics depend on Context ID
requirements.statement: The semantics of the Payload field MUST depend on the value of the Context ID field.

requirements.title: Allow an empty Payload field
requirements.statement: The Payload field MAY be empty.

requirements.title: Encode IP packets with Context ID zero
requirements.statement: IP packets MUST be encoded using HTTP Datagrams with the Context ID set to zero.

requirements.title: Carry a full IP packet when Context ID is zero
requirements.statement: When the Context ID is set to zero, the Payload field MUST contain a full IP packet from the IP Version field until the last byte of the IP payload.

requirements.title: Process received IP packets from HTTP Datagrams
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives an HTTP Datagram containing an IP packet MUST parse the IP header, perform local policy checks, consult its routing table to select an outbound interface, and then send the packet on that interface or pass it to a local application.

requirements.title: Allow additional filtering policies
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints MAY implement additional filtering policies on the IP packets they forward.

requirements.title: Treat failed checks as forwarding errors
requirements.statement: A received IP packet that fails any correctness or policy checks MUST be treated as a forwarding error, not a protocol violation, for IP proxying.

requirements.title: Check routes before sending IP packets over HTTP Datagrams
requirements.statement: When an endpoint receives an IP packet, it MUST check whether it matches routes mapped for an IP tunnel and perform the same forwarding checks as above before transmitting it over HTTP Datagrams.

requirements.title: Decrement Hop Count on encapsulation
requirements.statement: When IP proxying endpoints forward IP packets between different links, they MUST decrement the IP Hop Count (or TTL) upon encapsulation.

requirements.title: Do not decrement Hop Count on decapsulation
requirements.statement: When IP proxying endpoints forward IP packets between different links, they MUST not decrement the IP Hop Count (or TTL) upon decapsulation.

requirements.title: Decrement Hop Count before transmission
requirements.statement: The Hop Count of an IP packet MUST be decremented right before the packet is transmitted in an HTTP Datagram.

requirements.title: Exclude self-generated packets from hop-count decrement
requirements.statement: The IP Hop Count (or TTL) decrement upon encapsulation MUST not apply to IP packets generated by the IP proxying endpoint itself.

requirements.title: Abort request stream when QUIC MTU is too low
requirements.statement: If an endpoint is using QUIC DATAGRAM frames to convey IPv6 packets and it detects that the QUIC MTU is too low to allow sending 1280 bytes, it MUST abort the IP proxying request stream.

requirements.title: Send Destination Unreachable for invalid source addresses
requirements.statement: For invalid source addresses, an endpoint SHOULD send Destination Unreachable with ICMPv6 code 5.

requirements.title: Send Destination Unreachable for unroutable destination addresses
requirements.statement: For unroutable destination addresses, an endpoint SHOULD send Destination Unreachable with ICMPv6 code 0 or 1.

requirements.title: Send Packet Too Big for MTU-exceeding packets
requirements.statement: For packets that cannot fit within the outgoing-link MTU, an endpoint MUST send Packet Too Big.

requirements.title: Process proxied ICMP packets when ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT is absent
requirements.statement: If an endpoint does not send ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsules, it SHOULD process proxied ICMP packets from its peer.

requirements.title: Decrement hop count or TTL when encapsulating forwarded packets
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints MUST decrement the IP Hop Count (or TTL) when encapsulating forwarded packets.

requirements.title: Prefer HTTP/3 for IP proxying
requirements.statement: IP proxying SHOULD be performed over HTTP/3 to allow leveraging the QUIC DATAGRAM frame.

requirements.title: Send Packet Too Big feedback
requirements.statement: When an IP packet will not fit inside a QUIC DATAGRAM frame, the endpoint SHOULD send an ICMP Packet Too Big message to the sender of the dropped packet.

requirements.title: Suppress ECN signaling when congestion control is disabled
requirements.statement: If an IP proxying endpoint with an IP proxying request stream disables congestion control, it MUST NOT signal Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) support on the outer connection.

requirements.title: Mark Not-ECT outside congestion control
requirements.statement: The QUIC sender MUST mark all IP headers for QUIC packets outside congestion control with the Not ECN-Capable Transport (Not-ECT) codepoint.

requirements.title: Avoid non-equivalent DSCP markings under outer congestion control
requirements.statement: If tunneled packets are subject to congestion control by the outer connection, they MUST NOT carry DSCP markings that are not equivalent in forwarding behavior.

requirements.title: Do not copy inner DSCP values to the outer header
requirements.statement: If tunneled packets are subject to congestion control by the outer connection, the IP proxying endpoint MUST NOT copy the DSCP field from the inner IP header to the outer IP header.

requirements.title: Optionally forward ICMP packets to clients
requirements.statement: If the proxy receives an ICMP packet destined for that external IP address, it MAY forward it to the clients.

requirements.title: Filter ICMP forwarding by invoking packet scope
requirements.statement: Proxies that forward ICMP on shared external IP addresses MUST forward each ICMP packet only to the client whose scoping matches the invoking packet.

requirements.title: Prohibit opportunistic sending of IP packets in HTTP/1.x
requirements.statement: Opportunistic sending of IP packets MUST NOT be used in HTTP/1.x.

requirements.title: Delay capsules until a successful IP proxying response
requirements.statement: An intermediary that re-encodes a request from HTTP/2 or 3 to HTTP/1.1 MUST NOT forward any received capsules until it has parsed a successful IP proxying response.

requirements.title: Require Expert Review registration policy
requirements.statement: The MASQUE URI Suffixes registry MUST use the Expert Review registration policy.

requirements.title: Constrain registry path segments to token characters
requirements.statement: Registry Path Segment values MUST be ASCII strings containing only token characters.

requirements.title: Require distinct registry path segments
requirements.statement: Entries in this registry MUST have distinct Path Segment values.

requirements.title: Guide expert approval for MASQUE URI suffix requests
requirements.statement: Designated experts SHOULD approve requests when the requested Path Segment will not conflict with existing or expected future IETF work and the use case is relevant to proxying.

requirements.title: Application protocols provide idle-timeout guidance
requirements.statement: Application protocols that use QUIC SHOULD provide guidance on when deferring an idle timeout is appropriate.

requirements.title: Silently close on idle timeout
requirements.statement: If a max_idle_timeout is specified by either endpoint in its transport parameters, the connection MUST be silently closed and its state discarded when it remains idle for longer than the minimum of the max_idle_timeout values advertised by both endpoints.

requirements.title: Commit to immediate close before timeout
requirements.statement: An endpoint that announces a max_idle_timeout MUST initiate an immediate close if it abandons the connection before the effective timeout expires.

requirements.title: Restart idle timer on received packets
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST restart its idle timer when a packet from its peer is received and processed successfully.

requirements.title: Restart idle timer on fresh ack-eliciting send
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST also restart its idle timer when it sends an ack-eliciting packet if no other ack-eliciting packets have been sent since it last received and processed a packet.

requirements.title: Retain only closing-state essentials
requirements.statement: In the closing state, an endpoint MUST retain only enough information to generate a packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame and to identify packets as belonging to the connection.

requirements.title: Send CONNECTION_CLOSE in response to attributed packets while closing
requirements.statement: An endpoint in the closing state MUST send a packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in response to any incoming packet that it attributes to the connection.

requirements.title: Limit packet generation rate in closing state
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD limit the rate at which it generates packets in the closing state.

requirements.title: An endpoint's selected connection ID and the QUIC version are sufficient information to identify packets for a closing connection
requirements.statement: An endpoint's selected connection ID and the QUIC version are sufficient information to identify packets for a closing connection; the endpoint MAY discard all other connection state.

requirements.title: Retain keys to process CONNECTION_CLOSE
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY retain packet protection keys for incoming packets to allow it to read and process a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.

requirements.title: Drop keys and reply with CONNECTION_CLOSE
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY drop packet protection keys when entering the closing state and send a packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in response to any UDP datagram that is received.

requirements.title: To avoid being used for an amplification attack, such endpoints MUST limit the cumulative size of packets it sends to three times the cumulative size of the packets that are received and attributed to the connection
requirements.statement: To avoid being used for an amplification attack, such endpoints MUST limit the cumulative size of packets it sends to three times the cumulative size of the packets that are received and attributed to the connection.

requirements.title: To minimize the state that an endpoint maintains for a closing connection, endpoints MAY send the exact same packet in response to any received packet
requirements.statement: To minimize the state that an endpoint maintains for a closing connection, endpoints MAY send the exact same packet in response to any received packet.

requirements.title: Limit packets sent to unvalidated addresses
requirements.statement: An endpoint in the closing state MUST either discard packets received from an unvalidated address or limit the cumulative size of packets it sends to an unvalidated address to three times the size of packets it receives from that address.

requirements.title: That receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY send a single packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame before entering the draining state, using a NO_ERROR code if appropriate
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY send a single packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame before entering the draining state, using a NO_ERROR code if appropriate.

requirements.title: Send further packets
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send further packets.

requirements.title: Enter the draining state from the closing state if it receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, which indicates that the peer is also closing or draining
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY enter the draining state from the closing state if it receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, which indicates that the peer is also closing or draining.

requirements.title: Replace 0x1d CONNECTION_CLOSE in handshake packets
requirements.statement: A CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1d MUST be replaced by a CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1c when sending the frame in Initial or Handshake packets.

requirements.title: Enter closing state after sending CONNECTION_CLOSE
requirements.statement: After sending a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, an endpoint MUST immediately enter the closing state.

requirements.title: Enter draining state after receiving close
requirements.statement: After receiving a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, endpoints MUST enter the draining state.

requirements.title: Close immediately on protocol violation
requirements.statement: Violations of the protocol MUST lead to an immediate close.

requirements.title: These states SHOULD persist for at least three times the current PTO interval as defined in [QUIC-RECOVERY]
requirements.statement: These states SHOULD persist for at least three times the current PTO interval as defined in [QUIC-RECOVERY].

requirements.title: That have some alternative means to ensure that late-arriving packets do not induce a response, such as those that are able to close the UDP socket, MAY end these states earlier to allow for faster resource recovery
requirements.statement: Endpoints that have some alternative means to ensure that late-arriving packets do not induce a response, such as those that are able to close the UDP socket, MAY end these states earlier to allow for faster resource recovery.

requirements.title: Do not end closing or draining state early for servers with open sockets
requirements.statement: Servers that retain an open socket for accepting new connections SHOULD NOT end the closing or draining state early.

requirements.title: Discard connection state after closing or draining ends
requirements.statement: Once its closing or draining state ends, an endpoint SHOULD discard all connection state.

requirements.title: Send Stateless Reset after closing or draining ends
requirements.statement: The endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to any further incoming packets belonging to this connection.

requirements.title: Detect stateless reset from trailing bytes
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST detect a potential Stateless Reset using the trailing 16 bytes of the UDP datagram.

requirements.title: Remember recent stateless reset tokens
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST remember all stateless reset tokens associated with the connection IDs and remote addresses for datagrams it has recently sent.

requirements.title: Compare the remote-address token set to classify Stateless Reset
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST identify a received datagram as a Stateless Reset by comparing the last 16 bytes of the datagram with all stateless reset tokens associated with the remote address on which the datagram was received.

requirements.title: Skip the token check after successful packet processing
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY skip this check if any packet from a datagram is successfully processed.

requirements.title: Always check when the first packet cannot be processed
requirements.statement: However, the comparison MUST be performed when the first packet in an incoming datagram either cannot be associated with a connection or cannot be decrypted.

requirements.title: Ignore unused and retired reset tokens
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT check for any stateless reset tokens associated with connection IDs it has not used or for connection IDs that have been retired.

requirements.title: Avoid leaking token values during comparison
requirements.statement: When comparing a datagram to stateless reset token values, endpoints MUST perform the comparison without leaking information about the value of the token.

requirements.title: Stop sending packets after a stateless reset token match
requirements.statement: If the last 16 bytes of the datagram are identical in value to a stateless reset token, the endpoint MUST NOT send any further packets on this connection.

requirements.title: Use a recoverable connection ID length with static-key tokens
requirements.statement: An endpoint that uses this design MUST either use the same connection ID length for all connections or encode the length of the connection ID such that it can be recovered without state.

requirements.title: Do not reuse the connection ID and static key combination
requirements.statement: This method for choosing the stateless reset token means that the combination of connection ID and static key MUST NOT be used for another connection.

requirements.title: Do not reuse a connection ID after a revealed stateless reset
requirements.statement: A connection ID from a connection that is reset by revealing the stateless reset token MUST NOT be reused for new connections at nodes that share a static key.

requirements.title: Use each stateless reset token for only one connection ID
requirements.statement: The same stateless reset token MUST NOT be used for multiple connection IDs.

requirements.title: Allow duplicate stateless reset tokens to signal protocol violation
requirements.statement: Endpoints are not required to compare new values against all previous values, but a duplicate value MAY be treated as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Send a Stateless Reset in response to receiving a packet that it cannot associate with an active connection
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to receiving a packet that it cannot associate with an active connection.

requirements.title: Discard undersized QUIC packets
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST discard packets that are too small to be valid QUIC packets.

requirements.title: Allow Stateless Reset in response to long-header packets
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset in response to a packet with a long header.

requirements.title: Use CONNECTION_CLOSE for fatal connection errors when able
requirements.statement: An endpoint that wishes to communicate a fatal connection error MUST use a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame if it is able.

requirements.title: Errors that result in the connection being unusable, such as an obvious violation of protocol semantics or corruption of state that affects an entire connection, MUST be signaled using a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame (Section 19
requirements.statement: Errors that result in the connection being unusable, such as an obvious violation of protocol semantics or corruption of state that affects an entire connection, MUST be signaled using a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame (Section 19.19).

requirements.title: Signal application-specific protocol errors with frame type 0x1d
requirements.statement: Application-specific protocol errors MUST be signaled using the CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with a frame type of 0x1d.

requirements.title: Use CONNECTION_CLOSE type 0x1c for transport errors
requirements.statement: Transport errors, including all those described in this document, MUST be carried in the CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with a frame type of 0x1c.

requirements.title: As the AEAD for Initial packets does not provide strong authentication, an endpoint MAY discard an invalid Initial packet
requirements.statement: As the AEAD for Initial packets does not provide strong authentication, an endpoint MAY discard an invalid Initial packet.

requirements.title: Discard packets only without retained processing effects
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST not discard a packet unless it does not process the frames in the packet or it reverts the effects of any processing.

requirements.title: RESET_STREAM MUST only be instigated by the application protocol that uses QUIC
requirements.statement: RESET_STREAM MUST only be instigated by the application protocol that uses QUIC.

requirements.title: Define prematurely canceled stream rules
requirements.statement: Application protocols SHOULD define rules for handling streams that are prematurely canceled by either endpoint.

requirements.title: that detects an error SHOULD signal the existence of that error to its peer
requirements.statement: An endpoint that detects an error SHOULD signal the existence of that error to its peer.

requirements.title: The most appropriate error code (Section 20) SHOULD be included in the frame that signals the error
requirements.statement: The most appropriate error code (Section 20) SHOULD be included in the frame that signals the error.

requirements.title: Do not use stateless reset when frame transmission state exists
requirements.statement: A stateless reset MUST NOT be used by an endpoint that has the state necessary to send a frame on the connection.

requirements.title: Version Negotiation packets have no cryptographic protection
requirements.statement: Version Negotiation packets MUST NOT have cryptographic protection; see [QUIC-INVARIANTS].

requirements.title: Route based on the first packet
requirements.statement: Receivers MAY route based on the information in the first packet contained in a UDP datagram.

requirements.title: Do not coalesce packets with different connection IDs
requirements.statement: Senders MUST NOT coalesce QUIC packets with different connection IDs into a single UDP datagram.

requirements.title: Ignore later packets with a different DCID
requirements.statement: Receivers SHOULD ignore any subsequent packets with a different Destination Connection ID than the first packet in the datagram.

requirements.title: Process each coalesced packet separately
requirements.statement: The receiver of coalesced QUIC packets MUST individually process each QUIC packet and separately acknowledge each QUIC packet, as if the packets were received as the payload of different UDP datagrams.

requirements.title: Buffer or discard on decryption failure
requirements.statement: If decryption fails, the receiver MAY either discard or buffer the packet for later processing.

requirements.title: Continue processing remaining coalesced packets
requirements.statement: If decryption fails, the receiver MUST attempt to process the remaining packets.

requirements.title: Increase packet numbers by at least one
requirements.statement: A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a packet number within the same packet number space in one connection.

requirements.title: numbers in each space start at packet number 0
requirements.statement: Packet numbers in each MUST space start at packet number 0.

requirements.title: Treat unexpected acknowledgments as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD treat receipt of an acknowledgment for a packet it did not send as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, if it is able to detect the condition.

requirements.title: Acknowledge every packet at least once
requirements.statement: Every packet SHOULD be acknowledged at least once.

requirements.title: Acknowledge Initial and Handshake packets immediately
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST acknowledge all ack-eliciting Initial and Handshake packets immediately.

requirements.title: Acknowledge 0-RTT and 1-RTT packets within max_ack_delay
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST acknowledge all ack-eliciting 0-RTT and 1-RTT packets within its advertised max_ack_delay.

requirements.title: Do not send multiple ACK-only packets in response to one ack-eliciting packet
requirements.statement: Since packets containing only ACK frames are not congestion controlled, an endpoint MUST NOT send more than one such packet in response to receiving an ack-eliciting packet.

requirements.title: Send ACK frames with other frames for new acknowledgments
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD send an ACK frame with other frames when there are new ack-eliciting packets to acknowledge.

requirements.title: Avoid relying on ACK-only packets to elicit acknowledgments
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT rely on ACK-only packets to elicit acknowledgments from its peer.

requirements.title: Defer ACK frames when only non-ack-eliciting packets remain
requirements.statement: When only non-ack-eliciting packets need to be acknowledged, an endpoint MAY choose not to send an ACK frame with outgoing frames until an ack-eliciting packet has been received.

requirements.title: Avoid infinite feedback loops when adding ack-eliciting frames
requirements.statement: In that case, an endpoint MUST NOT send an ack-eliciting frame in all packets that would otherwise be non-ack-eliciting.

requirements.title: Send ACK frames after at least two ack-eliciting packets
requirements.statement: A receiver SHOULD send an ACK frame after receiving at least two ack-eliciting packets.

requirements.title: Allow multiple packets before deciding to ACK
requirements.statement: A receiver MAY process multiple available packets before determining whether to send an ACK frame in response.

requirements.title: Retain ACK ranges until safe to discard
requirements.statement: A receiver MUST retain an ACK Range unless it can ensure that it will not subsequently accept packets with numbers in that range.

requirements.title: Retain the largest successfully processed packet number
requirements.statement: Receivers can discard all ACK Ranges, but they MUST retain the largest packet number that has been successfully processed.

requirements.title: Include the largest received packet number in ACK frames
requirements.statement: A receiver SHOULD include an ACK Range containing the largest received packet number in every ACK frame.

requirements.title: Exclude uncontrolled delays from ACK Delay
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT include delays that it does not control when populating the ACK Delay field in an ACK frame.

requirements.title: Include decryption-key buffering delays
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD include buffering delays caused by unavailability of decryption keys.

requirements.title: Report measured delay when it exceeds max_ack_delay
requirements.statement: When the measured acknowledgment delay is larger than its max_ack_delay, an endpoint SHOULD report the measured delay.

requirements.title: Carry ACK frames only in the same packet number space
requirements.statement: ACK frames MUST only be carried in a packet that has the same packet number space as the packet being acknowledged.

requirements.title: Use 1-RTT for acknowledging 1-RTT packets
requirements.statement: Packets that are protected with 1-RTT keys MUST be acknowledged in packets that are also protected with 1-RTT keys.

requirements.title: Send non-PADDING frames periodically to elicit acknowledgments
requirements.statement: To avoid a deadlock, a sender SHOULD ensure that other frames are sent periodically in addition to PADDING frames to elicit acknowledgments from the receiver.

requirements.title: Include ACK frames when not sent recently
requirements.statement: When sending a packet for any reason, an endpoint SHOULD attempt to include an ACK frame if one has not been sent recently.

requirements.title: Include ECN counts in subsequent ACK frames
requirements.statement: These ECN counts MUST be included in subsequent ACK frames.

requirements.title: Increment ECN counts only while processing QUIC packets
requirements.statement: ECN counts MUST only be incremented when QUIC packets from the received IP packet are processed.

requirements.title: Validate ECN counts before using them
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives an ACK frame with ECN counts MUST validate the counts before using them.

requirements.title: Fail ECN validation when ECT(0) and CE counts are too small
requirements.statement: ECN validation MUST fail if the sum of the increase in ECT(0) and ECN-CE counts is less than the number of newly acknowledged packets that were originally sent with an ECT(0) marking.

requirements.title: Fail ECN validation when ECT(1) and CE counts are too small
requirements.statement: ECN validation MUST fail if the sum of the increases to ECT(1) and ECN-CE counts is less than the number of newly acknowledged packets sent with an ECT(1) marking.

requirements.title: Do not fail validation on ACK frames that do not advance the largest acknowledged packet number
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT fail ECN validation as a result of processing an ACK frame that does not increase the largest acknowledged packet number.

requirements.title: Even if validation fails, an endpoint MAY revalidate ECN for the same path at any later time in the connection
requirements.statement: Even if validation fails, an endpoint MAY revalidate ECN for the same path at any later time in the connection.

requirements.title: Upon successful validation, an endpoint MAY continue to set an ECT codepoint in subsequent packets it sends, with the expectation that the path is ECN capable
requirements.statement: Upon successful validation, an endpoint MAY continue to set an ECT codepoint in subsequent packets it sends, with the expectation that the path is ECN capable.

requirements.title: Network routing and path elements can change mid-connection
requirements.statement: Network routing and path elements can change mid-connection; an endpoint MUST disable ECN if validation later fails.

requirements.title: Check whether the path and peer support ECN before enabling it
requirements.statement: To enable ECN, a sending QUIC endpoint MUST first determine whether a path supports ECN marking and whether the peer reports the ECN values in received IP headers.

requirements.title: wait for a short period of time to collect multiple frames before sending a packet that is not maximally packed, to avoid sending out large numbers of small packets
requirements.statement: A sender MAY wait for a short period of time to collect multiple frames before sending a packet that is not maximally packed, to avoid sending out large numbers of small packets.

requirements.title: An implementation MAY use knowledge about application sending behavior or heuristics to determine whether and for how long to wait
requirements.statement: An implementation MAY use knowledge about application sending behavior or heuristics to determine whether and for how long to wait.

requirements.title: Pad Initial datagrams to 1200 bytes
requirements.statement: A client MUST expand the payload of all UDP datagrams carrying Initial packets to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes by adding PADDING frames to the Initial packet or by coalescing the Initial packet.

requirements.title: Pad server Initial datagrams to 1200 bytes
requirements.statement: A server MUST expand the payload of all UDP datagrams carrying ack-eliciting Initial packets to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes.

requirements.title: Allow oversized Initial datagrams when the path and peer support them
requirements.statement: Datagrams containing Initial packets MAY exceed 1200 bytes if the sender believes that the network path and peer both support the size that it chooses.

requirements.title: Discard undersized Initial packets at the server
requirements.statement: A server MUST discard an Initial packet that is carried in a UDP datagram with a payload that is smaller than the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes.

requirements.title: Allow servers to close on undersized Initial packets
requirements.statement: A server MAY also immediately close the connection by sending a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with an error code of PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

requirements.title: Limit bytes sent before validating the client address
requirements.statement: The server MUST also limit the number of bytes it sends before validating the address of the client.

requirements.title: Ignore ICMP PMTU decreases below the minimum datagram size
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST ignore an ICMP message that claims the PMTU has decreased below QUIC's smallest allowed maximum datagram size.

requirements.title: Validate ICMP messages against packet injection
requirements.statement: QUIC endpoints using PMTUD SHOULD validate ICMP messages to protect from packet injection as specified in [RFC8201] and Section 5.2 of [RFC8085].

requirements.title: Use the quoted packet to associate ICMP messages with a connection
requirements.statement: This validation SHOULD use the quoted packet supplied in the payload of an ICMP message to associate the message with a corresponding transport connection.

requirements.title: Validate ICMP messages with addresses, ports, and connection IDs
requirements.statement: ICMP message validation MUST include matching IP addresses and UDP ports and, when possible, connection IDs to an active QUIC session.

requirements.title: Ignore ICMP messages that fail validation
requirements.statement: The endpoint SHOULD ignore all ICMP messages that fail validation.

requirements.title: Do not increase PMTU based on ICMP messages
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT increase the PMTU based on ICMP messages.

requirements.title: Treat ICMP-driven PMTU reductions as provisional
requirements.statement: Any reduction in QUIC's maximum datagram size in response to ICMP messages MAY be provisional until QUIC's loss detection algorithm determines that the quoted packet has actually been lost.

requirements.title: Use DPLPMTUD or PMTUD to determine support for a desired size
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD use DPLPMTUD or PMTUD to determine whether the path to a destination will support a desired maximum datagram size without fragmentation.

requirements.title: Do not exceed the smallest allowed maximum datagram size without PMTU discovery
requirements.statement: In the absence of these mechanisms, QUIC endpoints SHOULD NOT send datagrams larger than the smallest allowed maximum datagram size.

requirements.title: Stop sending packets on a path that cannot support 1200 bytes
requirements.statement: If a QUIC endpoint determines that the PMTU between any pair of local and remote IP addresses cannot support the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes, it MUST immediately cease sending QUIC packets on the affected path except for those in PMTU probes or those containing CONNECTION_CLOSE frames.

requirements.title: Allow connection termination when no alternative path exists
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY terminate the connection if an alternative path cannot be found.

requirements.title: Maintain a maximum datagram size per address pair when doing PMTU discovery
requirements.statement: QUIC implementations that implement any kind of PMTU discovery SHOULD maintain a maximum datagram size for each combination of local and remote IP addresses.

requirements.title: Allow conservative maximum datagram size estimates
requirements.statement: A QUIC implementation MAY be more conservative in computing the maximum datagram size to allow for unknown tunnel overheads or IP header options or extensions.

requirements.title: Set BASE_PLPMTU consistently with QUIC's smallest allowed maximum datagram size
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD set the initial value of BASE_PLPMTU to be consistent with QUIC's smallest allowed maximum datagram size.

requirements.title: Maintain an MPS per address pair when using DPLPMTUD
requirements.statement: QUIC endpoints implementing DPLPMTUD MUST maintain a DPLPMTUD Maximum Packet Size for each combination of local and remote IP addresses.

requirements.title: Do not treat PMTU probe loss as congestion
requirements.statement: Loss of a QUIC packet that is carried in a PMTU probe SHOULD NOT trigger a congestion control reaction.

requirements.title: Allow clients to use reserved version numbers
requirements.statement: A client MAY use one of these version numbers with the expectation that the server will initiate version negotiation.

requirements.title: Reserved version numbers are not real protocols
requirements.statement: Reserved version numbers MUST NOT represent a real protocol.

requirements.title: Prior to receiving an acknowledgment for a packet number space, the full packet number MUST b...
requirements.statement: Prior to receiving an acknowledgment for a packet number space, the full packet number MUST be included; it is not to be truncated, as described below.

requirements.title: After an acknowledgment is received for a packet number space, the sender MUST use a packet n...
requirements.statement: After an acknowledgment is received for a packet number space, the sender MUST use a packet number size able to represent more than twice as large a range as the difference between the largest acknowledged packet number and the packet number being sent.

requirements.title: Use packet number encoding large enough for reordered delivery
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD use a large enough packet number encoding to allow the packet number to be recovered even if the packet arrives after packets that are sent afterwards.

requirements.title: Set the Version field to zero
requirements.statement: The Version field of a Version Negotiation packet MUST be set to 0x00000000.

requirements.title: Version-specific rules for the connection ID therefore MUST NOT influence a decision about wh...
requirements.statement: Version-specific rules for the connection ID therefore MUST NOT influence a decision about whether to send a Version Negotiation packet.

requirements.title: Allow multiple server Initial packets
requirements.statement: A server MAY send multiple Initial packets.

requirements.title: New packet numbers MUST be used for any new packets that are sent; as described in Section 17...
requirements.statement: New packet numbers MUST be used for any new packets that are sent; as described in Section 17.2.5.3, reusing packet numbers could compromise packet protection.

requirements.title: A server SHOULD treat a violation of remembered limits (Section 7.4.1) as a connection error...
requirements.statement: A server SHOULD treat a violation of remembered limits (Section 7.4.1) as a connection error of an appropriate type (for instance, a FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR for exceeding stream data limits).

requirements.title: This value MUST NOT be equal to the Destination Connection ID field of the packet sent by the...
requirements.statement: This value MUST NOT be equal to the Destination Connection ID field of the packet sent by the client.

requirements.title: The server MUST include a connection ID of its choice in the Source Connection ID field
requirements.statement: The server MUST include a connection ID of its choice in the Source Connection ID field.

requirements.title: A client MUST discard a Retry packet that contains a Source Connection ID field that is ident...
requirements.statement: A client MUST discard a Retry packet that contains a Source Connection ID field that is identical to the Destination Connection ID field of its Initial packet.

requirements.title: The client MUST use the value from the Source Connection ID field of the Retry packet in the...
requirements.statement: The client MUST use the value from the Source Connection ID field of the Retry packet in the Destination Connection ID field of subsequent packets that it sends.

requirements.title: Limit Retry responses per UDP datagram
requirements.statement: A server MUST NOT send more than one Retry packet in response to a single UDP datagram.

requirements.title: Limit Retry processing to one packet per connection attempt
requirements.statement: A client MUST accept and process at most one Retry packet for each connection attempt.

requirements.title: Discard subsequent Retry packets
requirements.statement: After the client has received and processed an Initial or Retry packet from the server, it MUST discard any subsequent Retry packets that it receives.

requirements.title: Clients MUST discard Retry packets that have a Retry Integrity Tag that cannot be validated;...
requirements.statement: Clients MUST discard Retry packets that have a Retry Integrity Tag that cannot be validated; see Section 5.8 of [QUIC-TLS].

requirements.title: Discard zero-length Retry tokens
requirements.statement: A client MUST discard a Retry packet with a zero-length Retry Token field.

requirements.title: The client responds to a Retry packet with an Initial packet that MUST include the provided R...
requirements.statement: The client responds to a Retry packet with an Initial packet that MUST include the provided Retry token to continue connection establishment.

requirements.title: The client copies the Source Connection ID field from the Retry packet to the Destination Con...
requirements.statement: The client copies the Source Connection ID field from the Retry packet to the Destination Connection ID field and MUST use this value until an Initial packet with an updated value is received; see Section 7.2.

requirements.title: Reuse handshake message after Retry
requirements.statement: A client MUST use the same cryptographic handshake message it included in this packet.

requirements.title: Server handling of changed handshake message
requirements.statement: A server MAY treat a packet that contains a different cryptographic handshake message as a connection error or discard it.

requirements.title: Allow 0-RTT after Retry
requirements.statement: A client MAY attempt 0-RTT after receiving a Retry packet by sending 0-RTT packets to the connection ID provided by the server.

requirements.title: Do not reset packet numbers after Retry
requirements.statement: A client MUST NOT reset the packet number for any packet number space after processing a Retry packet.

requirements.title: Abort on packet number reset
requirements.statement: A server MAY abort the connection if it detects that the client reset the packet number.

requirements.title: An endpoint that does not support this feature MUST disable it, as defined below
requirements.statement: An endpoint that does not support this feature MUST disable it, as defined below.

requirements.title: Administrative spin-bit disable controls
requirements.statement: Implementations MUST allow administrators of clients and servers to disable the spin bit either globally or on a per-connection basis.

requirements.title: Even when the spin bit is not disabled by the administrator, endpoints MUST disable their use...
requirements.statement: Even when the spin bit is not disabled by the administrator, endpoints MUST disable their use of the spin bit for a random selection of at least one in every 16 network paths, or for one in every 16 connection IDs, in order to ensure that QUIC connections that disable the spin bit are commonly observed on the network.

requirements.title: Disabled spin bit may carry any value
requirements.statement: When the spin bit is disabled, endpoints MAY set the spin bit to any value.

requirements.title: Ignore incoming spin-bit value when disabled
requirements.statement: When the spin bit is disabled, endpoints MUST ignore any incoming value.

requirements.title: When a server receives a 1-RTT packet that increases the highest packet number seen by the se...
requirements.statement: When a server receives a 1-RTT packet that increases the highest packet number seen by the server from the client on a given network path, it MUST set the spin value for that path to be equal to the spin bit in the received packet.

requirements.title: Update client spin value on new server packet
requirements.statement: When a client receives a 1-RTT packet that increases the highest packet number seen by the client from the server on a given network path, it MUST set the spin value for that path to the inverse of the spin bit in the received packet.

requirements.title: Reject premature MAX_STREAM_DATA for uncreated local streams
requirements.statement: Receiving a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a locally initiated stream that has not yet been created MUST be treated as a connection error of type STREAM_STATE_ERROR.

requirements.title: Treat MAX_STREAM_DATA on receive-only streams as STREAM_STATE_ERROR
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a receive-only stream MUST terminate the connection with error STREAM_STATE_ERROR.

requirements.title: Send STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED when blocked by stream flow control
requirements.statement: A sender SHOULD send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame (type=0x15) when it wishes to send data but is unable to do so due to stream-level flow control.

requirements.title: Terminate on STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED for send-only stream
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame for a send-only stream MUST terminate the connection with error STREAM_STATE_ERROR.

requirements.title: Once a sender MUST indicate a Retire Prior To value, smaller values sent in subsequent NEW_CO...
requirements.statement: Once a sender MUST indicate a Retire Prior To value, smaller values sent in subsequent NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames have no effect.

requirements.title: The PING frame MAY be used to keep a connection alive when an application or application prot...
requirements.statement: The PING frame MAY be used to keep a connection alive when an application or application protocol wishes to prevent the connection from timing out; see Section 10.1.2.

requirements.title: An endpoint therefore needs to understand the syntax of all frames before it MAY successfully...
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST understand the syntax of all frames before it can successfully process a packet.

requirements.title: Define interaction with prior extensions
requirements.statement: Such extensions SHOULD define their interaction with previously defined extensions modifying the same protocol components.

requirements.title: Extension frames are congestion controlled
requirements.statement: Extension frames MUST be congestion controlled.

requirements.title: Extension frames trigger ACK generation
requirements.statement: Extension frames MUST cause an ACK frame to be sent.

requirements.title: Use ECN information to manage congestion state
requirements.statement: If they have enabled ECN for packets they send, QUIC implementations SHOULD use the information in the ECN section to manage their congestion state.

requirements.title: Once acknowledged, a packet MUST remain acknowledged, even if it does not appear in a future...
requirements.statement: Once acknowledged, a packet MUST remain acknowledged, even if it does not appear in a future ACK frame.

requirements.title: A receiver of RESET_STREAM MAY discard any data that it already received on that stream
requirements.statement: A receiver of RESET_STREAM MAY discard any data that it already received on that stream.

requirements.title: Error on RESET_STREAM for send-only streams
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives a RESET_STREAM frame for a send-only stream MUST terminate the connection with error STREAM_STATE_ERROR.

requirements.title: Treat premature local STOP_SENDING as STREAM_STATE_ERROR
requirements.statement: Receiving a STOP_SENDING frame for a locally initiated stream that has not yet been created MUST be treated as a connection error of type STREAM_STATE_ERROR.

requirements.title: Terminate on STOP_SENDING for receive-only streams
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives a STOP_SENDING frame for a receive-only stream MUST terminate the connection with error STREAM_STATE_ERROR.

requirements.title: Allow optional out-of-order delivery to applications
requirements.statement: Implementations MAY offer the ability to deliver stream data out of order to a receiving application.

requirements.title: Keep retransmitted stream data stable at the same offset
requirements.statement: The data at a given offset MUST NOT change if it is sent multiple times.

requirements.title: Respect peer flow control limits
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send data on any stream without ensuring that it is within the flow control limits set by its peer.

requirements.title: To defend against this style of denial of service, endpoints that share a static key for stat...
requirements.statement: To defend against this style of denial of service, endpoints that share a static key for stateless resets (see Section 10.3.2) MUST be arranged so that packets with a given connection ID always arrive at an instance that has connection state, unless that connection is no longer active.

requirements.title: More generally, servers MUST NOT generate a stateless reset if a connection with the correspo...
requirements.statement: More generally, servers MUST NOT generate a stateless reset if a connection with the corresponding connection ID could be active on any endpoint using the same static key.

requirements.title: Servers SHOULD provide mitigations for this attack by limiting the usage and lifetime of addr...
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD provide mitigations for this attack by limiting the usage and lifetime of address validation tokens; see Section 8.1.3.

requirements.title: An endpoint MAY skip packet numbers when sending packets to detect this behavior
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY skip packet numbers when sending packets to detect this behavior.

requirements.title: A client MUST NOT send non-probing frames to a preferred address prior to validating that add...
requirements.statement: A client MUST NOT send non-probing frames to a preferred address prior to validating that address; see Section 8.

requirements.title: Optionally prevent connection attempts or migration to a loopback address
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY prevent connection attempts or migration to a loopback address.

requirements.title: Do not allow loopback connections or migration after prior non-loopback exposure
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD NOT allow connections or migration to a loopback address if the same service was previously available at a different interface or if the address was provided by a service at a non-loopback address.

requirements.title: Do not refuse an address without network-specific safety knowledge
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD NOT refuse to use an address unless they have specific knowledge about the network indicating that sending datagrams to unvalidated addresses in a given range is not safe.

requirements.title: Endpoints MAY choose to reduce the risk of request forgery by not including values from NEW_T...
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY choose to reduce the risk of request forgery by not including values from NEW_TOKEN frames in Initial packets or by only sending probing frames in packets prior to completing address validation.

requirements.title: Endpoints MAY choose to avoid sending datagrams to these ports or not send datagrams that mat...
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY choose to avoid sending datagrams to these ports or not send datagrams that match these patterns prior to validating the destination address.

requirements.title: Retire problematic connection IDs before use
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY retire connection IDs containing patterns known to be problematic without using them.

requirements.title: QUIC servers SHOULD NOT be deployed in networks that do not deploy ingress filtering [BCP38]...
requirements.statement: QUIC servers SHOULD NOT be deployed in networks that do not deploy ingress filtering [BCP38] and also have inadequately secured UDP endpoints.

requirements.title: Define forgery countermeasures for server migration extensions
requirements.statement: Any future extension that allows server migration MUST also define countermeasures for forgery attacks.

requirements.title: QUIC deployments SHOULD provide mitigations for the Slowloris attacks, such as increasing the...
requirements.statement: QUIC deployments SHOULD provide mitigations for the Slowloris attacks, such as increasing the maximum number of clients the server will allow, limiting the number of connections a single IP address is allowed to make, imposing restrictions on the minimum transfer speed a connection is allowed to have, and restricting the length of time an endpoint is allowed to stay connected.

requirements.title: Provide stream fragmentation mitigations
requirements.statement: QUIC deployments SHOULD provide mitigations for stream fragmentation attacks.

requirements.title: While there are legitimate uses for all messages, implementations SHOULD track cost of proces...
requirements.statement: While there are legitimate uses for all messages, implementations SHOULD track cost of processing relative to progress and treat excessive quantities of any non-productive packets as indicative of an attack.

requirements.title: Endpoints MAY respond to this condition with a connection error or by dropping packets
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY respond to this condition with a connection error or by dropping packets.

requirements.title: Require only codepoint value and contact information for provisional registration requests
requirements.statement: Provisional registration requests MUST require only the codepoint value and contact information.

requirements.title: New requests for codepoints from QUIC registries SHOULD use a randomly selected codepoint tha...
requirements.statement: New requests for codepoints from QUIC registries SHOULD use a randomly selected codepoint that excludes both existing allocations and the first unallocated codepoint in the selected space.

requirements.title: Allow contiguous ranges for multi-codepoint requests
requirements.statement: Requests for multiple codepoints MAY use a contiguous range.

requirements.title: For codepoints that are encoded in variable-length integers (Section 16), such as frame types...
requirements.statement: For codepoints that are encoded in variable-length integers (Section 16), such as frame types, codepoints that encode to four or eight bytes (that is, values 214 and above) SHOULD be used unless the usage is especially sensitive to having a longer encoding.

requirements.title: Allow requested codepoint values in registration applications
requirements.statement: Applications to register codepoints in QUIC registries MAY include a requested codepoint as part of the registration.

requirements.title: IANA MUST allocate the selected codepoint if the codepoint is unassigned and the requirements...
requirements.statement: IANA MUST allocate the selected codepoint if the codepoint is unassigned and the requirements of the registration policy are met.

requirements.title: Review codepoint removal requests
requirements.statement: A request to remove a codepoint MUST be reviewed by the designated experts.

requirements.title: Determine whether codepoints remain in use
requirements.statement: The experts MUST attempt to determine whether the codepoint is still in use.

requirements.title: Do not reclaim codepoints when use is identified
requirements.statement: If any use of the codepoints is identified by this search or a request to update the registration is made, the codepoint MUST NOT be reclaimed.

requirements.title: Allow removal when no use is identified
requirements.statement: If no use of the codepoint was identified and no request was made to update the registration, the codepoint MAY be removed from the registry.

requirements.title: The creation of a registry MAY identify a range of codepoints where registrations are governe...
requirements.statement: The creation of a registry MAY identify a range of codepoints where registrations are governed by a different registration policy.

requirements.title: Make Standards Track registrations permanent
requirements.statement: All registrations made by Standards Track publications MUST be permanent.

requirements.title: Protect reserved version-pattern codepoints
requirements.statement: All codepoints that follow the pattern 0x?a?a?a?a MUST NOT be assigned by IANA.

requirements.title: Exclude reserved version-pattern codepoints from listings
requirements.statement: All codepoints that follow the pattern 0x?a?a?a?a MUST NOT appear in the listing of assigned values.

requirements.title: Use stricter policy for low transport-parameter codepoints
requirements.statement: Values between 0x00 and 0x3f inclusive MUST be assigned using Standards Action or IESG Approval.

requirements.title: Include Parameter Name for transport parameters
requirements.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST include the Parameter Name field.

requirements.title: Include Frame Type Name for frame types
requirements.statement: Permanent registrations in this registry MUST include the Frame Type Name field.

requirements.title: Permit RESET_STREAM as the first frame
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY send a RESET_STREAM as the first frame that mentions a stream, causing the sending part of that stream to open and then immediately transition to the Reset Sent state.

requirements.title: Enter Recv when the peer-side sending part opens
requirements.statement: For a bidirectional stream, the receiving part MUST enter the Recv state when the sending part initiated by the endpoint enters the Ready state.

requirements.title: Create lower-numbered same-type streams first
requirements.statement: Before a stream is created, all streams of the same type with lower-numbered stream IDs MUST be created.

requirements.title: Recognize final size when FIN arrives
requirements.statement: When a STREAM frame with a FIN bit is received, the final size of the stream MUST be known.

requirements.title: Enter Size Known after FIN
requirements.statement: The receiving part of the stream MUST then enter the Size Known state.

requirements.title: Forbid terminal-state transmit frames
requirements.statement: A sender MUST NOT send STREAM, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, or RESET_STREAM frames from a terminal state.

requirements.title: Forbid post-reset transmission of STREAM frames
requirements.statement: A sender MUST NOT send a STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame for a stream in the Reset Sent state or any terminal state after sending a RESET_STREAM frame.

requirements.title: Signal aborting reads with STOP_SENDING
requirements.statement: If the stream is in the Recv or Size Known state, the transport SHOULD signal aborting reading by sending a STOP_SENDING frame to prompt closure of the stream in the opposite direction.

requirements.title: Count data after STOP_SENDING toward flow control
requirements.statement: STREAM frames received after sending a STOP_SENDING frame MUST still be counted toward connection and stream flow control even if they are discarded upon receipt.

requirements.title: Permit deferred RESET_STREAM in Data Sent
requirements.statement: If the stream is in the Data Sent state, the endpoint MAY defer sending the RESET_STREAM frame until the packets containing outstanding data are acknowledged or declared lost.

requirements.title: Prefer RESET_STREAM over retransmission after loss
requirements.statement: If any outstanding data is declared lost, the endpoint SHOULD send a RESET_STREAM frame instead of retransmitting the data.

requirements.title: Copy STOP_SENDING error codes when sending RESET_STREAM
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD copy the error code from the STOP_SENDING frame to the RESET_STREAM frame it sends.

requirements.title: Allow ignoring later RESET_STREAM error codes
requirements.statement: An endpoint that sends a STOP_SENDING frame MAY ignore the error code in any RESET_STREAM frames subsequently received for that stream.

requirements.title: Use STOP_SENDING only before peer reset
requirements.statement: STOP_SENDING SHOULD only be sent for a stream that has not been reset by the peer.

requirements.title: Ignore non-increasing flow-control frames
requirements.statement: A sender MUST ignore any MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frames that do not increase flow control limits.

requirements.title: Allow repeated or early credit advertisements
requirements.statement: A receiver MAY send a MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frame multiple times within a round trip or send it early enough to allow time for loss of the frame and subsequent recovery.

requirements.title: Use final size for flow control accounting
requirements.statement: The receiver MUST use the final size of the stream to account for all bytes sent on the stream in its connection-level flow controller.

requirements.title: Do not send data at or beyond final size
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send data on a stream at or beyond the final size.

requirements.title: Treat data beyond final size as an error
requirements.statement: A receiver SHOULD treat receipt of data at or beyond the final size as an error of type FINAL_SIZE_ERROR, even after a stream is closed.

requirements.title: Close on oversized stream-count values in transport parameters
requirements.statement: If an oversized max_streams value is received in a transport parameter, the connection MUST be closed immediately with TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.

requirements.title: Close on oversized stream-count values in frames
requirements.statement: If an oversized max_streams value is received in a frame, the connection MUST be closed immediately with FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.

requirements.title: Respect peer-advertised stream limits
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST NOT exceed the limit set by their peer.

requirements.title: Treat excessive stream IDs as stream limit errors
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives a frame with a stream ID exceeding the limit it has sent MUST treat this as a connection error of type STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR.

requirements.title: Send STREAMS_BLOCKED when blocked by peer limits
requirements.statement: An endpoint that is unable to open a new stream due to the peer's limits SHOULD send a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame.

requirements.title: Do not wait for STREAMS_BLOCKED before advertising credit
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT wait to receive STREAMS_BLOCKED before advertising additional credit.

requirements.title: Maintain a sufficient peer connection ID pool
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD ensure that its peer has a sufficient number of available and unused connection IDs.

requirements.title: Advertise active connection ID limit
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST advertise the number of active connection IDs they are willing to maintain using the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter.

requirements.title: Do not exceed the peer's active CID limit
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT provide more connection IDs than the peer's limit.

requirements.title: Allow temporary CID excess only with immediate retirement requirements
