requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY send connection IDs that temporarily exceed a peer's limit if the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame also requires the retirement of any excess by including a sufficiently large value in the Retire Prior To field.

requirements.title: Close on too many active CIDs
requirements.statement: After processing a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame and adding and retiring active connection IDs, if the number of active connection IDs exceeds the value advertised in the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter, an endpoint MUST close the connection with an error of type CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.

requirements.title: Supply a new connection ID when the peer retires one
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD supply a new connection ID when the peer retires a connection ID.

requirements.title: Optionally supply a new connection ID after an unused one appears
requirements.statement: If an endpoint provided fewer connection IDs than the peer's active_connection_id_limit, it MAY supply a new connection ID when it receives a packet with a previously unused connection ID.

requirements.title: Allow limiting the total number of issued CIDs
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY limit the total number of connection IDs issued for each connection to avoid the risk of running out of connection IDs.

requirements.title: Allow limiting CID issuance to reduce per-path state
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY also limit the issuance of connection IDs to reduce the amount of per-path state it maintains.

requirements.title: Keep enough peer-usable CIDs for migration
requirements.statement: An endpoint that initiates migration and requires non-zero-length connection IDs SHOULD ensure that the pool of connection IDs available to its peer allows the peer to use a new connection ID on migration.

requirements.title: Do not issue new connection IDs after selecting a zero-length one
requirements.statement: An endpoint that selects a zero-length connection ID during the handshake MUST not issue a new connection ID.

requirements.title: Use a zero-length destination connection ID toward such an endpoint
requirements.statement: A zero-length Destination Connection ID field MUST be used in all packets sent toward such an endpoint over any network path.

requirements.title: Continue accepting retired CIDs until the peer retires them
requirements.statement: The endpoint SHOULD continue to accept the previously issued connection IDs until they are retired by the peer.

requirements.title: Retire affected connection IDs before activating the new one
requirements.statement: Upon receipt of an increased Retire Prior To field, the peer MUST stop using the corresponding connection IDs and retire them with RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames before adding the newly provided connection ID to the set of active connection IDs.

requirements.title: Limit locally retired but unacknowledged connection IDs
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD limit the number of connection IDs it has retired locally for which RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames have not yet been acknowledged.

requirements.title: Track at least twice the active CID limit
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD allow for sending and tracking a number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames of at least twice the value of the active_connection_id_limit transport parameter.

requirements.title: Do not forget connection IDs without retiring them
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT forget a connection ID without retiring it.

requirements.title: Allow treating excessive unretired CIDs as an error
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY treat having connection IDs in need of retirement that exceed this limit as a connection error of type CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR.

requirements.title: Delay Retire Prior To updates
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD NOT issue updates of the Retire Prior To field before receiving RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames that retire all connection IDs indicated by the previous Retire Prior To value.

requirements.title: Prevent external correlation of connection IDs
requirements.statement: Connection IDs MUST NOT contain any information that can be used by an external observer to correlate them with other connection IDs for the same connection.

requirements.title: Do not reissue a connection ID on the same connection
requirements.statement: The same connection ID MUST NOT be issued more than once on the same connection.

requirements.title: Ensure the peer has a supply of connection IDs
requirements.statement: When an endpoint uses a non-zero-length connection ID, it MUST ensure that the peer has a supply of connection IDs from which to choose for packets sent to the endpoint.

requirements.title: Discard packets with a different version
requirements.statement: If a client receives a packet that uses a different version than it initially selected, it MUST discard that packet.

requirements.title: Send Version Negotiation for large unsupported packets
requirements.statement: If a server receives a packet that indicates an unsupported version and the packet is large enough to initiate a new connection for any supported version, the server SHOULD send a Version Negotiation packet.

requirements.title: Limit Version Negotiation responses
requirements.statement: A server MAY limit the number of packets to which it responds with a Version Negotiation packet.

requirements.title: Drop smaller unsupported-version packets
requirements.statement: Servers MUST drop smaller packets that specify unsupported versions.

requirements.title: Prefer Version Negotiation when possible
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD respond with a Version Negotiation packet, provided that the datagram is sufficiently long.

requirements.title: Send CONNECTION_REFUSED on connection refusal
requirements.statement: If a server refuses to accept a new connection, it SHOULD send an Initial packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with error code CONNECTION_REFUSED.

requirements.title: Buffer a limited number of 0-RTT packets
requirements.statement: If the packet is a 0-RTT packet, the server MAY buffer a limited number of these packets in anticipation of a late-arriving Initial packet.

requirements.title: Ignore premature Handshake packets from clients
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD ignore any Handshake packets sent before the client receives a server response.

requirements.title: Drop packets under all other circumstances
requirements.statement: Servers MUST drop incoming packets under all other circumstances.

requirements.title: Avoid stateless reset oracles in simple load balancing
requirements.statement: Server deployments that use this simple form of load balancing MUST avoid the creation of a stateless reset oracle.

requirements.title: Discard invalid packets lacking strong integrity protection
requirements.statement: Invalid packets that lack strong integrity protection, such as Initial, Retry, or Version Negotiation, MAY be discarded.

requirements.title: Limit Version Negotiation packets
requirements.statement: A server MAY limit the number of Version Negotiation packets it sends.

requirements.title: That supports only this version of QUIC MUST abandon the current connection attempt if it receives a Version Negotiation packet, with the following two exceptions
requirements.statement: A client that supports only this version of QUIC MUST abandon the current connection attempt if it receives a Version Negotiation packet, with the following two exceptions.

requirements.title: Discard stale Version Negotiation packets
requirements.statement: A client MUST discard any Version Negotiation packet if it has received and successfully processed any other packet, including an earlier Version Negotiation packet.

requirements.title: Discard Version Negotiation packets listing the selected version
requirements.statement: A client MUST discard a Version Negotiation packet that lists the QUIC version selected by the client.

requirements.title: Allow reserved versions in ignored version fields
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY add reserved versions to fields where unsupported versions are ignored, to test peer handling.

requirements.title: Send reserved-version packets for discard testing
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY send packets with a reserved version to test peer discard behavior.

requirements.title: Handshake uses long header packets to establish connection IDs
requirements.statement: During the handshake, packets with the long header MUST be used to establish the connection IDs used by both endpoints.

requirements.title: Use Source Connection ID to select the peer-facing Destination Connection ID
requirements.statement: Each endpoint MUST use the Source Connection ID field to specify the connection ID that is used in the Destination Connection ID field of packets being sent to it.

requirements.title: Use received source connection ID after the first Initial packet
requirements.statement: After processing the first Initial packet, each endpoint MUST set the Destination Connection ID field in subsequent packets it sends to the value of the Source Connection ID field it received.

requirements.title: Initial destination connection ID length minimum
requirements.statement: This Destination Connection ID MUST be at least 8 bytes in length.

requirements.title: Client reuses one destination connection ID until server packet receipt
requirements.statement: Until a packet is received from the server, the client MUST use the same Destination Connection ID value on all packets in this connection.

requirements.title: Populate the client Source Connection ID
requirements.statement: The client MUST populate the Source Connection ID field with a value of its choosing and set the Source Connection ID Length field to indicate the length.

requirements.title: Keep first-flight 0-RTT connection IDs aligned with the first Initial packet
requirements.statement: 0-RTT packets in the first flight MUST use the same Destination Connection ID and Source Connection ID values as the client's first Initial packet.

requirements.title: Change the Destination Connection ID it uses for sending packets in response to only the first received Initial or Retry packet
requirements.statement: A client MUST change the Destination Connection ID it uses for sending packets in response to only the first received Initial or Retry packet.

requirements.title: Set the destination connection ID from the first Initial packet
requirements.statement: A server MUST set the Destination Connection ID it uses for sending packets based on the first received Initial packet.

requirements.title: Allow further Destination Connection ID changes only from NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY make further changes to the Destination Connection ID only if the values are taken from NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames.

requirements.title: Discard subsequent Initial packets with a different Source Connection ID
requirements.statement: Subsequent Initial packets that include a different Source Connection ID MUST be discarded.

requirements.title: Include the first sent Initial Source CID in transport parameters
requirements.statement: Each endpoint MUST include the value of the Source Connection ID field from the first Initial packet it sent in the initial_source_connection_id transport parameter.

requirements.title: Echo the client Initial Destination Connection ID in original_destination_connection_id
requirements.statement: A server MUST include the Destination Connection ID field from the first Initial packet it received from the client in the original_destination_connection_id transport parameter.

requirements.title: Echo the Retry Source Connection ID when Retry is used
requirements.statement: If it sends a Retry packet, a server MUST also include the Source Connection ID field from the Retry packet in the retry_source_connection_id transport parameter.

requirements.title: The values provided by a peer for these transport parameters MUST match the values that an endpoint used in the Destination and Source Connection ID fields of Initial packets that it sent (and received, for servers)
requirements.statement: The values provided by a peer for these transport parameters MUST match the values that an endpoint used in the Destination and Source Connection ID fields of Initial packets that it sent (and received, for servers).

requirements.title: Validate transport parameters against connection ID values
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST validate that received transport parameters match received connection ID values.

requirements.title: Treat the absence of the initial_source_connection_id transport parameter from either endpoint or the absence of the original_destination_connection_id transport parameter from the server as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST treat the absence of the initial_source_connection_id transport parameter from either endpoint or the absence of the original_destination_connection_id transport parameter from the server as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.

requirements.title: The definition of a new transport parameter (Section 7
requirements.statement: The definition of a new transport parameter (Section 7.4.2) MUST specify whether storing the transport parameter for 0-RTT is mandatory, optional, or prohibited.

requirements.title: Use remembered values for the following parameters: ack_delay_exponent, max_ack_delay, initial_source_connection_id, original_destination_connection_id, preferred_address, retry_source_connection_id, and stateless_reset_token
requirements.statement: A client MUST NOT use remembered values for the following parameters: ack_delay_exponent, max_ack_delay, initial_source_connection_id, original_destination_connection_id, preferred_address, retry_source_connection_id, and stateless_reset_token.

requirements.title: Use server-provided 0-RTT transport parameter values
requirements.statement: The client MUST use the server's new values in the handshake instead; if the server does not provide new values, the default values are used.

requirements.title: Remember other processable server transport parameters
requirements.statement: A client that attempts to send 0-RTT data MUST remember all other transport parameters used by the server that it is able to process.

requirements.title: If 0-RTT data is accepted by the server, the server MUST NOT reduce any limits or alter any values that might be violated by the client with its 0-RTT data
requirements.statement: If 0-RTT data is accepted by the server, the server MUST NOT reduce any limits or alter any values that might be violated by the client with its 0-RTT data.

requirements.title: In particular, a server that accepts 0-RTT data MUST NOT set values for the following parameters (Section 18
requirements.statement: In particular, a server that accepts 0-RTT data MUST NOT set values for the following parameters (Section 18.2) that are smaller than the remembered values of the parameters.

requirements.title: Ignore unsupported transport parameters
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST ignore transport parameters that it does not support.

requirements.title: Treat invalid transport parameters as connection errors
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a transport parameter with an invalid value as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.

requirements.title: Send each transport parameter at most once
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send a parameter more than once in a given transport parameters extension.

requirements.title: Treat duplicate transport parameters as connection errors
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD treat receipt of duplicate transport parameters as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.

requirements.title: Buffer out-of-order CRYPTO frames
requirements.statement: Implementations MUST support buffering at least 4096 bytes of data received in out-of-order CRYPTO frames.

requirements.title: Choose to allow more data to be buffered during the handshake
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY choose to allow more data to be buffered during the handshake.

requirements.title: Close when handshake CRYPTO buffering is exceeded
requirements.statement: If an endpoint does not expand its buffer, it MUST close the connection with a CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code.

requirements.title: Containing discarded CRYPTO frames MUST be acknowledged because the packet has been received and processed by the transport even though the CRYPTO frame was discarded
requirements.statement: Packets containing discarded CRYPTO frames MUST be acknowledged because the packet has been received and processed by the transport even though the CRYPTO frame was discarded.

requirements.title: Construct tokens for server provenance
requirements.statement: A token sent in a NEW_TOKEN frame or a Retry packet MUST be constructed in a way that allows the server to identify how it was provided to a client.

requirements.title: Provide clients with an address validation token during one connection that can be used on a subsequent connection
requirements.statement: A server MAY provide clients with an address validation token during one connection that can be used on a subsequent connection.

requirements.title: When a server receives an Initial packet with an address validation token, it MUST attempt to validate the token, unless it has already completed address validation
requirements.statement: When a server receives an Initial packet with an address validation token, it MUST attempt to validate the token, unless it has already completed address validation.

requirements.title: If the token is invalid, then the server SHOULD proceed as if the client did not have a validated address, including potentially sending a Retry packet
requirements.statement: If the token is invalid, then the server SHOULD proceed as if the client did not have a validated address, including potentially sending a Retry packet.

requirements.title: Allow the handshake to proceed after successful validation
requirements.statement: If the validation succeeds, the server SHOULD then allow the handshake to proceed.

requirements.title: Include the token in all Initial packets it sends, unless a Retry replaces the token with a newer one
requirements.statement: The client MUST include the token in all Initial packets it sends, unless a Retry replaces the token with a newer one.

requirements.title: Do not use Retry tokens for future connections
requirements.statement: The client MUST NOT use the token provided in a Retry for future connections.

requirements.title: Discard Initial packets without expected token
requirements.statement: Servers MAY discard any Initial packet that does not carry the expected token.

requirements.title: Thus, a token SHOULD have an expiration time, which could be either an explicit expiration time or an issued timestamp that can be used to dynamically calculate the expiration time
requirements.statement: Thus, a token SHOULD have an expiration time, which could be either an explicit expiration time or an issued timestamp that can be used to dynamically calculate the expiration time.

requirements.title: Issued with NEW_TOKEN MUST NOT include information that would allow values to be linked by an observer to the connection on which it was issued
requirements.statement: A token issued with NEW_TOKEN MUST NOT include information that would allow values to be linked by an observer to the connection on which it was issued.

requirements.title: Ensure that every NEW_TOKEN frame it sends is unique across all clients, with the exception of those sent to repair losses of previously sent NEW_TOKEN frames
requirements.statement: A server MUST ensure that every NEW_TOKEN frame it sends is unique across all clients, with the exception of those sent to repair losses of previously sent NEW_TOKEN frames.

requirements.title: Information that allows the server to distinguish between tokens from Retry and NEW_TOKEN MAY be accessible to entities other than the server
requirements.statement: Information that allows the server to distinguish between tokens from Retry and NEW_TOKEN MAY be accessible to entities other than the server.

requirements.title: Include applicable unused tokens in Initial packets
requirements.statement: When connecting to a server for which the client retains an applicable and unused token, it SHOULD include that token in the Token field of its Initial packet.

requirements.title: Include a token that is not applicable to the server that it is connecting to, unless the client has the knowledge that the server that issued the token and the server the client is connecting to are jointly managing the tokens
requirements.statement: A client MUST NOT include a token that is not applicable to the server that it is connecting to, unless the client has the knowledge that the server that issued the token and the server the client is connecting to are jointly managing the tokens.

requirements.title: Tokens from prior connections may be reused
requirements.statement: A client MAY use a token from any previous connection to that server.

requirements.title: Reuse a token from a NEW_TOKEN frame for different connection attempts
requirements.statement: A client SHOULD NOT reuse a token from a NEW_TOKEN frame for different connection attempts.

requirements.title: Make address validation tokens hard to guess
requirements.statement: An address validation token MUST be difficult to guess.

requirements.title: For this design to work, the token MUST be covered by integrity protection against modification or falsification by clients
requirements.statement: For this design to work, the token MUST be covered by integrity protection against modification or falsification by clients.

requirements.title: Include source-address continuity information in Retry tokens
requirements.statement: Tokens sent in Retry packets SHOULD include information that allows the server to verify that the source IP address and port in client packets remain constant.

requirements.title: Include client-address continuity information in NEW_TOKEN frames
requirements.statement: Tokens sent in NEW_TOKEN frames MUST include information that allows the server to verify that the client IP address has not changed from when the token was issued.

requirements.title: Servers SHOULD ensure that tokens sent in Retry packets are only accepted for a short time, as they are returned immediately by clients
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD ensure that tokens sent in Retry packets are only accepted for a short time, as they are returned immediately by clients.

requirements.title: Additionally, an endpoint MAY consider the peer address validated if the peer uses a connection ID chosen by the endpoint and the connection ID contains at least 64 bits of entropy
requirements.statement: Additionally, an endpoint MAY consider the peer address validated if the peer uses a connection ID chosen by the endpoint and the connection ID contains at least 64 bits of entropy.

requirements.title: Prior to validating the client address, servers MUST NOT send more than three times as many bytes as the number of bytes they have received
requirements.statement: Prior to validating the client address, servers MUST NOT send more than three times as many bytes as the number of bytes they have received.

requirements.title: For the purposes of avoiding amplification prior to address validation, servers MUST count all of the payload bytes received in datagrams that are uniquely attributed to a single connection
requirements.statement: For the purposes of avoiding amplification prior to address validation, servers MUST count all of the payload bytes received in datagrams that are uniquely attributed to a single connection.

requirements.title: Pad Initial datagrams to 1200 bytes
requirements.statement: Clients MUST ensure that UDP datagrams containing Initial packets have UDP payloads of at least 1200 bytes, adding PADDING frames as necessary.

requirements.title: To prevent this deadlock, clients MUST send a packet on a Probe Timeout (PTO)
requirements.statement: To prevent this deadlock, clients MUST send a packet on a Probe Timeout (PTO); see Section 6.2 of [QUIC-RECOVERY].

requirements.title: Send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames to guard against packet loss
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames to guard against packet loss.

requirements.title: However, an endpoint SHOULD NOT send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in a single packet
requirements.statement: However, an endpoint SHOULD NOT send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in a single packet.

requirements.title: Limit PATH_CHALLENGE probe frequency
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD NOT probe a new path with packets containing a PATH_CHALLENGE frame more frequently than it would send an Initial packet.

requirements.title: Use unpredictable data in every PATH_CHALLENGE frame so that it can associate the peer's response with the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE
requirements.statement: The endpoint MUST use unpredictable data in every PATH_CHALLENGE frame so that it can associate the peer's response with the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE.

requirements.title: Expand datagrams that contain a PATH_CHALLENGE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes, unless the anti-amplification limit for the path does not permit sending a datagram of this size
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST expand datagrams that contain a PATH_CHALLENGE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes, unless the anti-amplification limit for the path does not permit sending a datagram of this size.

requirements.title: To ensure that the path MTU is large enough, the endpoint MUST perform a second path validation by sending a PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a datagram of at least 1200 bytes
requirements.statement: To ensure that the path MTU is large enough, the endpoint MUST perform a second path validation by sending a PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a datagram of at least 1200 bytes.

requirements.title: Unlike other cases where datagrams are expanded, endpoints MUST NOT discard datagrams that appear to be too small when they contain PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE
requirements.statement: Unlike other cases where datagrams are expanded, endpoints MUST NOT discard datagrams that appear to be too small when they contain PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE.

requirements.title: On receiving a PATH_CHALLENGE frame, an endpoint MUST respond by echoing the data contained in the PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a PATH_RESPONSE frame
requirements.statement: On receiving a PATH_CHALLENGE frame, an endpoint MUST respond by echoing the data contained in the PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a PATH_RESPONSE frame.

requirements.title: Delay transmission of a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame unless constrained by congestion control
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT delay transmission of a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame unless constrained by congestion control.

requirements.title: Send PATH_RESPONSE on the received path
requirements.statement: A PATH_RESPONSE frame MUST be sent on the network path where the PATH_CHALLENGE frame was received.

requirements.title: This requirement MUST NOT be enforced by the endpoint that initiates path validation, as that would enable an attack on migration
requirements.statement: This requirement MUST NOT be enforced by the endpoint that initiates path validation, as that would enable an attack on migration; see Section 9.3.3.

requirements.title: Expand datagrams that contain a PATH_RESPONSE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST expand datagrams that contain a PATH_RESPONSE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes.

requirements.title: However, an endpoint MUST NOT expand the datagram containing the PATH_RESPONSE if the resulting data exceeds the anti-amplification limit
requirements.statement: However, an endpoint MUST NOT expand the datagram containing the PATH_RESPONSE if the resulting data exceeds the anti-amplification limit.

requirements.title: However, the endpoint MUST initiate another path validation with an expanded datagram to verify that the path supports the required MTU
requirements.statement: However, the endpoint MUST initiate another path validation with an expanded datagram to verify that the path supports the required MTU.

requirements.title: Abandon path validation on a timer
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD abandon path validation based on a timer.

requirements.title: Allow other frames alongside path validation frames
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY include other frames with the PATH_CHALLENGE and PATH_RESPONSE frames used for path validation.

requirements.title: Limit sending to unvalidated addresses
requirements.statement: After receiving packets from an address that is not yet validated, an endpoint MUST limit the amount of data it sends to the unvalidated address to three times the amount of data received from that address.

requirements.title: Validate ECN Capability After Migration
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST validate ECN capability as described in Section 13.4 when it migrates to a new path.

requirements.title: Limit Sending Until Address Validation
requirements.statement: Until a peer's address is deemed valid, an endpoint MUST limit the amount of data it sends to that address.

requirements.title: Validate the previously active path with PATH_CHALLENGE
requirements.statement: In response to an apparent migration, endpoints MUST validate the previously active path using a PATH_CHALLENGE frame.

requirements.title: Respond to PATH_CHALLENGE on active paths with a non-probing packet
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives a PATH_CHALLENGE on an active path SHOULD send a non-probing packet in response.

requirements.title: Send subsequent packets to the new peer address
requirements.statement: If the recipient permits the migration, it MUST send subsequent packets to the new peer address.

requirements.title: Change the send address only in response to the highest-numbered non-probing packet
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST only change the address to which it sends packets in response to the highest-numbered non-probing packet.

requirements.title: Allow data on an unvalidated peer address
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY send data to an unvalidated peer address.

requirements.title: Skip validation of a peer address if that address has been seen recently
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY skip validation of a peer address if that address has been seen recently.

requirements.title: After verifying a new client address, the server SHOULD send new address validation tokens (Section 8) to the client
requirements.statement: After verifying a new client address, the server SHOULD send new address validation tokens (Section 8) to the client.

requirements.title: Sent on the old path MUST NOT contribute to congestion control or RTT estimation for the new path
requirements.statement: Packets sent on the old path MUST NOT contribute to congestion control or RTT estimation for the new path.

requirements.title: Use updated congestion state only after confirming the peer address
requirements.statement: On confirming a peer's ownership of its new address, an endpoint MUST immediately reset the congestion controller and round-trip time estimator for the new path to initial values unless the only change in the peer's address is its port number.

requirements.title: Allow Probe-Packet Loss Exceptions
requirements.statement: A sender MAY make exceptions for probe packets so their loss detection is independent and does not unduly cause the congestion controller to reduce its sending rate.

requirements.title: Allow a Separate PATH_CHALLENGE Timer
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY set a separate timer when a PATH_CHALLENGE is sent, and the timer is canceled if the corresponding PATH_RESPONSE is received.

requirements.title: Allow Retrying PATH_CHALLENGE on Timeout
requirements.statement: If the timer fires before the PATH_RESPONSE is received, an endpoint MAY send a new PATH_CHALLENGE and restart the timer for a longer period of time.

requirements.title: Set timer as described in QUIC-RECOVERY
requirements.statement: This timer SHOULD be set as described in Section 6.2.1 of [QUIC-RECOVERY].

requirements.title: Do Not Make the PATH_CHALLENGE Timer More Aggressive
requirements.statement: This timer MUST NOT be more aggressive.

requirements.title: Keep Provided Connection IDs Unlinkable
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST ensure that connection IDs they provide cannot be linked by any other entity.

requirements.title: At any time, endpoints MAY change the Destination Connection ID they transmit with to a value that has not been used on another path
requirements.statement: At any time, endpoints MAY change the Destination Connection ID they transmit with to a value that has not been used on another path.

requirements.title: Do not reuse a connection ID across multiple local addresses
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT reuse a connection ID when sending from more than one local address.

requirements.title: Prevent connection-id reuse across destination addresses
requirements.statement: Similarly, an endpoint MUST NOT reuse a connection ID when sending to more than one destination address.

requirements.title: Keep using the original server address after failed validation
requirements.statement: If path validation fails, the client MUST continue sending all future packets to the server's original IP address.

requirements.title: Move Exclusively to the Preferred Address After Validation
requirements.statement: Once the server has completed path validation and has received a non-probing packet with a new largest packet number on its preferred address, the server MUST send non-probing packets to the client exclusively from its preferred IP address.

requirements.title: Probe toward the client from the preferred address
requirements.statement: The server MUST probe on the path toward the client from its preferred address.

requirements.title: Drop newer packets received on the old IP address
requirements.statement: The server SHOULD drop newer packets for this connection that are received on the old IP address.

requirements.title: Continue processing delayed packets on the old IP address
requirements.statement: The server MAY continue to process delayed packets that are received on the old IP address.

requirements.title: Validate both server addresses concurrently after client migration
requirements.statement: In this case, the client SHOULD perform path validation to both the original and preferred server address from the client's new address concurrently.

requirements.title: Abandon validation after preferred address validation succeeds
requirements.statement: If path validation of the server's preferred address succeeds, the client MUST abandon validation of the original address and migrate to using the server's preferred address.

requirements.title: Optionally migrate after original address validation succeeds
requirements.statement: If path validation of the server's preferred address fails but validation of the server's original address succeeds, the client MAY migrate to its new address and continue sending to the server's original address.

requirements.title: Prefer the same address family for client migration
requirements.statement: A client that migrates to a new address SHOULD use a preferred address from the same address family for the server.

requirements.title: Handle prohibited migration packets
requirements.statement: If the peer violates this requirement, the endpoint MUST either drop the incoming packets on that path without generating a Stateless Reset or proceed with path validation and allow the peer to migrate.

requirements.title: Allow discarding state without a validated path
requirements.statement: When an endpoint has no validated path on which to send packets, it MAY discard connection state.

requirements.title: Permit waiting before state discard
requirements.statement: An endpoint capable of connection migration MAY wait for a new path to become available before discarding connection state.

requirements.title: Forbid local key updates before handshake confirmation
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT initiate a key update before confirming the handshake.

requirements.title: Gate repeated local updates on current-phase acknowledgment
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT initiate another key update until it has received an acknowledgment for a packet protected with keys from the current key phase.

requirements.title: Update receive keys when initiating a key update
requirements.statement: The endpoint that initiates a key update MUST also update the keys it uses for receiving packets.

requirements.title: Update send keys after peer-initiated key updates
requirements.statement: If a peer initiates a key update, the endpoint MUST update its send keys to the corresponding key phase before sending an acknowledgment for a packet that was received with updated keys.

requirements.title: Allow KEY_UPDATE_ERROR for unconfirmed consecutive peer updates
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY treat consecutive peer key updates that occur before confirmation of the prior update as a connection error of type KEY_UPDATE_ERROR.

requirements.title: Allow KEY_UPDATE_ERROR for old-key ACKs of newer-key packets
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY treat an acknowledgment carried in an old-key packet that acknowledges a newer-key packet as a connection error of type KEY_UPDATE_ERROR.

requirements.title: Avoid timing signals for invalid Key Phase bits
requirements.statement: Endpoints responding to an apparent key update MUST NOT generate a timing signal that reveals whether the Key Phase bit was invalid.

requirements.title: Retain current and next receive keys
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST be able to retain two sets of receive packet protection keys: the current keys and the next keys.

requirements.title: Never send packets with old keys
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send packets protected with old keys.

requirements.title: Protect higher packet numbers with same or newer keys
requirements.statement: Packets with higher packet numbers MUST be protected with the same or newer packet protection keys than packets with lower packet numbers.

requirements.title: Reject old-key packets that violate packet-number ordering
requirements.statement: If an endpoint successfully removes protection with old keys after newer keys were used for lower packet numbers, it MUST treat that condition as a connection error of type KEY_UPDATE_ERROR.

requirements.title: Wait before initiating another key update after confirmation
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD wait three times the PTO before initiating a key update after receiving the acknowledgment that confirms the previous key update.

requirements.title: Limit old read key retention to three PTOs
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD retain old read keys for no more than three times the PTO after receiving a packet protected with the new keys.

requirements.title: Count encrypted packets per key set
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST count the number of encrypted packets for each set of packet protection keys.

requirements.title: Stop using keys beyond the AEAD confidentiality limit
requirements.statement: If encrypted packet count with the same key exceeds the AEAD confidentiality limit, the endpoint MUST stop using that key.

requirements.title: Initiate key updates before the AEAD confidentiality limit
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST initiate a key update before sending more protected packets than the selected AEAD confidentiality limit permits.

requirements.title: Suppress non-retained stateless-reset responses
requirements.statement: After AEAD-limit terminal discard, an endpoint MUST suppress stateless-reset response emission when a later received packet does not resolve to a retained route or resolves only to route state without a remembered stateless-reset token for the same remote address and port.

requirements.title: Gate retained-route stateless-reset responses
requirements.statement: After AEAD-limit terminal discard, an endpoint MUST emit a stateless reset for a later received packet only when the packet resolves to a retained route linked to a remembered stateless-reset token for the same remote address and port and the loop-prevention and emission-rate gates permit the response; otherwise it suppresses the response.

requirements.title: Suppress reset responses to known reset triggers
requirements.statement: After AEAD-limit terminal discard, when a later retained-route trigger has Stateless Reset shape and its trailing token matches the retained token for the same remote address and port, the endpoint MUST suppress stateless-reset response emission rather than emitting another stateless reset.

requirements.title: Allow key update after handshake confirmation
requirements.statement: Once the handshake is confirmed, an endpoint MAY initiate a key update.

requirements.title: Let Key Phase detect key changes
requirements.statement: The Key Phase bit MUST allow a recipient to detect a change in keying material without needing to receive the first packet that triggered the change.

requirements.title: Update keys when Key Phase changes
requirements.statement: An endpoint that notices a changed Key Phase bit MUST update keys.

requirements.title: Decrypt the packet with the changed Key Phase
requirements.statement: An endpoint that notices a changed Key Phase bit MUST decrypt the packet that contains the changed value.

requirements.title: Update both endpoints on key update
requirements.statement: Initiating a key update MUST result in both endpoints updating keys.

requirements.title: Prohibit TLS KeyUpdate messages
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST NOT send a TLS KeyUpdate message.

requirements.title: Treat TLS KeyUpdate as a connection error
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST treat the receipt of a TLS KeyUpdate message as a connection error of type 0x010a, equivalent to a fatal TLS alert of unexpected_message.

requirements.title: Use caution with unauthenticated Initial data
requirements.statement: Implementations SHOULD use caution when relying on any data contained in Initial packets that is not otherwise authenticated.

requirements.title: Indicate encryption level in packet headers
requirements.statement: The packet-level header MUST indicate the encryption level.

requirements.title: Carry packet numbers in packet headers
requirements.statement: The packet-level header MUST include a packet sequence number.

requirements.title: Map encryption level to packet number space
requirements.statement: The encryption level MUST indicate the packet number space.

requirements.title: Prohibit packet number reuse
requirements.statement: Packet numbers MUST NOT repeat within a packet number space for the lifetime of a connection.

requirements.title: Send packet numbers monotonically
requirements.statement: Packet numbers MUST be sent in monotonically increasing order within a space.

requirements.title: Allow intentional packet number gaps
requirements.statement: Some packet numbers MAY never be used, leaving intentional gaps.

requirements.title: Initialize min_rtt from the first sample
requirements.statement: min_rtt MUST be set to latest_rtt on the first RTT sample.

requirements.title: Update min_rtt on later samples
requirements.statement: On all RTT samples after the first, min_rtt MUST be set to the lesser of min_rtt and latest_rtt.

requirements.title: Refresh min_rtt after persistent congestion
requirements.statement: Endpoints SHOULD set min_rtt to the newest RTT sample after persistent congestion is established.

requirements.title: Allow opportunistic min_rtt reestablishment
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY reestablish min_rtt at other times in the connection, such as when traffic volume is low and an acknowledgment is received with a low acknowledgment delay.

requirements.title: Avoid over-refreshing min_rtt
requirements.statement: Implementations SHOULD NOT refresh the min_rtt value too often.

requirements.title: Initialize smoothed RTT to the initial RTT
requirements.statement: `smoothed_rtt` is initialized to `kInitialRtt`.

requirements.title: Initialize RTT variation to half the initial RTT
requirements.statement: `rttvar` is initialized to `kInitialRtt / 2`.

requirements.title: Update RTT estimates on subsequent samples
requirements.statement: On subsequent RTT samples, an endpoint MUST set adjusted_rtt to latest_rtt - ack_delay when latest_rtt is at least min_rtt + ack_delay and otherwise set adjusted_rtt to latest_rtt, then update smoothed_rtt to 7/8 of its prior value plus 1/8 of adjusted_rtt and update rttvar to 3/4 of its prior value plus 1/4 of abs(smoothed_rtt - adjusted_rtt).

requirements.title: Seed smoothed RTT from the first RTT sample
requirements.statement: `smoothed_rtt` is set to `latest_rtt` on the first RTT sample after initialization.

requirements.title: Seed RTT variation from the first RTT sample
requirements.statement: `rttvar` is set to `latest_rtt / 2` on the first RTT sample after initialization.

requirements.title: Ignore max_ack_delay before handshake confirmation
requirements.statement: The endpoint SHOULD ignore max_ack_delay until the handshake is confirmed.

requirements.title: Allow dropping some adjusted samples
requirements.statement: Before handshake confirmation, an endpoint MAY ignore an RTT sample if adjusting the sample for acknowledgment delay would make it smaller than min_rtt.

requirements.title: Recommend a packet threshold of three
requirements.statement: The initial value for the packet reordering threshold (kPacketThreshold) is RECOMMENDED to be 3.

requirements.title: Avoid packet thresholds below three
requirements.statement: Implementations SHOULD NOT use a packet threshold less than 3.

requirements.title: Declare earlier packets lost after sufficient time
requirements.statement: Once a later packet within the same packet number space has been acknowledged, an endpoint SHOULD declare an earlier packet lost if it was sent a threshold amount of time in the past.

requirements.title: Bound the time threshold by timer granularity
requirements.statement: To avoid declaring packets lost too early, the time threshold MUST be at least the local timer granularity.

requirements.title: Keep PTO above granularity
requirements.statement: The PTO period MUST be at least kGranularity.

requirements.title: Use the earlier PTO across Initial and Handshake spaces
requirements.statement: When ack-eliciting packets in multiple packet number spaces are in flight, the PTO timer MUST be set to the earlier value of the Initial and Handshake packet number spaces.

requirements.title: Defer application-data PTO until handshake confirmation
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT set its PTO timer for the Application Data packet number space until the handshake is confirmed.

requirements.title: Restart PTO on send, acknowledgment, or key discard
requirements.statement: A sender SHOULD restart its PTO timer every time an ack-eliciting packet is sent or acknowledged, or when Initial or Handshake keys are discarded.

requirements.title: Delay server PTO until address validation traffic arrives
requirements.statement: If no additional data can be sent, the server's PTO timer MUST NOT be armed until datagrams have been received from the client.

requirements.title: Arm the client PTO before handshake confirmation
requirements.statement: The client MUST set the PTO timer if it has not received an acknowledgment for any of its Handshake packets and the handshake is not confirmed, even if there are no packets in flight.

requirements.title: Send Handshake probes when keys are available
requirements.statement: When the PTO fires, the client MUST send a Handshake packet if it has Handshake keys.

requirements.title: Send Initial probes otherwise
requirements.statement: When the PTO fires and the client does not have Handshake keys, it MUST send an Initial packet in a UDP datagram with a payload of at least 1200 bytes.

requirements.title: Reuse prior-smoothed RTT on resumed connections
requirements.statement: Resumed connections over the same network MAY use the previous connection's final smoothed RTT value as the resumed connection's initial RTT.

requirements.title: Default initial RTT to 333 milliseconds
requirements.statement: When no previous RTT is available, the initial RTT SHOULD be set to 333 milliseconds.

requirements.title: Use PATH_CHALLENGE and PATH_RESPONSE timing for initial RTT
requirements.statement: A connection MAY use the delay between sending a PATH_CHALLENGE and receiving a PATH_RESPONSE to set the initial RTT for a new path.

requirements.title: Do not treat PATH_CHALLENGE/PATH_RESPONSE delay as an RTT sample
requirements.statement: That delay SHOULD NOT be considered an RTT sample.

requirements.title: Reset timers when keys are discarded
requirements.statement: When Initial or Handshake keys are discarded, the PTO and loss detection timers MUST be reset.

requirements.title: Permit early CRYPTO probes for handshake speedup
requirements.statement: To speed up handshake completion under these conditions, an endpoint MAY, for a limited number of times per connection, send a packet containing unacknowledged CRYPTO data earlier than PTO expiry, subject to the address-validation limits.

requirements.title: Probe with at least one ack-eliciting packet
requirements.statement: When a PTO timer expires, a sender MUST send at least one ack-eliciting packet in the packet number space as a probe.

requirements.title: Allow two full-sized PTO datagrams
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY send up to two full-sized datagrams containing ack-eliciting packets to avoid an expensive consecutive PTO expiration due to a single lost datagram or to transmit data from multiple packet number spaces.

requirements.title: Keep PTO probe packets ack-eliciting
requirements.statement: All probe packets sent on a PTO MUST be ack-eliciting.

requirements.title: Use other packet number spaces for PTO probes
requirements.statement: In addition to sending data in the packet number space for which the timer expired, the sender SHOULD send ack-eliciting packets from other packet number spaces with in-flight data, coalescing packets if possible.

requirements.title: Include new data in PTO probes
requirements.statement: An endpoint SHOULD include new data in packets that are sent on PTO expiration.

requirements.title: Allow previously sent data in PTO probes
requirements.statement: Previously sent data MAY be sent if no new data can be sent.

requirements.title: Allow alternative probe-content strategies
requirements.statement: Implementations MAY use alternative strategies for determining the content of probe packets, including sending new or retransmitted data based on the application's priorities.

requirements.title: Send a PING when no probe data exists
requirements.statement: When there is no data to send, the sender SHOULD send a PING or other ack-eliciting frame in a single packet, rearming the PTO timer.

requirements.title: Allow declaring in-flight packets lost instead of probing
requirements.statement: Instead of sending an ack-eliciting packet, the sender MAY mark any packets still in flight as lost.

requirements.title: Do not infer loss from PTO expiration
requirements.statement: A PTO timer expiration MUST NOT cause prior unacknowledged packets to be marked as lost.

requirements.title: Reset recovery and congestion state on Retry
requirements.statement: Clients that receive a Retry packet MUST reset congestion control and loss recovery state, including any pending timers.

requirements.title: Retain cryptographic handshake state across Retry
requirements.statement: Clients MUST retain other connection state, in particular cryptographic handshake messages.

requirements.title: Permit RTT estimation from Retry timing
requirements.statement: The client MAY compute an RTT estimate to the server as the time period from when the first Initial packet was sent to when a Retry or Version Negotiation packet is received.

requirements.title: Allow using Retry-derived RTT as the initial RTT
requirements.statement: The client MAY use this value in place of its default for the initial RTT estimate.

requirements.title: Discard recovery state when protection keys go away
requirements.statement: The sender MUST discard all recovery state associated with packets sent with discarded Initial or Handshake keys.

requirements.title: Remove discarded packets from bytes in flight
requirements.statement: The sender MUST remove those packets from the count of bytes in flight.

requirements.title: Discard recovery state for rejected 0-RTT packets
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST discard recovery state for all in-flight 0-RTT packets when 0-RTT is rejected.

requirements.title: Recompute the initial window when datagram size changes
requirements.statement: If the maximum datagram size changes during the connection, the initial congestion window SHOULD be recalculated with the new size.

requirements.title: Reset the initial window after handshake-driven MTU reduction
requirements.statement: If the maximum datagram size is decreased in order to complete the handshake, the congestion window SHOULD be set to the new initial congestion window.

requirements.title: Recommend a two-packet minimum congestion window
requirements.statement: The minimum congestion window SHOULD be 2 * max_datagram_size.

requirements.title: Enter recovery on loss or ECN-CE increase
requirements.statement: A sender MUST enter a recovery period when it detects packet loss or when the ECN-CE count reported by its peer increases.

requirements.title: Cut the slow start threshold on recovery entry
requirements.statement: On entering a recovery period, a sender MUST set the slow start threshold to half the congestion window when loss is detected.

requirements.title: Restore congestion window before leaving recovery
requirements.statement: The congestion window MUST be set to the reduced value of the slow start threshold before exiting the recovery period.

requirements.title: Permit gentler recovery-window reduction
requirements.statement: Implementations MAY reduce the congestion window immediately upon entering a recovery period or use other mechanisms, such as Proportional Rate Reduction, to reduce the congestion window more gradually.

requirements.title: Hold the congestion window steady during recovery
requirements.statement: During a recovery period, the congestion window MUST NOT change in response to new losses or increases in the ECN-CE count.

requirements.title: Leave recovery when a recovery-period packet is acknowledged
requirements.statement: A recovery period MUST end and the sender enter congestion avoidance when a packet sent during the recovery period is acknowledged.

requirements.title: Limit congestion-avoidance growth to one datagram per acknowledged window
requirements.statement: A sender in congestion avoidance MUST limit the increase to the congestion window to at most one maximum datagram size for each congestion window that is acknowledged.

requirements.title: Ignore undecryptable packet loss before keys are available
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY ignore the loss of Handshake, 0-RTT, and 1-RTT packets that might have arrived before the peer had packet protection keys to process those packets.

requirements.title: Do not ignore later packet loss
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST NOT ignore the loss of packets that were sent after the earliest acknowledged packet in a given packet number space.

requirements.title: Do not block probe packets with congestion control
requirements.statement: Probe packets MUST NOT be blocked by the congestion controller.

requirements.title: Count probe packets as additional flight
requirements.statement: A sender MUST count these packets as being additionally in flight.

requirements.title: Delay persistent congestion until at least one RTT sample exists
requirements.statement: Persistent congestion SHOULD NOT start until there is at least one RTT sample.

requirements.title: Reset cwnd to the minimum on persistent congestion
requirements.statement: When persistent congestion is declared, the sender's congestion window MUST be reduced to the minimum congestion window.

requirements.title: Pace all in-flight packets
requirements.statement: A sender SHOULD pace sending of all in-flight packets based on input from the congestion controller.

requirements.title: Either pace or cap bursts
requirements.statement: Senders MUST either use pacing or limit such bursts.

requirements.title: Limit bursts to the initial congestion window
requirements.statement: Senders SHOULD limit bursts to the initial congestion window.

requirements.title: Allow larger bursts when the path can absorb them
requirements.statement: A sender with knowledge that the network path can absorb larger bursts MAY use a higher limit.

requirements.title: Do not pace pure ACK packets
requirements.statement: Packets containing only ACK frames SHOULD therefore not be paced.

requirements.title: Do not increase cwnd when underutilized
requirements.statement: When bytes in flight is smaller than the congestion window and sending is not pacing limited, the congestion window SHOULD NOT be increased in either slow start or congestion avoidance.

requirements.title: Do not call yourself application-limited because of pacing delay
requirements.statement: A sender SHOULD NOT consider itself application limited if it would have fully utilized the congestion window without pacing delay.

requirements.title: Allow alternate cwnd-updating mechanisms after underutilization
requirements.statement: A sender MAY implement alternative mechanisms to update its congestion window after periods of underutilization, such as those proposed for TCP in RFC 7661.

requirements.title: Require alternate controllers to obey RFC 8085
requirements.statement: If a sender uses a different controller than the one specified in this document, the chosen controller MUST conform to the congestion-control guidelines in Section 3.1 of RFC 8085.

requirements.title: Respect the bytes-in-flight ceiling
requirements.statement: An endpoint MUST NOT send a packet if it would cause bytes_in_flight to be larger than the congestion window, unless the packet is sent on a PTO timer expiration or when entering recovery.

requirements.title: Respond to unsupported Extended CONNECT protocols
requirements.statement: If a server advertises support for Extended CONNECT but receives an Extended CONNECT request with an unknown or unsupported ":protocol" value, the server SHOULD respond with a 501 (Not Implemented) status code.

requirements.title: Provide optional problem-details information
requirements.statement: A server MAY provide more information via a "problem details" response.

requirements.title: Listen on UDP port 853 by default
requirements.statement: A DNS server that supports DoQ MUST listen for and accept QUIC connections on the dedicated UDP port 853, unless there is a mutual agreement to use another port.

requirements.title: Connect to UDP port 853 by default
requirements.statement: A DNS client desiring to use DoQ with a particular server MUST establish a QUIC connection to UDP port 853 on the server, unless there is a mutual agreement to use another port.

requirements.title: Disallow UDP port 53
requirements.statement: A DoQ connection MUST NOT use UDP port 53.

requirements.title: Indicate DoQ support with ALPN token doq
requirements.statement: During connection establishment, DoQ support MUST be indicated by selecting the Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) token "doq" in the crypto handshake.

requirements.title: Generate Message ID when forwarding from DoQ
requirements.statement: When forwarding a DNS message from DoQ over another transport, a DNS Message ID MUST be generated according to the rules of the protocol that is in use.

requirements.title: Set Message ID to zero when forwarding to DoQ
requirements.statement: When forwarding a DNS message from another transport over DoQ, the Message ID MUST be set to 0.

requirements.title: Encode DNS messages with a 2-octet length field
requirements.statement: All DNS messages sent over DoQ connections MUST be encoded as a 2-octet length field followed by the message content as specified in [RFC1035].

requirements.title: Select the next available client-initiated bidirectional stream
requirements.statement: The client MUST select the next available client-initiated bidirectional stream for each subsequent query on a QUIC connection.

requirements.title: Process queries as they arrive
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD process queries as they arrive.

requirements.title: Send DNS query on selected stream
requirements.statement: A client MUST send the DNS query over the selected stream.

requirements.title: Signal end of client stream with STREAM FIN
requirements.statement: A client MUST indicate through the STREAM FIN mechanism that no further data will be sent on that stream.

requirements.title: Send responses on the same stream
requirements.statement: The server MUST send the response(s) on the same stream.

requirements.title: Signal end of server stream with STREAM FIN
requirements.statement: The server MUST indicate, after the last response, through the STREAM FIN mechanism that no further data will be sent on that stream.

requirements.title: Allow deferred processing until client STREAM FIN
requirements.statement: A server MAY defer processing of a query until the STREAM FIN has been indicated on the stream selected by the client.

requirements.title: Prefer DOQ_REQUEST_CANCELLED for cancellation
requirements.statement: A DoQ client that cancels an outstanding request SHOULD use the error code DOQ_REQUEST_CANCELLED.

requirements.title: Use registered specific error code
requirements.statement: A DoQ client MAY use a more specific error code registered according to Section 8.4.

requirements.title: Abandon corresponding DNS transaction
requirements.statement: The corresponding DNS transaction MUST be abandoned.

requirements.title: Discard response after late STOP_SENDING
requirements.statement: If the server response has already been sent, the client MUST discard the incoming response.

requirements.title: Stop processing after STOP_SENDING
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD NOT continue processing a DNS transaction if they receive a STOP_SENDING.

requirements.title: Limit cancellation request volume
requirements.statement: Servers MAY impose implementation limits on the total number or rate of cancellation requests.

requirements.title: Close connection on cancellation limits
requirements.statement: If limits are encountered, servers MAY close the connection.

requirements.title: Use DOQ_EXCESSIVE_LOAD for debugging
requirements.statement: Servers wanting to help client debugging MAY use the error code DOQ_EXCESSIVE_LOAD.

requirements.title: Stop processing on early RESET_STREAM
requirements.statement: Servers MUST NOT continue processing a DNS transaction if they receive a RESET_STREAM request from the client before the client indicates the STREAM FIN.

requirements.title: Issue RESET_STREAM unless already reset or response complete
requirements.statement: The server MUST issue a RESET_STREAM to indicate that the transaction is abandoned unless it has already done so for another reason or it has already sent the response and indicated the STREAM FIN.

requirements.title: Notify client of SERVFAIL with SERVFAIL response
requirements.statement: A client SHOULD be notified of SERVFAIL through a response whose Response Code is set to SERVFAIL.

requirements.title: Issue RESET_STREAM on internal error
requirements.statement: If a server cannot send a DNS response because of an internal error, it SHOULD issue a QUIC RESET_STREAM frame.

requirements.title: Set RESET_STREAM error code to DOQ_INTERNAL_ERROR
requirements.statement: The error code SHOULD be set to DOQ_INTERNAL_ERROR.

requirements.title: Abandon the corresponding DNS transaction
requirements.statement: The corresponding DNS transaction MUST be abandoned.

requirements.title: Limit unsolicited RESET_STREAM frames before closing
requirements.statement: Clients MAY limit unsolicited QUIC RESET_STREAM frames received on a connection before closing it.

requirements.title: Protocol error: STREAM FIN before complete message
requirements.statement: If a client or server receives a STREAM FIN before receiving all the bytes for a message indicated in the 2-octet length field, it MUST treat this as a fatal error.

requirements.title: Treat unknown or unexpected error codes as unspecified
requirements.statement: An implementation MUST treat use of an error code in an unexpected context or receipt of an unknown error code as equivalent to DOQ_UNSPECIFIED_ERROR.

requirements.title: Monitor server idle time
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD monitor server idle time, defined as the time since the last packet from the server was received.

requirements.title: Check idle time before sending a query
requirements.statement: When a client prepares to send a new DNS query to the server, it SHOULD check whether the idle time is sufficiently lower than the idle timer.

requirements.title: Send query over existing connection when idle time permits
requirements.statement: If the client's idle time is sufficiently lower than the idle timer, the client SHOULD send the DNS query over the existing connection.

requirements.title: Open a new connection when idle time is not low enough
requirements.statement: If the client's idle time is not sufficiently lower than the idle timer, the client SHOULD establish a new connection and send the query over that connection.

requirements.title: Allow session resumption and 0-RTT when supported
requirements.statement: A client MAY use session resumption and 0-RTT if the server supports them.

requirements.title: Prohibit 0-RTT for non-replayable transactions
requirements.statement: The 0-RTT mechanism MUST NOT be used to send DNS requests that are not replayable transactions.

requirements.title: Classify QUERY and NOTIFY transactions as replayable
requirements.statement: Transactions with an OPCODE of QUERY or NOTIFY MUST be considered replayable.

requirements.title: Use a Strict usage profile for DoQ stubs
requirements.statement: DoQ stubs SHOULD use a Strict usage profile.

requirements.title: Opportunistic usage profile fallback
requirements.statement: An implementation using the Opportunistic usage profile SHOULD fall back to DoT or cleartext DNS if the DoQ connection attempt fails.

requirements.title: Back off after DoQ failure
requirements.statement: Implementations using the Opportunistic profile SHOULD back off from DoQ for at least the timeout value after the failure.

requirements.title: Use resumption tickets only once
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD use resumption tickets only once, as specified in Appendix C.4 of RFC8446.

requirements.title: Avoid resumption after connectivity changes
requirements.statement: By default, clients SHOULD NOT use session resumption if the client's connectivity has changed.

requirements.title: Use address validation tokens only with resumption
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD only use the address validation tokens when they are also using session resumption.

requirements.title: Issue long-lived resumption tickets
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD issue session resumption tickets with a sufficiently long lifetime.

requirements.title: Implement anti-replay mechanisms
requirements.statement: Servers SHOULD implement the anti-replay mechanisms specified in Section 8 of RFC8446.

requirements.title: Default to privacy-preserving new sessions
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD prioritize privacy and start new sessions when connectivity changes.

requirements.title: Send responses promptly on the specific stream
requirements.statement: A DoQ implementation SHOULD send responses on the specific stream as soon as possible, without waiting for availability of responses for previously opened streams.

requirements.title: Accept cleared QUIC-bit packets after transport-parameter processing
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives grease_quic_bit from a peer MUST accept packets whose QUIC Bit is 0 after it has received and processed that peer's transport parameters.

requirements.title: Limit SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM to 0 or 1
requirements.statement: The value of the SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting MUST be either 0 or 1.

requirements.title: Reject invalid SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM values
requirements.statement: If the SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting is received with any value other than 0 or 1, the receiver MUST terminate the connection with error H3_SETTINGS_ERROR.

requirements.title: Gate DATAGRAM frames on SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM
requirements.statement: QUIC DATAGRAM frames MUST NOT be sent until the SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting has been both sent and received with a value of 1.

requirements.title: Allow 0-RTT clients to store SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM
requirements.statement: When clients use 0-RTT, they MAY store the value of the server's SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting.

requirements.title: Send nondecreasing SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM when accepting 0-RTT
requirements.statement: When servers decide to accept 0-RTT data, they MUST send a SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting greater than or equal to the value they sent to the client in the connection where they sent the NewSessionTicket message.

requirements.title: Validate stored SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM during 0-RTT
requirements.statement: If a client stores the value of the SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting with its 0-RTT state, the client MUST validate that the new value of the SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting sent by the server in the handshake is greater than or equal to the stored value.

requirements.title: Terminate on lowered SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM
requirements.statement: If the validation fails, the client MUST terminate the connection with error H3_SETTINGS_ERROR.

requirements.title: Maximum SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM value
requirements.statement: The SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM setting parameter MUST NOT have a value greater than 1.

requirements.title: Allow empty HTTP Datagram Payload fields
requirements.statement: The HTTP Datagram Payload field MAY be empty.

requirements.title: Associate HTTP Datagrams only with supporting requests
requirements.statement: HTTP Datagrams MUST only be sent with an association to an HTTP request that explicitly supports them.

requirements.title: Terminate requests that receive unsupported HTTP Datagrams
requirements.statement: If an HTTP Datagram is received and it is associated with a request that has no known semantics for HTTP Datagrams, the receiver MUST terminate the request.

requirements.title: Abort HTTP/3 request streams on unsupported HTTP Datagrams
requirements.statement: If HTTP/3 is in use, the request stream MUST be aborted with H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR (0x33).

requirements.title: Allow HTTP extensions to override HTTP Datagram requirements
requirements.statement: HTTP extensions MAY override the HTTP Datagram requirements by defining a negotiation mechanism and semantics for HTTP Datagrams.

requirements.title: Capsule type encoding
requirements.statement: The Capsule Type field MUST be a variable-length integer indicating the type of the capsule.

requirements.title: Silently drop unknown capsules
requirements.statement: Endpoints that receive a Capsule with an unknown Capsule Type MUST silently drop that Capsule and skip over it to parse the next Capsule.

requirements.title: Map Capsule protocol errors to malformed HTTP messages
requirements.statement: A receiver that encounters an error processing the Capsule Protocol MUST treat it as a malformed or incomplete HTTP message.

requirements.title: Require exactly the fields defined for each Capsule payload
requirements.statement: Each Capsule's payload MUST contain exactly the fields identified in its description.

requirements.title: Treat extra or truncated Capsule payload fields as malformed
requirements.statement: A Capsule payload with extra bytes after the identified fields or truncated before their end MUST be treated as a malformed or incomplete message.

requirements.title: Verify redundant Capsule length encodings are self-consistent
requirements.statement: Redundant length encodings MUST be verified to be self-consistent.

requirements.title: Treat truncated capsules after clean stream termination as malformed
requirements.statement: If a Capsule stream is cleanly terminated and its last Capsule is truncated, this MUST be treated as a malformed or incomplete message.

requirements.title: Treat non-Boolean Capsule-Protocol values as absent
requirements.statement: Recipients MUST handle any other Capsule-Protocol value type as if the field were not present.

requirements.title: Ignore unknown Capsule-Protocol parameters
requirements.statement: Receivers MUST ignore unknown parameters.

requirements.title: Allow intermediaries to process unknown upgrade tokens
requirements.statement: Intermediaries MAY use the Capsule-Protocol header field to allow processing of HTTP Datagrams for unknown HTTP upgrade tokens.

requirements.title: Prohibit Capsule-Protocol on disallowed HTTP responses
requirements.statement: The Capsule-Protocol header field MUST NOT be used on HTTP responses with a status code that is both different from 101 (Switching Protocols) and outside the 2xx (Successful) range.

requirements.title: Recommend sending Capsule-Protocol with Capsule Protocol
requirements.statement: When using the Capsule Protocol, HTTP endpoints SHOULD send the Capsule-Protocol header field to simplify intermediary processing.

requirements.title: HTTP Datagram Payload may be empty
requirements.statement: The HTTP Datagram Payload field MAY be empty.

requirements.title: Drop oversized HTTP Datagrams instead of converting them
requirements.statement: If the HTTP Datagram is too large to fit in a DATAGRAM frame, the intermediary SHOULD drop the HTTP Datagram instead of converting it to a DATAGRAM Capsule.

requirements.title: Intermediary may re-encode DATAGRAM Capsules
requirements.statement: An intermediary MAY send a DATAGRAM Capsule to forward an HTTP Datagram that was received in a QUIC DATAGRAM frame and vice versa.

requirements.title: Intermediaries require Capsule Protocol identification before re-encoding
requirements.statement: Intermediaries MUST not perform this re-encoding unless they have identified the use of the Capsule Protocol on the corresponding request stream.

requirements.title: Require a Capsule Type field in each registration
requirements.statement: All registrations in this registry MUST include a "Capsule Type" field that contains a short name or label for the Capsule Type.

requirements.title: IANA assignment is prohibited
requirements.statement: These values MUST NOT be assigned by IANA.

requirements.title: Listing as assigned values is prohibited
requirements.statement: These values MUST NOT appear in the listing of assigned values.

requirements.title: Require absolute URI Template form
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST be in absolute form.

requirements.title: Require non-empty URI Template components
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST include non-empty scheme, authority, and path components.

requirements.title: Limit URI Template level
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST be a level 3 template or lower.

requirements.title: Reconstruct URI and open UDP tunnel
requirements.statement: The UDP proxy MUST extract target_host and target_port from the URI reconstructed from the request headers, decode their percent-encoding, and open a UDP socket to the requested target.

requirements.title: Respond before target packet
requirements.statement: The UDP proxy MUST respond to the request without waiting for a packet from the target.

requirements.title: Resolve DNS names before replying
requirements.statement: If target_host is a DNS name, the UDP proxy MUST perform DNS resolution before replying to the HTTP request.

requirements.title: Validate source address on non-connected sockets
requirements.statement: If the UDP proxy uses a non-connected socket, it MUST validate the IP source address on received packets to ensure they match the client's request.

requirements.title: Validate source port on non-connected sockets
requirements.statement: If the UDP proxy uses a non-connected socket, it MUST validate the UDP source port on received packets to ensure they match the client's request.

requirements.title: Discard unmatched packets
requirements.statement: Packets that do not match MUST be discarded by the UDP proxy.

requirements.title: Reject request on errors
requirements.statement: If errors occur during this process, the UDP proxy MUST reject the request.

requirements.title: Include Connection header field value Upgrade in response
requirements.statement: The response SHALL include a Connection header field with value "Upgrade".

requirements.title: Start HTTP Datagrams with Context ID
requirements.statement: All HTTP Datagrams associated with UDP Proxying request streams MUST start with a Context ID field.

requirements.title: Use 62-bit Context IDs
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST be 62-bit integers in the range 0 to 2^62-1.

requirements.title: Encode Context IDs as varints
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST be encoded as variable-length integers; see Section 16 of [QUIC].

requirements.title: Dynamically allocate non-zero Context IDs
requirements.statement: Non-zero Context ID values MUST be dynamically allocated.

requirements.title: Reserve Context ID 0 for UDP payloads
requirements.statement: The Context ID value of 0 MUST be reserved for UDP payloads.

requirements.title: Allocate even-numbered Context IDs on the client
requirements.statement: Non-zero even-numbered Context IDs MUST be client-allocated.

requirements.title: Allocate odd-numbered Context IDs on the proxy
requirements.statement: Odd-numbered Context IDs MUST be proxy-allocated.

requirements.title: Do not re-allocate Context IDs in a namespace
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST NOT be re-allocated within a given HTTP namespace.

requirements.title: Scope Context IDs per HTTP request
requirements.statement: The Context ID namespace MUST be tied to a given HTTP request.

requirements.title: Permit future Context ID registration mechanisms
requirements.statement: Future extensions MAY use HTTP header fields or capsules to register Context IDs.

requirements.title: Unknown Context ID handling
requirements.statement: If an HTTP/3 Datagram carrying an unknown Context ID is received, the receiver SHALL either drop it silently or buffer it temporarily for about a round trip while awaiting registration of the corresponding Context ID.

requirements.title: UDP packets use Context ID zero
