requirements.statement: UDP packets MUST be encoded using HTTP Datagrams with Context ID zero.

requirements.title: Context ID zero carries unmodified UDP payload
requirements.statement: When Context ID is zero, the UDP Proxying Payload field MUST contain the unmodified payload of a UDP packet.

requirements.title: UDP Proxying Payload may be empty
requirements.statement: The UDP Proxying Payload field MAY be empty.

requirements.title: Transmit UDP payloads in QUIC DATAGRAM frames
requirements.statement: When using HTTP/3 with the QUIC Datagram extension, UDP payloads MUST be transmitted in QUIC DATAGRAM frames.

requirements.title: Limit QUIC DATAGRAM payload size
requirements.statement: QUIC DATAGRAM frames MUST carry UDP payloads only up to a length determined by the QUIC connection configuration and the Path MTU (PMTU).

requirements.title: Do not capsule oversized UDP payloads
requirements.statement: If a UDP proxy is using QUIC DATAGRAM frames and it receives a UDP payload from the target that will not fit inside a QUIC DATAGRAM frame, the UDP proxy SHOULD NOT send the UDP payload in a DATAGRAM capsule.

requirements.title: Ignore ECN bits received from target
requirements.statement: A UDP proxy MUST ignore ECN bits in the IP header of UDP packets received from the target.

requirements.title: Set ECN bits to Not-ECT on outbound UDP packets
requirements.statement: A UDP proxy MUST set the ECN bits to Not-ECT on UDP packets it sends to the target.

requirements.title: Avoid increasing UDP burstiness
requirements.statement: UDP proxies SHOULD avoid increasing burstiness of UDP traffic.

requirements.title: Do not queue packets to increase batching
requirements.statement: UDP proxies SHOULD NOT queue packets to increase batching.

requirements.title: Do not disable congestion control without certainty
requirements.statement: The underlying HTTP connection MUST NOT disable congestion control unless it has an out-of-band way of knowing with absolute certainty that the inner traffic is congestion-controlled.

requirements.title: Do not signal ECN support when congestion control is disabled
requirements.statement: If a client or UDP proxy with a connection containing a UDP Proxying request stream disables congestion control, it MUST NOT signal Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) support on that connection.

requirements.title: Mark IP headers Not-ECT when congestion control is disabled
requirements.statement: If a client or UDP proxy with a connection containing a UDP Proxying request stream disables congestion control, it MUST mark all IP headers with the Not-ECT codepoint.

requirements.title: Allow ECN feedback reporting when permitted
requirements.statement: It MAY continue to report ECN feedback via QUIC ACK_ECN frames or the TCP ECE bit, as the peer may not have disabled congestion control.

requirements.title: Prefer HTTP/3 for UDP proxying
requirements.statement: UDP proxying SHOULD be performed over HTTP/3 to allow leveraging the QUIC DATAGRAM frame.

requirements.title: Select a compatible negotiated version
requirements.statement: When an endpoint can parse the client's first flight using the client's Chosen Version and the client's Version Information lists at least one mutually supported compatible version, the server MUST select one such version as the Negotiated Version, continue the handshake using that version, and preserve the client's Original Version long enough to authenticate the Version Information carried on that original first flight.

requirements.title: Adopt and validate the negotiated version
requirements.statement: A client that learns the Negotiated Version from the server's handshake packets MUST validate that the server's Chosen Version matches the Negotiated Version and close the connection with a version negotiation error if they do not match. When the negotiated version is compatible with the client's Original Version, the client continues the connection using that negotiated version for subsequent packets.

requirements.title: Parse peer Version Information
requirements.statement: Both endpoints MUST parse their peer's Version Information during the handshake.

requirements.title: Close on Version Information parsing failure
requirements.statement: If parsing Version Information fails, such as when it is too short or its length is not divisible by four, the endpoint MUST close the connection.

requirements.title: Reject zero Version Information values
requirements.statement: If an endpoint receives a Chosen Version equal to zero, or any Available Version equal to zero, it MUST treat it as a parsing failure.

requirements.title: Reject missing client Chosen Version preference
requirements.statement: If a server receives Version Information where the Chosen Version is not included in Available Versions, it MUST treat it as a parsing failure.

requirements.title: Define dohpath as a single-valued UTF-8 relative URI template
requirements.statement: The single-valued `dohpath` SvcParamKey MUST have a value that is a relative URI Template encoded in UTF-8.

requirements.title: Require dohpath when ALPN indicates HTTP
requirements.statement: If the `alpn` SvcParam indicates HTTP support, `dohpath` MUST be present.

requirements.title: Require a dns variable in the URI Template
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST contain a `dns` variable.

requirements.title: Require valid :path expansion
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST expand to a valid and functional `:path` value.

requirements.title: Send DoH requests to the HTTPS origin from the SVCB record
requirements.statement: When using this SVCB record, the client MUST send DoH requests to the HTTPS origin identified by the `https` scheme, the authentication name, and the port from the `port` SvcParam if present.

requirements.title: Direct HTTP requests to the dohpath expansion resource
requirements.statement: HTTP requests MUST be directed to the resource produced by expanding the `dohpath` URI Template.

requirements.title: Avoid querying HTTPS RRs when using dohpath
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD NOT query HTTPS RRs when using `dohpath`.

requirements.title: Use the SVCB SvcParams and address records for HTTPS connections
requirements.statement: The SvcParams and address records associated with this SVCB record SHOULD be used for the HTTPS connection.

requirements.title: Publish an equivalent HTTPS RR
requirements.statement: Service operators SHOULD publish an equivalent HTTPS RR.

requirements.title: Do not identify or authenticate during DNS queries
requirements.statement: A client of this SVCB mapping MUST NOT identify or authenticate itself when performing DNS queries, except to servers that it specifically knows are not vulnerable to such attacks.

requirements.title: Avoid further queries after an invalid response
requirements.statement: If an endpoint sends an invalid response to a DNS query, the client SHOULD NOT send more queries to that endpoint.

requirements.title: Optionally log invalid DNS query responses
requirements.statement: If an endpoint sends an invalid response to a DNS query, the client MAY log this error.

requirements.title: Authenticate to the server's authentication name
requirements.statement: During secure transport establishment, clients MUST authenticate the server to its authentication name.

requirements.title: Prefer SVCB-reliant behavior after successful resolution
requirements.statement: If use of this specification is optional, clients SHOULD switch to SVCB-reliant behavior when SVCB resolution succeeds.

requirements.title: Allow dependent specifications to adjust fallback behavior
requirements.statement: Specifications making use of this mapping MAY adjust this fallback behavior to suit their requirements.

requirements.title: Encrypted DNS options include an ADN
requirements.statement: Encrypted DNS options MUST always include an ADN.

requirements.title: Router or forwarder single LAN-facing address
requirements.statement: A router embedding a recursive server or a forwarder MUST include one IP address pointing to one of its LAN-facing interfaces.

requirements.title: Follow RFC8106 conflict rules for RA and DHCP discovery
requirements.statement: If encrypted DNS resolvers are discovered by a host using both RA and DHCP, the rules discussed in Section 5.3.1 of [RFC8106] MUST be followed.

requirements.title: Use default trust anchors unless explicit trust anchors are configured
requirements.statement: The DNS client MUST use the default system or application PKI trust anchors unless configured otherwise to use explicit trust anchors.

requirements.title: Request OPTION_V6_DNR
requirements.statement: The DHCPv6 client MUST include OPTION_V6_DNR in an Option Request Option (ORO).

requirements.title: Accept multiple OPTION_V6_DNR instances
requirements.statement: The DHCPv6 client MUST be prepared to receive multiple instances of the OPTION_V6_DNR option.

requirements.title: Treat each resolver separately
requirements.statement: Each OPTION_V6_DNR option MUST be treated as a separate encrypted DNS resolver.

requirements.title: Process instances by service priority
requirements.statement: The DHCPv6 client MUST process OPTION_V6_DNR instances in service-priority order, where a smaller value indicates higher preference.

requirements.title: Silently discard invalid OPTION_V6_DNR values
requirements.statement: The DHCPv6 client MUST silently discard any OPTION_V6_DNR that fails Section 3.1.8 validation.

requirements.title: Silently discard multicast and loopback addresses
requirements.statement: The DHCPv6 client MUST silently discard multicast and host loopback addresses in OPTION_V6_DNR.

requirements.title: Request OPTION_V4_DNR to Discover Encrypted DNS Resolver
requirements.statement: The DHCPv4 client MUST request an encrypted DNS resolver by including OPTION_V4_DNR in the Parameter Request List.

requirements.title: Receive Multiple DNR Instance Data Entries
requirements.statement: The DHCPv4 client MUST be prepared to receive multiple "DNR Instance Data" entries in OPTION_V4_DNR.

requirements.title: Process Instances by Service Priority
requirements.statement: These instances MUST be processed by service priority, with smaller values indicating higher preference.

requirements.title: Discard Invalid OPTION_V4_DNR Entries
requirements.statement: The DHCPv4 client MUST silently discard any OPTION_V4_DNR that fails the validation steps in Section 3.1.8.

requirements.title: Receive multiple Encrypted DNS options
requirements.statement: The host MUST be prepared to receive multiple Encrypted DNS options in RAs.

requirements.title: Process instances by service priority
requirements.statement: These instances MUST be processed in service-priority order, where a smaller service priority value indicates a higher preference.

requirements.title: Allow discarding requests with too many repeated attributes
requirements.statement: The responder MAY discard the full request if the count of repeated attributes exceeds an implementation-specific threshold.

requirements.title: Ignore duplicate identical attributes after the first
requirements.statement: If the request includes multiple bitwise identical attributes, the responder SHOULD process only the first occurrence and ignore the rest.

requirements.title: Return ENCDNS_IP* attributes when supported and allowed
requirements.statement: For each ENCDNS_IP* attribute from the CFG_REQUEST, if the responder supports the corresponding address family and there are no policy restrictions, the responder MUST send back one or more ENCDNS_IP* attributes in the CFG_REPLY with an appropriate list of IP addresses, service parameters, and an ADN.

requirements.title: Prefer the alpn service parameter
requirements.statement: The service parameters SHOULD include at least the "alpn" service parameter.

requirements.title: Support SHA2-256
requirements.statement: Implementations MUST support SHA2-256.

requirements.title: Disallow ENCDNS_IP* use after NULL authentication unless preconfigured
requirements.statement: If the IKEv2 responder has used the NULL Authentication method to authenticate itself, the initiator MUST NOT use returned ENCDNS_IP* resolvers configuration unless the initiator is preconfigured, e.g., in the operating system or the application.

requirements.title: Avoid DATAGRAM capsules for oversized IP packets
requirements.statement: If an IP packet will not fit inside a QUIC DATAGRAM frame, the IP proxy SHOULD NOT send the IP packet in a DATAGRAM capsule.

requirements.title: Limit QUIC DATAGRAM frame payload size
requirements.statement: QUIC DATAGRAM frames MUST carry only packets up to the length determined by the QUIC connection configuration and the Path MTU (PMTU).

requirements.title: Transmit IP packets in QUIC DATAGRAM frames
requirements.statement: When using HTTP/3 with the QUIC Datagram extension, IP packets MUST be transmitted in QUIC DATAGRAM frames.

requirements.title: Drop oversized IP packets
requirements.statement: When an IP packet will not fit inside a QUIC DATAGRAM frame, the endpoint SHOULD drop the IP packet.

requirements.title: Optionally differentiate traffic by DSCP markings
requirements.statement: If an IP proxying endpoint is configured as part of a Differentiated Services domain, it MAY implement traffic differentiation based on these markings.

requirements.title: Optionally translate DSCP values for QUIC datagrams
requirements.statement: If tunneled packets use QUIC datagrams and are not subject to congestion control by the outer connection, the IP proxying endpoints MAY translate the DSCP field value from the tunneled traffic to the outer IP header.

requirements.title: Do not coalesce inner packets with different DSCP markings
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints MUST NOT coalesce multiple inner packets into the same outer packet unless they have the same DSCP marking or an equivalent traffic class.

requirements.title: Avoid burstiness of IP traffic
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints SHOULD avoid increasing burstiness of IP traffic.

requirements.title: Avoid extra packet batching
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints SHOULD NOT queue packets to increase batching beyond the minimal amount required to take advantage of hardware offloads.

requirements.title: Disable congestion control for DATAGRAM-only packets
requirements.statement: The outer HTTP connection MAY disable congestion control for packets that contain only QUIC DATAGRAM frames encapsulating IP packets.

requirements.title: Restrict IP proxying to authenticated users
requirements.statement: HTTP servers that support IP proxying SHOULD restrict its use to authenticated users.

requirements.title: Avoid persistent per-client address assignment
requirements.statement: Proxies SHOULD avoid persistent per-client address (prefix) assignment when possible.

requirements.title: Follow BCP38 to prevent source address spoofing
requirements.statement: In such scenarios, endpoints MUST follow the recommendations from [BCP38] to prevent source address spoofing.

requirements.title: Require absolute-form URI Template
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST be in absolute form.

requirements.title: Limit URI Template level to 3 or lower
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST be a level 3 template or lower.

requirements.title: Require non-empty URI Template components
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST include non-empty scheme, authority, and path components.

requirements.title: Resolve DNS names before replying
requirements.statement: If the "target" variable is a DNS name, the IP proxy MUST perform DNS resolution before replying to the HTTP request.

requirements.title: Extract tunnel variables from the reconstructed URI
requirements.statement: An IP proxy MUST extract the optional `target` and `ipproto` variables from the reconstructed URI, decode their percent-encoding, and establish an IP tunnel.

requirements.title: Report proxy errors with Proxy-Status details
requirements.statement: If errors occur during this process, the IP proxy SHOULD send details using an appropriate Proxy-Status header field.

requirements.title: Validate decoded tunnel variables
requirements.statement: IP proxies MUST validate the decoded `target` and `ipproto` variables against Section 4.6.

requirements.title: Reject requests when processing errors occur
requirements.statement: If errors occur during this process, the IP proxy MUST reject the request.

requirements.title: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 IP proxying uses Extended CONNECT
requirements.statement: When using HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, IP proxying requests MUST use HTTP Extended CONNECT.

requirements.title: Servers send an HTTP Setting
requirements.statement: Servers MUST send an HTTP Setting, as specified in [EXT-CONNECT2] and [EXT-CONNECT3].

requirements.title: Response meets Capsule Protocol HTTP requirements
requirements.statement: The response MUST meet the requirements of HTTP responses that start the Capsule Protocol.

requirements.title: Limit IP Version values to 4 or 6
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST be either 4 or 6.

requirements.title: Encode ADDRESS_REQUEST IP Version as an unsigned 8-bit integer
requirements.statement: The ADDRESS_REQUEST IP Version field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: Zero IP Protocol value semantics
requirements.statement: If the IP Protocol field value is 0, all protocols MUST be allowed.

requirements.title: Nonzero IP Protocol values
requirements.statement: If the IP Protocol field value is not 0, it MUST represent an allowable next header value carried in IP headers that are sent directly in HTTP Datagrams (the outermost IP headers).

requirements.title: Always allow ICMP traffic
requirements.statement: ICMP traffic MUST always be allowed, regardless of the IP Protocol field value.

requirements.title: Withdrawn range semantics
requirements.statement: If a given address range was present in a prior capsule but the most recently received ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule does not contain it, the receiver MUST consider that range withdrawn.

requirements.title: Encode ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT IP Protocol as an unsigned 8-bit integer
requirements.statement: The ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT IP Protocol field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT supersession
requirements.statement: If multiple ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsules are sent in one direction, each ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule MUST supersede prior ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsules.

requirements.title: Allow any number of new capsules
requirements.statement: Both endpoints MAY send any number of these new capsules.

requirements.title: Reject scoping requests for extension-header protocol numbers
requirements.statement: IP proxies MAY reject requests to scope to protocol numbers that are used for extension headers.

requirements.title: Walk extension headers to the outermost non-extension protocol number
requirements.statement: Upon receiving packets, implementations that support scoping or routing by Internet Protocol Number MUST walk the chain of extensions to find the outermost non-extension Internet Protocol Number to match against the scoping rule.

requirements.title: Expand URI templates for IP proxying requests
requirements.statement: When sending its IP proxying request, the client SHALL perform URI Template expansion to determine the path and query of its request.

requirements.title: Protect IP proxying over HTTP with encryption
requirements.statement: IP proxying over HTTP MUST be operated over TLS or QUIC encryption, or another equivalent encryption protocol, to provide confidentiality, integrity, and authentication.

requirements.title: Limit Context ID size to 62 bits
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST be 62-bit integers (0 to 2^62-1).

requirements.title: Encode Context IDs as variable-length integers
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST be encoded as variable-length integers.

requirements.title: Allocate non-zero Context IDs dynamically
requirements.statement: Non-zero Context ID values MUST be dynamically allocated.

requirements.title: Reserve Context ID 0 for IP payloads
requirements.statement: The Context ID value of 0 MUST be reserved for IP payloads.

requirements.title: Disallow Context ID reallocation within a request
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST NOT be re-allocated within a given HTTP request.

requirements.title: Permit future extensions to register Context IDs
requirements.statement: Future extensions MAY use HTTP header fields or capsules to register Context IDs.

requirements.title: Allow optimistic proxied IP packet sending
requirements.statement: When using HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, a client MAY optimistically start sending proxied IP packets before receiving the response to its IP proxying request.

requirements.title: Use ICMP to signal forwarding errors
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints SHOULD signal forwarding errors to their peer by generating ICMP packets and sending them using HTTP Datagrams.

requirements.title: Do not forward link-local traffic beyond the received interface
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints MUST not forward any link-local traffic beyond the IP proxying interface on which it was received.

requirements.title: Ensure IPv6 tunnel MTU of at least 1280 bytes
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints that operate as routers and support IPv6 MUST ensure the IP tunnel link MTU is at least 1280 bytes.

requirements.title: Use ICMPv6 echo requests to verify link MTU
requirements.statement: Unless endpoints have an out-of-band guarantee that the previous techniques are sufficient, IP proxying endpoints MUST use ICMPv6 echo requests with 1232 bytes of data to determine the link MTU and tear down the tunnel if no response is received.

requirements.title: Define new capsule types for configuration exchange
requirements.statement: Extensions SHOULD define new capsule types for configuration exchange when needed.
